108 Bocce is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  McCoy-Oni. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with McCoy-Oni.
Its union is  Road to Heaven [DLC], which also requires  108 Responsive Prayers [DLC].
## Effects
108 Bocce places a black aura around the player, dealing damage to every enemy who is inside of it. It also has 8 beads orbiting around the character.
 Cooldown acts similar to Hitbox Delay for 108 Bocce. Damage will be dealt instantly to an enemy if they have never been in the circle before, after which they cannot be hit by it again until the 108 Bocce's Cooldown is over, even if they temporarily leave its area.
The difference between  Luck and  Curse will boost the damage of 108 Bocce, each 1% of difference gives 1% damage multiplier to the base damage, with the maximum multiplier being 11x while having a difference of 1000%.
## Levels
108 Bocce has 8 Levels. At max level, 108 Bocce has +28 Base Damage and -0.3 seconds of  Cooldown.

## Tips
- It is important to pick only one stat to focus on. Curse is easier to get up higher with  Skull O'Maniac,  Gold Ring,  Metaglio Right, and  Torrona's Box. Luck can be renewable unlike Curse but one must encounter a lot of  Little Clovers for it to be worth it.
- Characters with infinitely scaling Luck or Curse can be extremely powerful,  Smith,  Avatar,  Cosmo,  Gyorunton,  Gyoruntin,  Keitha,  Je-Ne-Viv,  Scientist,  Sniper, and  Blackmore are great choices. Beware that scaling Curse may get out of hand very easily, and it is not recommended compared to scaling Luck.
- With Wicked Season (XIII), despite leveling up increasing  Luck and  Curse at the same time, half of the time one of them will be doubled, increasing the potential of 108 Bocce. However, if Wicked Season is used in conjunction with other items or abilities that increase Luck or Curse, the power of 108 Bocce will fluctuate, becoming weaker when Wicked Season increases the stat the player does not focus on. This is usually not a major issue if the player focuses on Curse, as the weapon will be at the apex of its power when Curse is doubled, but may present an issue in a Luck-focused build, as 108 Bocce will be at its absolute weakest when the player's Curse is doubled and powerful weapons are necessary to handle the increased hordes.
## Trivia
- 108 Bocce is very similar to  Garlic, with only some differences in stats, without any utility effects, and is affected by  Luck and  Curse.
- The weapon's name refers to bocce, an Italian sport that can trace its history all the way back to the Roman Empire, played with 8 colored balls. The icon resembles an ojuzu, a string of 108 prayer beads commonly used by Japanese Buddhists.
- This weapon is most likely a reference to Donovan Baine from the Darkstalkers series.

108 Responsive Prayers is a weapon in Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Jaman Jato ★.
Its union is  Road to Heaven, which also requires  108 Bocce [DLC].
## Effects
108 Responsive Prayers creates ofuda amulets in a spiral vertically around the user, with the ofuda amulets rotating in the same direction as the user. When the weapon fires, after a short delay, it will create explosions centered on these amulets, displaying the characters "不", "動", "明", and "王", (a Buddhist Bodhisattva), dealing damage to enemies hit as the explosions continue down the screen. 
The damage of the above explosions is increased by +1% for every 1% difference in  Luck and  Curse, maxing out at a damage increase of 11x at a difference of 1000%.
The number of explosions done by 108 Responsive Prayers in a single activation is increased by both  Duration and  Amount.
108 Responsive Prayers has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same explosion. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
108 Responsive Prayers has 8 levels. At max level, 108 Responsive Prayers has +8 Base Damage, +1 second of Duration, +40% Area, and +1 Amount.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | "Actually it's just 16. Damage affected by the difference between Curse and Luck."
| Level 2 | Base Damage up by 4.
| Level 3 | Effect lasts 0.5 seconds longer.
| Level 4 | Base Area up by 20%.
| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 4.
| Level 6 | Effect lasts 0.5 seconds longer.
| Level 7 | Base Area up by 20%.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectile.

- The name of this weapon may be a reference to the first entry in the Touhou Project bullet hell game series, Highly Responsive To Prayers. The weapon closely resembles ofuda amulets used by Shinto and Buddhist priests, including the game's protagonist, shrine maiden Reimu Hakurei.

Acerbatus is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Optical Shot, requiring Max level  Karoma's Mana. Evolving it keeps Optical Shot as hidden weapon.
## Effects
Acerbatus fires large, piercing yellow light balls at faced direction with a short delay before traveling away. The faster the character is moving in the faced direction, the farther the projectile will fire. The more enemies defeated, the more damage it deals. It also makes Optical Shot keep firing at the faced direction too.

The Acquazzone is a hidden weapon in Vampire Survivors. It is currently only used in the Ode to Castlevania DLC by the  Ferryman and  Atlantis Shrine Wizard.  Para Kooleo also possesses a hidden copy of Acquazzone that temporarily activates whenever he evolves a weapon.
Acquazzone behaves similarly to  The Drowner's attack by creating a zone of water filled with swirling bubbles on the bottom half of the screen. It flashes white when it strikes, damaging all enemies within the bottom half of the screen, and will pulse several times with damage based on  Amount. The Acquazzone has a base damage of 10 and base  Cooldown of 5 seconds.
This attack does not damage light sources.
## Trivia
- "Acquazzone" is Italian for "Heavy downpour".
- The Acquazzone itself closely resembles the staff used by the  The Drowner.

The Alchemy Whip is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Leon Belmont, and is unlocked by surviving 6 minutes with him.
Its Evolution is the  Vampire Killer, which requires the  Tirajisú.
After obtaining the  Black Disk, Evolving the Alchemy Whip unlocks  Sara Trantoul as a playable character.
As a magic whip, it can be picked from  Morning Star.
## Effects
The Alchemy Whip swings horizontally within a short range, damaging enemies within. With  Amount increased, Alchemy Whip will perform a triple strike: Attacks horizontally first, than attacks 45 degree up, and ends with 45 degree down attack. It ignores  Speed and  Duration.
For the first 10 Bosses killed, each Boss killed grants the Alchemy Whip a flat +2 increase to Base Damage. Afterwards, each boss will only grant +1 Base Damage.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Alchemy Whip to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels

The Alucard Shield is a weapon and a gift from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the gift of the  Alucard Swords, requiring at least six evolved weapons, including the Alucard Swords, and at least six maxed out passives.
Warning: Weapons that are absorbed do not count for Unlocks that require evolving a specific weapon.
## Effects
The Alucard Shield's main benefit is its absorption of all evolved weapons, turning them hidden, while preventing them from Limit Breaking. It will also free up any slots these evolved weapons occupied.
The weapon itself summons a shield in front of the character, which deals massive damage to enemies it touches.
While Alucard Swords is absorbed, the color of each of its slashes are randomized.
## Limit Break
With Limit Break, Alucard Shield can't be further leveled up.

## Tips
- The 'minimum' number of evolved weapons needed to get the Alucard Shield is six. If more than six evolved weapons were obtained through  Candybox and evolving that weapon, or through  Super Candybox II Turbo, then those extra evolved weapons will also be absorbed.
- Weapons that do not evolve will not get absorbed. This includes the  Victory Sword, which only 'gifts' the  Sole Solution, rather than evolving into it.
- Emerald Diorama weapons that are absorbed before glimmering are still able to glimmer even while hidden.

Alucard Spear is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Eric Lecarde. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 30,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Thunderbolt Spear with  Wings. Evolving it and  Iron Ball unlocks  Shanoa as a playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
The Alucard Spear is a melee-type weapon that sends out a spear (affected by  Area and  Amount) to damage enemies. This weapon can perform a spin attack that happens when the player changes their movement to the opposite direction of the spear, causing it to swing around and hit all enemies in the way. This also slightly extends the projectile's  Duration, enough to allow it to be swung around indefinitely.
## Levels
Alucard Spear has 8 levels. At Max level, it has +2  Amount (3 total), +30 Base Damage (40 total), +60%  Area, and -0.5 seconds Cooldown (down to 2.5 seconds).

## Tips
- With good timing, the spears can be kept around nearly indefinitely, allowing them to build up for massive damage output.
- To achieve the best results, try making turns right as the first spear is about to reach the end of its arc, or approximately every 0.5 seconds.
- The actual hitbox of the Alucard Spear is dependent on the direction you aim your movement with your keyboard or joystick. As long as you're flipping the spear back and forth while aiming at an enemy, they'll take hefty damage
- A way to assist with finding your aim is using another weapon, like  Raging Fire.
## Trivia
- The way this weapon attacks, and how it functions, are very similar to how Eric attacks in Castlevania: Bloodlines. Unlike here, in Bloodlines you are able to start it from a vertical strike, not just horizontal.

Alucard Swords is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Alucart Sworb, requiring Max level.
It can be evolved into  Alucard Shield with Max any 6 evolutions, any 6 passives. Be careful as the weapons will be absorbed, though still active, making room for 5 new weapons.
## Effects
Alucard Swords summons phantoms of  Alucard that dash to an enemy and slash everything in Area around them, selecting a new target after each slash. Amount increases the number of phantoms that spawn and the amount of times they can switch targets before despawning. The maximum number of phantoms from a single activation is 6.
The color of the phantom's outline, and the slashes it creates, change after each weapon evolution (excluding itself). Its color changes in order are: red (base), grey (one evolution), green (two evolutions), turquoise (three evolutions), yellow (four evolutions), and blue (five evolutions).
## Levels
Alucard Swords has 8 levels. At Max level, it gets +20 Base Damage (70 total), +3 Amount (7 total) and +50% Area.

Alucart Sworb is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Alucard. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 10,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Alucard Swords once fully leveled. Evolving it unlocks  Christopher Belmont as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Alucart Sworb stabs multiple times in the horizontally-faced direction, each subsequent stab going further away from the character. It ignores  Speed and  Duration.

Ammo Appalate is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the starting weapon of  Zi'Appunta Belpaese. It is unlocked by defeating a total of 251,096 shooting enemies.
Its evolution is  Gunastrophe, which requires  Bracer at max level. Evolving it unlocks  Zi'Appunta Belpaese as playable character.
## Effects
Ammo Appalate shoots small white bullets at the closest enemy in the faced direction in a burst, and saves up ammo if there are no enemies to be unloaded later.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Horse Cartridge. It levels up as Ammo Appalate does. It shoots bullets at the closest enemy away from where the character is facing.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Ammo Appalate to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Ammo Appalate's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
## Levels
Ammo Appalate has 8 levels. At max level, Ammo Appalate has +6 Base Damage, +20% Area, +5 Amount, and +6 Pierce.

## Trivia
- Its name means "Ammo in huge quantities", reflecting the fact that ammo is stockpiled with this weapon and released at once. The name originates from the Italian vernacular "a palate", which can be literally translated as "in shovelfuls" or more liberally as "in spades".
- In line with Zi'Appunta's Tomb Raider references, the number of kills required to unlock the Ammo Appalate is close to the release date of the first Tomb Raider game: 24 October 1996.

Anima of Mortaccio is a morph from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.3.0. It is the evolution of  Bone, and requires  Chaos Malachite relic and reaching level 80 while playing as  Mortaccio.
Alternatively, it can be obtained via Cosmic Finger rewards from  Gold Fingers or the Edition of  Mortaccio's  Survarot.
## Effects
Anima of Mortaccio throws spinning bones in a random direction. The bone travels in a straight line, bouncing off of enemies, walls, and the edges of the screen, accelerating each bounce until the end of its duration. It also adds a pair of bone arms on the character. After five normal bone shots, they start rotating around the character, then they fling off as another pair of bouncing projectiles until they return to the character. The arms leave behind afterimages. It also causes Mortaccio to visually transform into a  Goshadokuro. If another character other than Mortaccio gets the weapon, a translucent, transformed Mortaccio appears behind the character.
Anima of Mortaccio gains extra Pool Limit.
 Duration increases how long the arms spin around the character and bounce around the screen. They spin for at least 8 seconds, and increase by 1 second for every 0.5 seconds beyond 4 seconds for the normal bones duration. They bounce around for at least 4 seconds and as long as other normal bones if the duration is longer.
 Amount multiplies the damage of the arms by 0.5 x total Amount.
Each bounce multiples the velocity of the bones by 1.1.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows the bones to explode when they expire. Damage is based on  Curse.

## Tips
- Anima of Mortaccio benefits from every passive item that can affect weapon stats. The collection tab says that it works best with  Duration and  Speed.
- Anima of Mortaccio has similar behavior to  Runetracer, but lacks its piercing. This makes it especially effective when the player is surrounded by enemies. The bones will have more time to bounce around and deal damage before expiring.
- With the arms' damage scale with  Amount, taking  Beginning (X) can make them even more effective.
## Trivia
- Anima of Mortaccio morphing Mortaccio into a giant skeleton is a reference to the Giant Skeleton enemy, specifically Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow's that has no legs and crawls along the ground.
- It also specifically references Creaking Skull's guardian soul where a giant arm appears behind Soma and crushes enemies. When it is not used by Mortaccio, the skeleton becomes transparent with a blue shade, making it look more similar to Creaking Skull.
- Anima of Mortaccio resembles part of the Italian saying "L'anima de li mortacci tuoi" which roughly translates to "The soul of your bad dead relatives", it is a way to insult someone's ancestors. However, depending on the context in which it is said, it may not be as insulting as it sounds when translated, as it is sometimes said to call out on friends, as an impersonal outburst or even referred to oneself to express regret.

Anura is a weapon introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Drolta Tzuentes [DLC]. It can be purchased from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Dark Frogamorphosis [DLC], which also requires  Soul Eater.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook [DLC].
## Effects
Being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Anura has a charge time before activation, which is indicated by the brightness of its created magic circle.
Anura creates a magic circle above the character. After being fully charged, the magic circle stops in place and begins summoning green frogs that damage enemies as they jump.  Amount is multiplied by  Duration divided by Hitbox Delay, rounding up.
Anura has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same frog. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Speculo Anura. It levels up as Anura does and creates a magic circle below the character which purple frogs, but does not benefit from Limit Breaking.

Arch Angle is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Grand Cross [DLC] at max level and  Heaven Sword.
## Effects
Arch Angle summons mini cross projectiles that aim at the nearest enemy, dealing damage to any enemy that they come into contact with, and a transparent beam of light in the center of the player's screen that spans the height of the screen, being the same visual seen from Grand Cross. Whenever a cross projectile overlaps the beam, the beam will pulse, dealing 1.3x the damage of Arch Angle. This beam will not deal contact damage - it must pulse to deal damage.
- Much like Grand Cross,  Revivals have no effect on this weapon.
Compared to Grand Cross, Arch Angle has higher Interval,  Speed, and a faster  Cooldown, but lower Base Damage and  Amount.
Unlike  Heaven Sword, Arch Angle cannot crit by default, requiring  Slash (XVI).
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Grand Cross's projectiles to bounce off the edges of the screen twice. Upon bouncing, the sword completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows critical hit. Critical chance is affected by  Luck.

Argent Flow is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Megalo Miang Moonspell. It is the evolution of  Festive Winds, requiring  Torrona's Box at max level.
## Effects
Argent Flow creates a stream of wind that spans the length of the screen, dealing damage to enemies that contact it. This wind will follow the user and will always be centered on them. The number of hitboxes is increased by  Amount, though the visual effects of the weapon are unaffected.
The base  Cooldown and  Duration are equal, meaning that a stream of wind will almost always be active. Increases to either stat can allow multiple instances to overlap.
Compared to Festive Winds, Argent flow has improved Base Damage and  Duration, but worse  Speed,  Amount,  Cooldown, Repeat Interval, and Pool Limit.
- Note that, despite also having a Speed Limit Break option, Speed does not have any effect on Argent Flow.
When an enemy is hit by Argent Flow, the damage it receives from any source is increased by 2%, up to a maximum of 10000% damage (100x) at 5,000 hits. 
Argent Flow has a 5% chance to generate  Little Hearts that heal 1 point of health upon killing an enemy. This chance is affected by  Luck.
Argent Flow has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more than every 0.5 seconds by the same stream of wind. Note that, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Argent Flow is a listed weapon of Twilight Requiem, but currently has no effect.
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Healing provided by  Little Hearts is doubled, and a damaging pulse is triggered when a Little Heart is collected.

Arma Dio is a weapon selector from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.10. It is unlocked by collecting it in any stage.
## Effects
Obtaining Arma Dio opens a list of all passive items still available. Its rarity is multiplied by  Luck. Like most weapons, it will be removed from the item pool upon being picked.
Passive items which only get added to the level-up item pool after certain requirements are met, like all Mini Crewmates[DLC] requiring their corresponding weapon at a certain level and  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] requiring any weapon from the Operation Guns, are only selectable via the Arma Dio after those requirements are met.
The following passive items cannot be picked:
-  Silver Ring
-  Gold Ring
-  Metaglio Left
-  Metaglio Right
-  Academy Badge [DLC]
- All Familiars[DLC](which can be picked from  Familiar Forge [DLC])
-  Outer Saboteur [DLC]
## Combos
See Combos for a list of all item interactions.

## Tips
- There are many ways to unlock Arma Dio:
- In Laborratory, entering enough rooms to the north and hitting enough levers to spawn it.
- Find any of the three in Neo Galuga [DLC] shown on the map.
- Find any of the four in Ode to Castlevania [DLC] shown on the map.
- When playing as  Santa Ladonna, an Arma Dio spawns once she reaches level 40.
- Arma Dio can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "apritisedano".
- Arma Dio can be selected with the  Candybox, allowing the player to get over six passives at once regardless of the map. This is not recommended unless the player is limiting weapons through  Silent Old Sanctuary (XX), would not benefit from having an extra weapon, or needs Karoma's Mana to upgrade a weapon. It will be removed from the Candybox once acquired by any method.
- Since Arma Dio is an active weapon, it cannot be obtained by leveling up when the player reaches the limit of weapons equipped. Uniting weapons (if the option exists) to free up weapon slot if an extra passive item is desirable.
- Arma Dio becomes useless once all passive items on its list are collected.
-  Hail from the Future (X) can provide up to seven Arma Dios per run.
## Trivia
- "Arma Dio" roughly means "God Weapon" in Italian, but it also is a pun on "Armadio", meaning "Cabinet".

Arrow of Goth is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of the  Alamaric Sniper, and can be purchased and unlocked from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Dies Irae [DLC], which also requires  Mannajja.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Arrow of Goth summons golden bows behind the character. The bow will shoot an arrow, travelling horizontally while piercing enemies, then disappear. Increasing  Amount summons more bows.
Arrow of Goth has a special "critical" attack based on  Luck: Instead of dealing critical damage, it summons 21 golden arrows (forming a 6-layer triangle) once.
- Note that this is not an actual critical hit, and is instead a chance-based special attack. It does not deal critical damage.
## Levels
Arrow of Goth has 8 levels. At max level, Arrow of Goth has +50 Base Damage, +100%  Speed, and +6  Amount.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Critical hits maximise amount of projectiles.
| Level 2 | Fires 2 more projectiles.
| Level 3 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 50%.
| Level 4 | Base Damage up by 20.
| Level 5 | Fires 2 more projectiles.
| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 50%.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 20.
| Level 8 | Fires 2 more projectiles.

Ashella is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Calogero Bloodmoon. It is unlocked by obtaining the blood rain. It can alternatively be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "armpit".
Its evolution is  Bloodlust, which requires max level  Duplicator.
## Effects
Ashella alternates between slashing in an arc above and below the player, dealing damage to enemies hit by the head of the axe as it rotates.
 Amount acts similarly to Duration, where each additional Amount increases the length of the combo.  Cooldown decreases the delay between combos.
 Speed increases how fast the axe swings complete their arc.
The area of Ashella scales in accordance to the square root of  Area.
- Despite this, with high enough Area, issues can still arise with Ashella's ability to hit nearby enemies.
Ashella has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same axe. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. 
## Levels
Ashella has 8 levels. At max level, Ashella has +30 Base Damage, -0.25 seconds of Cooldown, +30% Speed, +2 Amount, and +2.5% Critical Chance.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Can deal critical hits.
| Level 2 | Cooldown reduced by 0.25 seconds. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 3 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 4 | Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 5 | Base Speed up by 10%. Critical chance increases by 2.5%.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 10. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 8 | Base Damage up by 10.

Ashes of Muspell is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Flames of Misspell, requiring  Torrona's Box at max level.
## Effects
Ashes of Muspell spawns a burst of black flames in the faced direction and behind the character.
Ashes of Muspell has a bigger  Area, increased  Duration, increased  Speed, lower  Cooldown, and increased Pool Limit over the Flames of Misspell.
For every 5,000 enemies killed, Ashes of Muspell's base damage is increased by 1, without cap. This increase is retroactive.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Ashes of Muspell's flames explode upon hitting an enemy, dealing half of its damage in an area.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Gains a chance to fire more than twice when activated.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels

Atmo-Torpedo is an evolved weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Diver Mines, requiring  Weapon Power-Up and  Attractorb.
## Effects
Atmo-Torpedo replaces the rolling mine projectiles with torpedoes that independently fly towards their designated enemies, choosing their targets randomly but putting high priority on those near the edges of the screen. 
Upon landing, the torpedoes create vortex zones that drag enemies in and deal periodic damage - the bigger the zone, the stronger its pull. These zones scale with both  Area and  Duration.

## Tips
- The size of vortex zones determines the strength of the pull, with bigger zones being able to drag in enemies outside of their damage radius, while smaller zones will only hold enemies that walk into them. As such,  Area and  Duration are both crucial stats to increase for this weapon's effectiveness.
- Due to the nature of Atmo-Torpedoes' aiming, it is not recommended to rely on it as your sole defensive option unless you have scaled your character's stats up beforehand.
- The vortex zones' pull is strong enough to hold practically any enemy, including hidden item guardians and even  The Reaper. With a  Laurel to endure the initial hits, one could survive for a prolonged time past the stage time limit with just those two weapons alone.

## Effects
The Aurablaster Tip adds an effect where every 7th activation of the Vanitas Whip triggers a hidden  Aura Blast Cross explosion. Axe is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Lama Ladonna and  Axe Armor [DLC], and one of the starting weapons of  missingN▯. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Death Spiral, which requires  Candelabrador.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms [DLC].
## Effects
Axe throws projectiles above the player, which arc downward. The first axe is thrown directly above the character and subsequent axes from  Amount are thrown in quick succession towards the direction the player is facing in progressively wider arcs.  Speed determines how far up axes can be thrown before they start falling. Each axe can initially hit up to three enemies before dissipating.
Axe scales with the character's  Area stat multiplied by 1.3.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Axe's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls. Whenever an axe bounces off an enemy, it gains upwards momentum like it is being thrown again, but in the opposite direction in the horizontal axis.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Axe to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have 30% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Axe now aims at nearest enemy instead of thrown upward, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Axe has 8 levels. At max level, Axe has +60 Base Damage, +2 Amount, and +4 Pierce.

## Tips
- The axes will have longer arcs when paired with  Speed bonuses, allowing them to hit enemies farther above you. Very low Speed may cause axes to simply drop.
- Axe benefits greatly from  Area bonuses as the axes are big already and even have a bonus multiplier. The bigger they are, the more likely they will hit enemies and use up all their Pierce. Luckily,  Candelabrador is what evolves Axe anyway.
- Axe can deal critical damage after  Slash (XVI) is picked. The more  Luck you have, the more likely you are to deal critical hits. Luck can be increased with  Clover,  Little Clovers, or the Luck PowerUp.
- A good strategy to focus damage with Axe is to get right below a crowd, and let axes fly up into it. Combined with the already high base damage with piercing,  Amount bonuses, and upward bounces from  Iron Blue Will (VII), it can deal hundreds of concentrated damage all at once.

Belnades' Spellbook is a weapon selector from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It becomes available at the start of a stage when unlocked and equipped by an eligible character. It allows the player to select one of the Ode to Castlevania spells (which needs to be unlocked first), which include:
-  Raging Fire
-  Ice Fang
-  Gale Force
-  Rock Riot
-  Fulgur
-  Keremet Bubbles
-  Hex
-  Refectio
-  Summon Spirit Tornado and  Anura
## Unlocking
The Belnades' Spellbook is unlocked by evolving all 8 spells that can be evolved, which refers to all the weapons above except  Summon Spirit Tornado and  Anura. This does not have to be done in a single run.

BFC2000-AD is an evolved weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Blade Crossbow, requiring  Weapon Power-Up and  Clover. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
BFCD2000-AD keeps the properties of its predecessor, while gaining a separate Glaive Beam attack that summons a pillar of light with large glaives orbiting within it, appearing from the bottom of the screen and making their way upwards while shredding enemies in their path.
The Glaive Beam activates independently of regular attacks, its chance of appearing relying on  Luck - the higher it is, the more frequently the attack happens. When activated, massive Glaives will spiral upwards, dealing damage to any enemies they come in contact with, lasting until all the glaives are gone. These Glaives are capable of dealing critical damage with a x10 multiplier.
Unlike the regular attacks, Glaive Beam ignores  Area,  Speed and  Duration. It can scale with  Might,  Cooldown (more frequent attempts to activate),  Luck (for activations and critical hits) and  Amount.

## Tips
- BFC2000-AD glaives have much lower knockback compared to  Blade Crossbow, as such evolving it should be a priority if you do not wish to compensate for the knockback with weapons that can freeze or otherwise hold enemies in place.
- Since luck increases both the chance of activation and critical hits, it is an extremely important stat to scale up if going for this evolution.
- When activating multiple times in short succession, Glaive Beams will stack their durations instead of overlapping, leading to potentially long periods of having the beam active.
- Because of this, scaling  Amount can be a good way to help the beam reach a point where it will constantly be active.
- The giant glaives are the only part of the beam capable of doing damage, so relying solely on it for protection might not be the best idea. Try to have other weapons to defend yourself in close quarters, such as  King Bible or  Time Warp.
## Trivia
- The name of BFC2000-AD seems to be a reference to BFG-9000 in the DOOM series, while C stands for Crossbow.
- Doom: The Dark Ages also introduced a weapon named Ballistic Force Crossbow (BFC).

Big Fuzzy Fist is an evolved weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is evolved from  Metal Claw with  Weapon Power-Up and  Hollow Heart. Evolving it for the first time will grant the platyer 50,000 as a reward.
## Effects
Instead of horizontal attacks, Big Fuzzy Fist summons two metal fists that lock onto and pummel the strongest enemy in their range, creating shockwaves that damage the target and every enemy around it. These shockwaves can increase in size with  Area, and the number of hits per trigger depends on  Amount. 
The strongest enemy is chosen by their  Max Health, and will be attacked relentlessly until it either dies, a stronger enemy appears, or it is left out of range. The fists can split up and attack separate targets if no sufficiently powerful foes are in range.
If the weapon triggers again while the fists are still present (possible through low  Cooldown, high Amount, and/or  Sapphire Mist (I)), instead of spawning a new pair of fists the currently existing pair will speed up, locking onto and attacking enemies faster and faster. 
The same effect will happen if the player is hurt, regardless if the damage source comes from enemies or weapons such as  Muramasa. If damaged by enemies, the fists will switch priority to protecting the player from anything nearby for a few seconds.

Blacken Firmament is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Baal'Thasar. It can alternatively be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "illibbro".
Its evolution is  Damnation, which requires  Torrona's Box at max level.
## Effects
Blacken Firmament creates a large pool of void at the top of the screen, which is purely visual. Occaisionally, Blacken Firmament will pick a random, on-screen enemy to erase, instantly defeating it and leaving a dimensional tear where it was erased. The number of enemies erased with each activation is increased with  Amount.
Dimensional tears will linger in the same spot where the enemy targeted was erased, dealing contact damage and pulling in any nearby enemies.  Duration will increase how long a dimensional tear lingers before disappearing, and  Area increases the size of tears. As tears continue to linger, they will emit bubble particles towards the void at the top of the screen. Again, this effect is purely visual.
Blacken Firmament deals  Hell damage.
Blacken Firmament has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same dimensional tear. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. 
## Arcanas

Blade Crossbow is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Sheena Etranzi [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Sheena Etranzi.
Its evolution is  BFC2000-AD [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Clover.
## Effects
Blade Crossbow fires a spinning glaive in the faced direction that has a slightly homing ability which curves toward the enemy. Once it hits an enemy, it stops moving, increases in  Area, spins until  Duration ends, then returns to the character. When returning, the glaive will strike enemies it encounters on the way.
Blade Crossbow has a 0.1 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1tenth of a second by the same glaive. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

Listed weapons also emit special damaging zones affected by Amount and Magnet. Enemies within Magnet range take damage based on Amount.
Blood Astronomia (XXI) is one of the Arcanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by reaching level 50 while playing as  Poe Ratcho.
 Brauner [DLC] starts with this Arcana.
## Overview
While Blood Astronomia (XXI) is active, the following weapons receive an additional Blood Weapon effect upon being activated. These effects are based on the individual weapons' base stats and the player stats, with calculated stats factoring both of them, the player stats cap, oscillating stats, and other bonuses.
-  Garlic and  Soul Eater
-  Pentagram and  Gorgeous Moon
-  Song of Mana and  Mannajja
-  Clock Lancet
-  Laurel
-  Sonic Dash [DLC] and  Rapidus Fio [DLC]
Blood Astronomia (XXI) also turns the player's  Magnet area into a zone that damages enemies. It has a base damage of 5, multiplied by  Amount. It has a  Cooldown of 2 seconds and no Knockback.
## Garlic and Soul Eater
When they are off cooldown, they place zones on the ground under the character that each damages enemies individually based on the calculated damage. The area of the zones is based on  Magnet's radius divided by 32 or the calculated  Area of the weapon, whichever is bigger. The amount of zone placed is based on calculated Amount. It lasts for calculated  Duration.
## Pentagram and Gorgeous Moon
When they trigger, they place multiple zones around the player which can erase enemies similar to a  Rosary. Enemies with instant kill resistance are still immune to this. The amount of zones placed is based on: base Amount*3+player Amount. The zones can be triggered calculated  Amount of times before disappearing. They expire after calculated  Cooldown plus calculated  Duration, which means they would disappear shortly after the weapons trigger again.
## Song of Mana and Mannajja
When they fire, planets spawn and orbit in an ellipse around the character and the center point stays in place. They orbit further away with higher  Magnet. Each planet deals the calculated damage. The amount of planets spawned is based on: base Amount*3+player Amount. Each planet can hit a calculated Amount of times before disappearing. They expire after calculated  Cooldown plus calculated  Duration, which means they would disappear shortly after the weapons trigger again.
## Clock Lancet
When it fires, it places a zone on the ground under the character which deals a flat 5 damage. It disappears only after calculated  Duration. The area of the zone is based on  Magnet's radius. Enemies hit by the zone are slowed down permanently if the enemy is not immune to debuffs; each hit reduces the movement speed of the affected enemy by an additional 1% multiplied by base  Amount, until it reaches a minimum of 20% of their original speed. The slow effect stacks multiplicatively with other movement speed modifications. Note that this reduces the same attribute as Mannajja,  Shadow Servant [DLC], and  Time Warp [DLC] so their slowing effect do not stack multiplicatively.
## Laurel
When it regenerates a shield, it places a zone on the ground under the character. The area of the zone is based on  Magnet's radius. Its damage is based on: base damage*player Amount. The zone can be triggered calculated Amount2 of times before disappearing. It expires after calculated  Cooldown plus calculated  Duration, which means they would disappear shortly after the weapons trigger again.
## Sonic Dash and Rapidus Fio
When they activate, they first create a linear zone of red starlight at the faced direction forward and backward, which widens based on  Magnet, then it spawn four red constellations within the zone, dealing the calculated damage. Each constellation can be triggered calculated Amount of times before disappearing. It expires after calculated  Cooldown plus calculated  Duration, which means they would disappear shortly after the weapons trigger again.
## Tips
- These weapons do not benefit from  Amount without this Arcana. With it, a lot of effects have exponential growth based on Amount.
- Most effects are based on the weapon's base Amount, and all have a value of 1 by default without any ability to change it. Gorgeous Moon is an exception where its base Amount can be increased by Limit Break. It can generate the instant kill zones up to the pool limit of the weapon easily and each zone can be triggered a lot of times.
- Evolving Clock Lancet or Laurel into  Infinite Corridor or  Crimson Shroud and uniting Soul Eater, Gorgeous Moon, or Mannajja into  Dark Frogamorphosis [DLC],  Venus Crescent [DLC], or  Dies Irae [DLC] removes their Blood weapon effect.
- In the case of Amount exceeding +10 due to  Golden Eggs, the base attack will ignore this cap, allowing it to scale infinitely with Amount. This does not apply to the zones created from other weapons in conjunction with this Arcana.
## Trivia
- The name of this Arcana is a reference to the song "Bloody Tears", which is the theme song for outdoor daytime areas in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
- Blood Astronomia (XXI) can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "ilmondo", which means "the world" in Italian.
- This makes Blood Astronomia (XXI) a representation of The World Major Arcana card, symbolizing celebration, fulfillment, accomplishments, harmony, and the completion of a journey.
- This is reflected in a more literal interpretation of its ability to grant its supporting weapons unique space or planet-themed effects that revolve around the original's, such as the planets summoned by the Song of Mana and Mannajja being based off the planets of the Solar System, as well as Pluto.

Bloodlust is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Ashella, requiring max  Duplicator.
## Effects
Bloodlust acts similarly to its predecessor,  Ashella. However, Bloodlust will instead swing completely around the player. When an axe has finished swinging, it will linger on the ground. The time an axe lingers on the ground is increased by  Duration. 
- Note that the handles of both Bloodlust and its lingering axes can not crit; only the axe heads are able to.
Compared to Ashella, Bloodlust has +20% Speed, +0.8 seconds of Duration, +0.45 seconds of Interval, and +22 Pool Limit.
Whenever Bloodlust deals a Critical Hit, its Critical Damage is mulitplied by the player's  Amount. There is no limit to this scaling. 
- "Weapon" amount from Limit Break and  Beginning (X) do not increase its Critical Damage.
- If Weapons ScreenShake is enabled, then the screen will shake whenever Bloodlust deals a critical hit.
- If Damage Numbers are enabled, then any Critical Damage will be displayed with large, crimson damage numbers, much like  Stamazza [DLC].
Bloodlust deals  Blood damage.
Bloodlust has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same axe. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

Bloody Tear is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Whip, and requires  Hollow Heart. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Fuwalafuwaloo, which also requires  Vento Sacro at max level.
It is the starting weapon of  Minnah Mannarah.
## Effects
Bloody Tear's attack creates a red slash horizontally that originates from the player's torso, damaging all enemies in the area.
Bloody Tear's slashes are larger when evolved.
Consecutive slashes from increased  Amount alternate between firing towards and away from the direction the character is facing, getting progressively higher.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 10% chance to occur. This is lowered by 10% compared to Whip with  Slash (XVI). The chance is affected by  Luck.
The player can heal 8 points of health if an enemy was damaged by a critical hit. This lifesteal effect has a one second delay before it can be triggered again. It is not affected by  Recovery.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Bloody Tear's critical hit to heal double their amount and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Slash (XVI) - Bloody Tear's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.

## Tips
- Bloody Tear works best when paired with  Sarabande of Healing (VI). Even when not uniting into  Fuwalafuwaloo, the increased healing and the additional damage pulse enhance the weapon's capabilities.
- With enough  Amount, Bloody Tear can be a very deadly weapon when you are positioned south of enemies.
- Bloody Tear can deal critical damage by default. The more  Luck the player has, the more likely they are to deal critical hits.
- Bloody Tear's lifesteal effect can only trigger once per second and only on critical hits. This means that to heal the fastest, you must maximize your  Luck and  Cooldown bonuses to decrease the downtime of it not attacking with critical hits.
- Bloody Tear has a normal amount of knockback but it has an area-of-effect that can be controlled unlike most weapons, so it can be useful when trying to escape enemies closing in on the player. This is especially useful when combined with the lifesteal effect, which can let them take some damage if necessary to get away.
- Quickly switching between facing left and right will allow multiple slashes in the same direction rather than alternating.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the iconic Whip weapons from the Castlevania series. The icon is similar to the whips from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin.
- The lifesteal effect may be a reference to Dark Metamorphosis spell from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, as it also heals 8 health when it "draws blood" (deals critical hits), which a whip can do.
- Its name references the Castlevania song "Bloody Tears".

Bone is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Mortaccio and  Fake Trevor [DLC]. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Mortaccio is unlocked. It can also be obtained from  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000, or by selecting this weapon from  Candybox.
Its evolution is  Anima of Mortaccio, which requires  Chaos Malachite and reaching level 80 while playing as Mortaccio.
## Effects
Bone throws a small spinning bone at a random direction. The bone travels in a straight line, bouncing off enemies, walls, and the edges of the screen until the end of its duration.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows the Bone's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on  Curse.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Bone now aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Bone has 8 levels. At max level, Bone has +60 Base Damage, +40% Area, +100% Speed, +2 to Amount, and +0.6 seconds of Duration.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Throws a bouncing projectile.
| Level 2 | Base Area up by 20%. Effect lasts 0.2 seconds longer.
| Level 3 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 20.

## Tips
- Bone benefits from every passive item that can affect weapon stats. The collection tab says that it works best with  Duration and  Speed.
- Bone has similar behavior to  Runetracer, but lacks its piercing. This makes it especially effective when the player is surrounded by enemies. The bones will have more time to bounce around and deal damage before expiring.
- Bone starts off weak, but becomes exceptionally powerful after leveling and with bonuses from passive items. This makes it especially good as a supporting weapon, as it will scale with the player for the duration of the game.

Boo Roo Boolle is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Mille Bolle Blu, which requires the  Spellbinder at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Boo Roo Boolle shoots colorful bubbles at the enemy closest to the player character which linger on the ground.
Boo Roo Boolle has more Base Damage,  Area, and a higher Pool Limit, but  Amount is lowered by two.
Each bubble can now hit enemies multiple times. Boo Roo Boolle has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same bubble. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

Bracelet is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.9.0. It is the starting weapon of  Gyorunton and  Fake Sypha [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 30 minutes with either  Divano Thelma or  Iguana Gallo Valletto.
Its evolution is  Bi-Bracelet that can be further evolved into  Tri-Bracelet, both of which do not require any passive item.
## Effects
Bracelet shoots out a group of cloudy sparkle projectiles with limited  Duration at random enemies.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Projectiles have a chance to freeze enemies, chance is affected by  Luck, freezing duration is equal to Bracelet's  Duration.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Has a chance to fire more than twice every activation.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels
Bracelet has 6 levels. At max level, Bracelet gets +20 Base Damage, +10% Area, +1 Amount, and +2 Pierce.

| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 10.

The Bullova is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Dolores. It is dropped by  Specter of Iwanaga-hime in Yomi (north-west world) in Emerald Diorama.
Its Evolution is the  Falconwind, which requires the  Skull O'Maniac and Hell's Fury tech. It is unlocked by evolving it.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Bullova summons a giant battle axe that slashes horizontally. It ignores  Speed.
Can glimmer the "Hell's Fury" tech, creating a red vertical damaging zone across the screen, continuously damaging enemies it touches.

The Burning Alcarde is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is  Eric Lecarde's skill that is used when he is on low health.
HP-Critical skill when his health reaches below 20%, where he becomes invulnerable for 20 seconds, gains -20% Cooldown, and gets a flame aura that deals damage to surrounding enemies. The skill may only be activated again after recovering all HP. Receiving fatal damage resulting in a game-over will not trigger the skill.
## Trivia
- This is one of the few weapons in the game to have its own music theme.

C-U-Laser is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Lucia Zero [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Lucia Zero.
Its evolution is  Pronto Beam [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Tirajisú.
## Effects
C-U-Laser fires a line of piercing laser beams in the faced direction, the beams' starting point being slightly away from the character.  Duration affects the length of the laser beam and the overall damage it may deal.
The laser beams fired can move slightly with the character, but only as long as they're moving in the same direction as the lasers.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - The starting point of each laser explodes upon expiring, damaging enemies nearby. Explosion damage is affected by  Curse.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives C-U-Laser a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
## Levels
C-U-Laser has 8 Levels. At max level, C-U-Laser has +20 Base Damage, +40% Speed, +2 Amount, and +0.8 seconds of Duration.

| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 20%.

## Notes
- Because of the laser's firing offset, hitting enemies directly below or above the character can be troublesome. Try to have other weapons to cover these areas for you.
- Due to the lasers' abysmall base area, increasing  Amount and moving a lot can be a more efficient way to cover more of the screen early on as  Area will need to be increased a lot to affect the lasers adequately.
- Lasers travel out based on  Speed, so reaching -100% of it will prevent C-U-Laser from functioning.
## Trivia
- "C-U-Laser" is a pun on "see you later".

Candybox is a weapon selector from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.10.0. It is unlocked by discovering every standard evolution and union.
Its Gift is  Super Candybox II Turbo, obtainable only when opening a  Treasure Chest after obtaining a Candybox.
It is the starting weapon of  Big Trouser.  Queen Sigma can also buy the Candybox from the Merchant for 1,000, replacing the option to buy  Golden Eggs.
## Effects
Obtaining Candybox opens a list of all base weapons remaining to be obtained in the run. For a weapon to appear in the Candybox, it has to be used at least once in the entire save file beforehand.
Weapons that were banished will also still appear in the list. Its rarity is multiplied by  Luck. Under normal circumstances, it is only available once. If it is not taken when it is first offered, it will never be offered again with level ups.
It may also appear in treasure chests and requires a fully upgraded Weapon and Passive inventory (so that Coin Bags spawn in chests). Once these conditions are met, Candybox has a small luck-based chance to appear in any treasure chest the player opens, in place of a Big Coin Bag. Five-item treasure chest guarantees spawning a Candybox with the above condition maxed.
The following weapons cannot be picked due to being redundant for Candybox:
-  Morning Star[DLC]
-  Coat of Arms[DLC]
-  Spectral Sword[DLC]
-  Belnades' Spellbook[DLC]
-  Ebony Diabologue[DLC]
-  Intuition[DLC]
Unlocking and using all five Ode to Castlevania selectors mentioned above will unlock Candybox as an alternative starting weapon for  Alucard [DLC],  Shanoa [DLC], and  Soma Cruz [DLC].

- Candybox is one of the few ways to obtain more than six weapons outside of specific characters with hidden weapons, spawning weapons at certain levels, or picking up stage weapons.

Cardinal Rain is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Scarlet Needle and requires  Pummarola at max level.
## Effects
Cardinal Rain functions nearly identically to its predecessor,  Scarlet Needle, instead attacking any enemy on screen, presumably randomly, rather than the closest enemy to the player. Cardinal Rain retains the ability to pin enemies in place and uses the same type of damage number as Scarlet Needle.
Cardinal Rain has +3 Base Damage, +5 Amount, and +30 Pool Limit compared to Scarlet Needle.
The damage of Cardinal Rain is multiplied by ( 1 +  Recovery). 
While Cardinal Rain is active, blood will rain down across the screen, intensifying as this weapon's Amount increases. This rain is purely visual and deals no damage.
Cardinal Rain deals  Blood damage.
Cardinal Rain has a 0.05 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.05 seconds by the same needle. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. 
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Needles explode when they expire, dealing damage based on  Curse.
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Allows Cardinal Rain to fire faster while moving, increasing with  Move Speed.

Carnage Heart is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Troll Bomb [DLC] at max level and  NO FUTURE.
## Effects
Carnage Heart functions as an improved version of  NO FUTURE. Carnage Heart doubles the damage dealt by the explosions generated in retaliation and from those generated by projectiles as they bounce, and Carnage Heart's  Cooldown no longer depends on its  Duration, allowing it to fire much faster. Instead of the explosion radius being displayed with a test pattern, a miniature copy of the shockwaves generated by Troll Bomb and  Neutron Bombs are used instead.
Compared to  Troll Bomb, Carnage Heart has much lower Base Damage and greatly decreased  Cooldown.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy instead of in random directions, and gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Carréllo is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.4.2. It is the starting weapon of  Bianca Ramba. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Bianca Ramba is unlocked. It can also be obtained from  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000, by selecting this weapon from the  Candybox, or as a chance from the  Gold Finger Pickup when achieving the "Bronze Finger" tier.
Its evolution is  Carrozza!, which requires  Chaos Lazulia and reaching level 80 while playing as Bianca Ramba.
## Effects
Carréllo shoots a single cart that travels horizontally, with mechanical sparks emitting from the wheels, to the direction the player is facing. It bounces off of obstacles and the sides of the screen, running over any enemies along the way.
The amount of bounces before it shatters is determined by Amount, with its base Amount of 2 allowing it to bounce once. The explosion upon shattering also damages enemies.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Carréllo's carts to bounce three more times.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Carréllo's carts to bounce three more times.
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Carréllo's Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by Move Speed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Makes Carréllo aims at nearest enemy, allowing it travel to different directions. Also gain  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Carréllo has 8 levels. At max level, Carréllo has +90 Base Damage, +40% Area, +100% Speed, and +0.9 seconds Cooldown.

## Tips
- With appropriate amounts of Projectile Speed and Move Speed, the character can move at the same speed as the cart, preventing it from colliding with edges of the screen and reducing its bounces. This can be used to create a wall of up to 30 indefinitely lasting carts paving your way.

## Trivia
- Carréllo is the second weapon to have its Cooldown increased upon leveling up, the first being Song of Mana.
- Despite having a value in the chance attribute, the weapon does not utilize it.
- Carréllo's id is "CART2". "CART" is used for the Dairy Carts.
- "Carrello" means "Cart" in Italian, but the specific accent points, like many other puns in the game, to Roman dialect - although it would be pronounced "caréllo" then, with one "R" only.

Carrozza! is a morph from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the evolution of  Carréllo, and requires the  Chaos Lazulia relic and reaching level 80 while playing as  Bianca Ramba.
Alternatively, it can be obtained via Cosmic Finger rewards from  Gold Fingers or the Edition of  Bianca Ramba's  Survarot.
## Effects
Carrozza! retains the carts fired by  Carréllo, which bounces off of obstacles and the boundaries of the player's screen.
In addition to this, Carrozza! also summons the  Take Us Away train from Laborratory. This train is alternatingly summoned above and below the player, running across the screen. The  Area,  Duration, and  Speed of the train are set and cannot be changed. Instead, these stats increase the damage the train deals. Carréllo projectiles are affected normally.
The exact formula for the above damage increase is Might*(BaseDamage+0.001Duration+Speed+Area).
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Carrozza!'s carts to bounce three more times.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Carrozza!'s carts to bounce three more times.
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Carrozza!'s  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Carts aim at nearest enemy, and Carrozza! gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
With Limit Break, Carrozza! can be further leveled up.

Cavendish is an evolved weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Gros Michel [DLC], requiring  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Cavendish flings curving bananas in the faced direction and opposite of it, alternating between each direction, and spreading out for each banana. These bananas will always deal critical damage and explode, and do not despawn after exploding, so they expire only after exhausting all their bounces or the  Duration elapses. It also gains Base Damage and  Amount.
Cavendish also doubles the base critical hit chance of weapons that can deal critical hits.
Upon activation, there is a  Luck-based, 1 in 1,000 chance for Cavendish to trigger Bananastrophe, which displays the Cavendish joker, then shatters it and explodes into a burst of 8-bit Gros Michels bouncing all over the screen for a short period, much like  Gunastrophe.  Duration affects how long a bouncing banana can last, and Amount increases the number of bursts and the number of bananas each burst based on 50+CalculatedAmount*10.
Upon evolving Gros Michel into Cavendish, Outer Saboteur is removed from the passive slot and turns into Inner Saboteur, placed over the character's face and can still evolve other Ante Chamber DLC weapons. Obtaining Cavendish from a  Super Candybox II Turbo will give the player the option of obtaining Outer Saboteur via a Level Up.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Cavendish's projectiles to bounce off enemies two more times.
-  Slash (XVI) - Cavendish's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

-  Reinhardt Schneider's [DLC] critical damage bonus pairs excellently with this weapon, acting as a constant damage multiplier.
- This weapon can increase survivability by increasing the critical hit chance of  Bloody Tear and  Fuwalafuwaloo, which will heal upon crit.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a direct reference to the Cavendish joker from Balatro.
- The effect, where it has a 1 in 1,000 chance to trigger Bananastrophe in Vampire Survivors, is a reference to the effect of Cavendish in Balatro, where it provides x3 mult and has a 1 in 1,000 chance of going extinct after a played hand.
- The fact that  Gros Michel evolves to the Cavendish in Vampire Survivors is a reference to how the Cavendish becomes available after having an expired Gros Michel in Balatro.

Celestial Booster is a weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Perkeo [DLC]. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its evolution is  Negative Space [DLC], which requires  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Celestial Booster creates planets that orbit around the player. The weapon will start by summoning a rocket, with each additional  Amount, it will summon a new planet, starting with Mercury and ending with Pluto. Upon receiving a new planet, a Planet Card will appear above the player, showcasing which planet was received. A maximum of 10 projectiles can be summoned by this weapon, despite the Pool Limit of 100. This maximum accounts for both the Amount stat and the Amount that Celestial Booster receives from its levels.
Celestial Booster's damage increases with the amount of gold the player has collected during that run:
- Below 10,000, Celestial Booster will gain 0.0005 Base Damage, per Gold collected, up to +5 Base Damage at 10,000.
- Above 10,000, Celestial Booster's bonus base damage will follow the formula:
2.5*log100(runCoins)
runCoins≡total amount of gold collected during the run
Effectively, Celestial Booster will gain another +2.5 Base Damage for every 100x increase in gold above 10,000.
Celestial Booster is one of the few weapons not affected by  Cooldown. Instead, all of its planets will be active as soon as they are obtained.
## Levels
Celestial Booster has 9 levels. At max level, Celestial Booster has +7 Base Damage, +20% Speed, +20% Area, and +8 Amount.
| Level 1 | Planets orbit around you. Damage increases by amount of coins collected this run.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.

| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 5 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Area up by 10%.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 2.
| Level 7 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Area up by 10%.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 9 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 3.

## Tips
- Various sources of Gold, such as  Disco of Gold (XV),  Hail from the Future (X), and  Survarots, can greatly increase this weapon's performance.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the Rocket joker, and Celestial Packs from Balatro, which are used to gain Planet Cards.
- It is fitting that this weapon is associated with  Perkeo [DLC], given that in Balatro, Perkeo creates a negative copy of a consumable, which may be a Planet Card. Its evolution,  Negative Space [DLC], is a reference to this mechanic.
- It gains damage with more coins collected because Celestial Packs are bought with money in Balatro, thus getting more Planet Cards and powering up their associated hands. Rocket joker also provides money at the end of every round, while not mechanically referenced by how this weapon works, it is thematically related with money increasing its strength.
- Celestial Booster works similarly to the Blood  Song of Mana or  Mannajja weapon gained from  Blood Astronomia (XXI).

Celestial Dusting is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.5.1. It is the starting weapon of  O'Sole Meeo. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after O'Sole Meeo is unlocked. It can also be obtained from  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000, or by selecting this weapon from  Candybox.
Its evolution is  Profusione D'Amore, which requires  Chaos Altemanna and reaching level 80 while playing as O'Sole Meeo.
## Effects
Celestial Dusting fires flowers away from the player character's walking direction that bounce off of walls and obstacles, but pierce through an unlimited number of enemies. As they reach the end of their  Duration, they slow down and shed petals in a small X shape, dealing additional damage to nearby enemies.
 Move Speed increases its overall spawn rate when moving, when the character stops it initiates the default  Cooldown. Celestial Dusting ignores  Speed bonuses outside of its level ups.
Celestial Dusting has a 0.3 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.3 seconds by the same flower. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
At max level, Celestial Dusting gains a 66% chance to generate a  Little Heart when an enemy is defeated. This chance is unaffected by  Luck.
In Il Molise in particular, the Celestial Dusting provides additional health to Molisanos, instead of damaging them.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Celestial Dusting's Little Hearts to heal 2 points of health and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows the flowers to explode when they expire. The explosions also have the same chance to generate Little Hearts. Damage is based on  Curse.
## Levels
Celestial Dusting has 8 levels. At max level, Celestial Dusting has +5 Base Damage, +90% Speed, +1 to Amount, +1.0 seconds to Duration, and has a chance to generate Little Hearts when enemies are defeated.

## Tips
- Celestial Dusting fires rather quickly, so with some  Amount,  Cooldown, and  Move Speed bonuses, it can produce a constant stream of flowers behind you.
- Like  Hellfire, Celestial Dusting benefits heavily from  Area bonuses increasing the size of the vast amount of flowers.
- By tapping direction keys rapidly, Celestial Dusting can shoot out flowers all around the character away from where the character is facing. If you have to stay still around a dense group of enemies, it can retain the faster fire rate from moving.
- Uniquely, in Il Molise, the plant enemies in this stage are healed instead of damaged by Celestial Dusting's plants. The player will still gain some passive experience by healing the plants. Healing the plants for an extended amount of time will eventually unlock a secret character.
- Notably, the healing appears to add max health, instead of just regenerating missing ones. This means that Celestial Dusting can increase the health of the plants past their normal cap, and cause them to become effectively immortal.
- The amount of health the plants get is dependent on the damage that would be typically dealt, divided by 5[Verify].
- When using  Twilight Requiem (II), the explosion from the flowers expiring also heals plants, as they inherit the property of the weapon, like they can generate  Little Heart if the explosion kills an enemy.

 Celestial Dusting as featured in the O'Sole Meeo pin set.
## Trivia
- Celestial Dusting is a reference to the 2006 action-adventure game Ōkami, in which a white wolf goddess and main protagonist Amaterasu leaves grass and flowers behind her as she walks and runs.
- She can use her tail dipped in ink to stroke on a screenshot of the environment with different symbols and creates different effects, the techniques are called Celestial Brush, with "brush" being a synonym for "dusting".
- One of the Celestial Brush techniques is Bloom, which revives plant life by drawing a circle around a dying one, generating Praise that is used to upgrade aspects of the character like max health and amount of ink pot used for the techniques. This is referenced in Il Molise where Celestial Dusting heals the plants and still generating experience.
- This weapon is individually featured as part of the  O'Sole Meeo pin set.
- This is one of the three weapons where that is the case, with the two others being the  Gatti Amari and the  Cross.

Celestial Voulge is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.7.0. It is the evolution of  Glass Fandango, and requires  Wings at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
## Effect
Celestial Voulge has two attack patterns which involve firing a short-ranged translucent blue blade: While moving, it attacks in the faced direction; while standing still, it will have the standard attack speed delay and attack in six directions around the character. It gains a bonus to  Area and  Amount.
 Move Speed increases its overall fire rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.
It gains 2.5 times  Area during the time-freeze triggered by  Orologion. It deals triple damage to frozen enemies.
Collecting  Orologions while Celestial Voulge is present also transforms them into Starry Heavens. They still freeze enemies as usual, but cause them to move towards the player while taking continuous damage.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have a 5% chance to occur. It can also freeze enemies, which have a 5% chance to occur. The chances are affected by  Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Increases Celestial Voulge's critical strike damage to 4x.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Enemies frozen by Celestial Voulge will explode.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - Enemies frozen by Celestial Voulge will drop  Crystallized Soul when killed.

## Tips
- Celestial Voulge synergizes well with  Crystal Cries (XII) as it can deal extra damage to frozen enemies. It has a chance to freeze enemies by default on top of improving Orologion into Starry Heavens, making freeze builds even stronger.
- Starry Heavens eliminates the only weakness of Orologion, which is frozen enemies would stop in place. The player has to move to spawn more enemies, and as they spawn from offscreen, they are further away and take more time to defeat them, lowering the rate of new enemies spawning considerably. Besides allowing frozen enemies to move, it deals damage over time as a full-screen effect, making it even more efficient at clearing hordes of enemies.
## Trivia
- Celestial Voulge is the first weapon that has the ability to "evolve" a pickup item.
- Starry Heavens was inspired by the Galaxy Stop ability from Final Fantasy Tactics.

Centralis Custos is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by defeating 7,000 enemies with  Cornell.
Its union is  Trinum Custodem [DLC], which also requires  Dextro Custos [DLC] and  Sinestro Custos [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Centralis Custos creates an aura above the character with a red Cerberus head and three concentric circles around it, similar to  Garlic, damaging enemies it touches. It also provides +10  Armor, +2  Recovery, and -10%  Cooldown boost for a brief time after the character takes damage, with  Duration increasing its length.
Cooldown acts similarly to Hitbox Delay for Centralis Custos. Damage will be dealt instantly to an enemy if they have never been in the circle before, after which they cannot be hit by it again until the Centralis Custos' Cooldown is over, even if they temporarily leave its area.
## Levels
Centralis Custos has 6 levels. At max level, Centralis Custos has +12 Base Damage, +40% Area, and -0.3 seconds of Cooldown.

## Trivia
- This weapon is based on Arma Custos, with its sprite based on Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia. It appears on top of Shanoa when active and boosts STR (strength), the value increases as she takes damage. This effect gets translated as an Armor, Recovery, and Cooldown boost for Centralis Custos.
- However, Arma Custos was only a buff and does not do damage (its name is "Armor Guardian" in Latin). With it gaining aura damage, it is no longer just an armor so the name gets changed to Centralis Custos ("Central Guardian" in Latin), similar to the other two directional guardians  Dextro Custos and  Sinestro Custos.

Chaos Rune is a secret weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is unlocked by casting the spell "guinigigi".
Its evolution is  Wicked Ruler, which requires  Spellbinder at max level.
## Effects
Chaos Rune shoots red runes upwards from the bottom of the screen, passing through enemies and arcing back down chaotically.
- Note that the runes fired by Chaos Rune are only able to deal damage after reaching their apex and falling back down. Runes will not deal damage to enemies when they are shot upwards.
 Amount affects how many runes are summoned with each activation, while  Speed and  Duration affect how many times each rune can deal damage.
Chaos Rune has a 0.03 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.03 seconds by the same rune. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
Chaos Rune has 8 levels. At max level, Chaos Rune has +20 Base Damage, +3 Amount, and +2 Pierce.

- Given that no character has the Chaos Rune as their starting weapon (as of 1.14), after unlocking it with the spell it can only be obtained by choosing it when leveling up. Once it has been obtained and added to the collection it will then become accessible through the  Candybox, allowing  Big Trouser and other characters to start with it.
- Because of Chaos Rune's Rarity, when trying to obtain it for the first time players may wish to aggressively seal or banish other weapons, or use a character with many rerolls such as  Queen Sigma.
## Trivia
- Chaos Rune was added in the 1.14 update, though poncle had never hinted about this weapon nor made it unlockable by any other means before the completion of the Gallo Tower ARG.
- The color and overall style of this weapon's runes are identical to the runes that can be found in the Secrets menu.
- Similar runes can also be seen in the background of the Gallo Tower.

Cherry Bomb is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.2.13. It is the starting weapon of  Yatta Cavallo. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Yatta Cavallo is unlocked. It can also be obtained from the  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000, or by selecting it from  Candybox.
Its evolution is  Yatta Daikarin, which requires  Chaos Rosalia and reaching level 80 while playing as Yatta Cavallo.
## Effect
Cherry Bomb throws a small spinning bomb at the nearest enemy. The bomb travels in a straight line, bouncing off enemies, walls, and edges of the screen. They will decelerate and eventually stop; when they explode, they create a shockwave, flower petals, and a firework with a similar sound effect.
Depending on its level and the  Luck stat, there is a chance for the bomb to explode.  Might and  Area affect both the bouncing Cherry Bombs and their explosions.
## Levels
Cherry Bomb has 8 levels. At max level, Cherry Bomb has +10 Base Damage, +100% Area, +60% Speed, +1 to Amount, and a 60% chance to explode.
