Firearm is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Brad Fang [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Brad Fang.
Its evolution is  Fire-L3GS [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Candelabrador.
## Effects
Firearm fires a spinning ring of fire projectiles at the nearest enemy.  Amount affects how many fire projectiles a ring contains.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Fire projectiles explode on contact, effectively increase its damage output.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

FireBall is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is a starting weapon of  Sargon. It can alternatively be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "fuocopalla".
Its union is  FireStall, which also requires  FireFall and  FireWall at max level.
## Effects
FireBall releases a fireball in the direction the character is moving, piercing enemies it hits. The fireball starts small, but grows in size over time until it expires. When it hits the edge of the screen, it bounces in an arc.  Duration increases how long fireballs last.
Once FireBall's projectiles reach an area of 3 units, or around 4.29x the base size, further increases to their Area will begin having a reduced effect, scaling logarithmically instead of linearly.
 Area increases the damage of FireBall's projectiles. Every +1% increase to Area will increase the damage of FireBall by 1%, maxing out at a multiplier of 5x at +400% Area.
FireFall has a 5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 5 seconds by the same fireball. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX): Allows FireBall's projectiles to deal half of their Base Damage in an area as retaliatory damage.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX): Enemies defeated by FireBall's projectiles will drop  Scorched Souls.
## Levels
FireBall has 6 levels. At max level, FireBall has +25 Base Damage, +60% Speed, +50% Area, +0.5 seconds of Duration, and -1 second of Cooldown.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Generates an expanding damaging zone. Damage multiplied by Area.
| Level 2 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 20%.
| Level 3 | Base Area up by 25%. Effect last 0.5 seconds longer.
| Level 4 | Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds. Base Damage up by 10. Base Speed up by 20%
| Level 5 | Base Area up by 25%. Effect lasts 0.5 seconds longer.
| Level 6 | Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds. Base Damage up by 10. Base Speed up by 20%.

FireFall is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is a starting weapon of  Sargon. It can alternatively be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "fuocaduta".
Its union is  FireStall, which also requires  FireBall and  FireWall at max level.
## Effects
FireFall drops a small column of fire from the sky on the furthest on-screen enemy, dealing damage in a circle when it lands as fire spirals outward. Consecutive fireballs, from increased  Amount, will target enemies near the initial enemy targeted, trending towards the player.
Due to a bug, FireFall currently does not possess any special  Might scaling, unlike weapons such as  SpellStrike [DLC].
FireFall has a 0.25 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.25 seconds by the same fire column. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX): Allows FireFall's projectiles to deal half of their Base Damage in an area as retaliatory damage.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX): Enemies defeated by FireFall's projectiles will drop  Scorched Souls.

FireStall is a weapon union from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Megalo Sargon. It is the union of  FireFall,  FireBall, and  FireWall.
## Effects
FireStall retains similar behavior to its constituent parts, with minor changes centering around the 2 sets of oscillations sets of  FireWall:
-  FireFall will target the oscillating sets of FireWall, rather than the further enemy.
-  FireBall will instead be emitted from the sets of FireWall. Since there are 2 sets of FireWall, 2 instances of FireBall will be emitted rather than 1.
-  FireWall is duplicated and reversed. Two sets of FireWall exist, oscillating up and down on either side of the player. FireWall retains its ability to rotate with the player.
All 3 parts of FireStall retain their special stat scalings.
FireStall will retain all Limit Break upgrades given to FireFall, FireBall, and FireFall when evolving.
Every 20-30 seconds, reduced by  Cooldown, FireStall will initiate a singularity. During this time, the two sets of FireWall will begin spiraling towards the character, in the center of the screen. When they collide, a wave of fire is released, damaging enemies along its path. The Base Damage of this singularity follows the formula:
Amount(BaseDamage+0.001Duration+Speed+Area).
Additionally, the Base Damage of the singularity will increase by 5 for every time the singularity has activated. There is no limit to this bonus.
FireStall's singularity has a 0.05 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.05 seconds by the same singularity. FireStall's constituent parts retain their individual Hitbox Delays. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. 
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX): Allows FireStall's projectiles to deal half of their Base Damage in an area as retaliatory damage.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX): Enemies defeated by FireStall's projectiles will drop  Scorched Souls.
## Levels
With Limit Break, FireStall can be further leveled up.

FireWall is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is a starting weapon of  Sargon. It can alternatively be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "fuocomuro".
Its union is  FireStall, which also requires  FireFall and  FireBall at max level.
## Effects
FireWall creates a small arc of flames in the direction the character is facing, rotating alongside them. 
The base number of flames is 2, with each additional Amount increasing the number of flames by 3. As more flames are added, the weapon's arc will expand, adding more arcs as FireWall reaches the maximum number of flames in a given arc. The maximum number of flames in each arc is as follows, repeating cyclically:
| Arc Number | Maximum Flames
| 1 | 6
| 2 | 8
| 3 | 7
| 4 | 5
| 5 | 3
| 6 | 2
| 7 | 1
Each flame can hit enemies 4 times, which each level the weapon has increases this value by 4 up to a maximum of 24 hits at max level. Note that this is not the same as the weapon's hit rate, which is impacted by Hitbox Delay. 
 Duration increases how long flames linger before expiring.
FireWall has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same flame. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX): Allows FireWall's projectiles to deal half of their Base Damage in an area as retaliatory damage.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX): Enemies defeated by FireWall's flames will drop  Scorched Souls.
## Levels
FireWall has 6 levels. At max level, FireWall has +10 Base Damage, and +4 Amount

| Level 1 | Generates a directional damaging zone. Greatly affected by Amount.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 4 | Fires 2 more projectile.
| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile.

Flamberge is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Final Emperor. It is dropped by the Malevolent Door Spirit in Grelon (South-East world) in Emerald Diorama.
Its Evolution is the  Zweihander, which requires the Bull Crush tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Once triggered, the Flamberge throws spinning swords upwards, which will drop down and stab into the ground, like a area-of-effect version of  Axe. It ignores Speed and Duration.
Can glimmer the "Bull Crush" tech, summoning a giant sword that slashes a large area.
Flamberge has a 2% chance to critically hit for x2 damage. The critical hit chance is affected by Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Increases Flamberge's critical strike damage by 4x.
## Levels
The Flamberge has 6 levels. At max level, the Flamberge has +1  Amount, +10 Base Damage, and +40%  Area.

| Level 6 | Base Area up by 20%.

Flames of Misspell is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.0. It is the starting weapon of  Avatar Infernas. Other characters can obtain it after Avatar Infernas is unlocked.
Its evolution is  Ashes of Muspell, which requires  Torrona's Box at max level.
## Effects
Flames of Misspell shoots a burst of flames, similar to  Nduja Fritta Tanto, in the direction the player is moving or last moved.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Flames of Misspell's flames explode upon hitting an enemy, dealing half of its damage in an area.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Gains a chance to fire more than twice when activated.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels
Flames of Misspell has 8 levels. At max level, Flames of Misspell has +20 Base Damage, +100% Area, +50% Speed, and -1.5 seconds of Cooldown.

| Level 5 | Base Speed up by 25%.
| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 7 | Base Area up by 50%. Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds.
| Level 8 | Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds.

## Trivia
- The name of this weapon may be a reference to  The Directer being misspelled.
- Flames of Misspell is a reference to Muspelheim, also known as Muspell, the realm of fire, home to the fire giants in Norse mythology.

Flash Arrow is a weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Keitha Muort.
Flash Arrow can be evolved into  Millionaire [DLC] with  Bracer at max level.
## Effects
Flash Arrow shoots an arrow in the direction the player is moving or last moved. It can pierce through many enemies.
 Amount multiplies its damage instead of providing more arrows.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have a 20% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) doubles the damage of Flash Arrow's critical hits, causing them to deal 4x damage.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) allows the arrows to bounce off of the edges of the screen three times. Upon bouncing, the arrow completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them according to the edge.
## Levels
Flash Arrows has 8 levels. At max level, Flash Arrows has +30 Base Damage, +40%  Area, +50%  Speed, +21 Pierce, -2 seconds of  Cooldown.

## Trivia
- Flash Arrow is a reference to Flash Arrow, a weak early-game tech in multiple SaGa games.
- Flash Arrow was created in response to players requesting a "Bowgun" weapon and poncle honoring that request, but giving it a twist so at worst characters are throwing the arrow. They acknowledged having weapons of that type was important, however they did not wish to "over-incorporate" them in fear of violating the narrative boundaries of the game which they had originally set.
- This weapon is quite similar to Knife.

The Fleuret is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is one of the two starting weapons of  Tsunanori Mido. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its Evolution is the  Dress Sword, which requires the Crystalline Carve tech, and can be evolved into  Espada Ropera with Shocking Rush tech; Fully evolving it unlocks  Splashers starting weapon and solo skin for  Tsunanori Mido.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Fleuret slashes at closest enemy within attacking range, creating a damaging area around it, similar to  Confodere. Speed affects damage. It ignores Duration.
Can glimmer the "Crystalline Carve" tech.

Forbidden Siren is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Screams from the Void and max level  Attractorb.
## Effects
Forbidden Siren retains nearly all of the behavior of  Screams from the Void, including its ability to retaliate, as both the Screams from the Void part and suction part of Forbidden Siren are considered separate weapons. Unlike some other weapons that function as two distinct weapons, such as weapons in the  Belnades' Spellbook [DLC], the effects of Forbidden Siren do not depend on method of obtainment; both factors of the weapon will always be present. When activating, Forbidden Siren will create music note projectiles that are purely visual and deal no damage.
Forbidden Siren will increase the damage of Screams from the Void by 1.5x and increase its knockback stat by 5. When evolving from Screams from the Void, Forbidden Siren will also retain any Limit Break upgrades given to Screams from the Void. 
Forbidden Siren creates an invisible area of effect that is the same size as the weapon's Area. This area of effect is guaranteed to  Defang any enemies in it, except if they have defang resistance. Enemies in this zone will be continuously pulled towards the user.
Compared to Screams from the Void, Forbidden Siren has -2 Amount, +0.6 seconds of Duration, +0.45 seconds of Hitbox Delay, +1 Knockback, and +20 Pool Limit.
Forbidden Siren itself, and not its hidden Screams from the Void, has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the inward pull. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. 
- Due to the central pull being constant, and Screams from the Void being treated as a separate weapon, Forbidden Siren effectively has the same Hitbox Delay as Screams from the Void.

Four Seasons is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Menya Moonspell [DLC].
Its evolution is  Godai Shuffle [DLC], which requires  Candelabrador at max level.
## Effects
Four Seasons creates two orbiting beads diagonally away from the character, with four pairs of them forming a rectangle around the character. They are the center of four explosions, with flowers, green leaves, autumn leaves, and snowflakes; with the characters 春 (spring), 夏 (summer), 秋 (autumn), and 冬 (winter); in the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right beads respectively in that order.
 Area causes the explosion to be bigger, while level ups can move the beads further apart until they reach the corners.  Amount and  Duration affect damage of Four Seasons instead; with the base damage formula (baseDamage + Duration in seconds) * Amount.

Fulgur is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Yoko Belnades. It can be dropped by defeating the The Creature boss in the unlockable area near the Parm Aegis in the DLC stage. It is unlocked by evolving it.
It can be evolved into  Tenebris Tonitrus with Max level  Duplicator.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effects
Fulgur summons an azure magic circle at the facing-middle edge of the screen. Once activated, it teleports between the middle, top, and bottom edge of the screen, and simultaneously, fires a piercing projectile from the character’s location to the location of the magic circle each time it teleports.

-  Tragic Princess (III) - Fulgur's cooldown reduces while moving.

Fuwalafuwaloo is a weapon union from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.7.2. It is the union of  Vento Sacro at max level and  Bloody Tear.
It is the starting weapon of  Rose De Infernas.
## Effects
Fuwalafuwaloo, similar to  Vento Sacro, creates multiple dark red slashes horizontally in front of the character and a circle of slashes that cycle around the character, damaging all enemies in the area.
Fuwalafuwaloo's Base Damage is dramatically increased compared to Vento Sacro, and it is half of  Bloody Tear. It has one more slash per burst and a slight increase in Knockback.
 Duration increases how long the hitbox lingers.  Move Speed increases its overall fire rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.  Speed makes the slashes go further out horizontally.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 5% chance to occur. This is lowered by 5% compared to Bloody Tear. The chance is affected by  Luck.
The character can heal 8 points of health if an enemy was damaged by a critical hit. This lifesteal effect has a 0.5 seconds delay before it can be triggered again, which is halved from Bloody Tear. It is not affected by  Recovery.
Critical hits also trigger an explosion which has a separate 0.5 seconds delay. It spawns on top of the enemy it hits, deals the critical damage, and is affected by  Area. The explosions cannot trigger the lifesteal effect.
Fuwalafuwaloo gains bonus damage from walking nonstop. It caps at 40 flat damage. The actual bonus comes from distance walked divided by 200,000 up to the cap, which takes 8 million units. This bonus will reset once the character stop moving. The unit is for distance walked is slightly arbitrary and it is not as big as it seems in the game.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Fuwalafuwaloo's critical hit to heal double their amount and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Slash (XVI) - Fuwalafuwaloo's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy horizontally, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

## Tips
- With enough  Amount,  Cooldown, and  Move Speed, Fuwalafuwaloo can be a very deadly weapon to where you are facing horizontally.
- Fuwalafuwaloo can deal critical damage by default. The more  Luck you have, the more likely you are to deal critical hits. Luck can be increased with  Clover,  Little Clovers, or the Luck PowerUp. Luck can also be scaled throughout the game with  Wicked Season (XIII) at a rate of 1% per 2 levels.
-  Slash (XVI) doubles critical damage, making it very powerful in conjunction with this weapon that deals its critical damage over a wide area.
- Fuwalafuwaloo's lifesteal and explosion effect can only trigger twice per second and only on critical hits. This means that to trigger them the fastest, you must maximize your Luck, Cooldown, and Movement Speed bonuses to decrease the downtime of it not attacking with critical hits.
- Fuwalafuwaloo has a normal amount of knockback, but it has an Area-of-Effect that can be controlled unlike most weapons, so it can be useful when trying to escape enemies closing in on you.
- Moving vertically while facing only one direction with a wall behind you can be very effective.
- Because of the uninterrupted movement needed to effectively use this weapon and its base weapon, it has negative synergy with  Shadow Pinion and  Valkyrie Turner, which require stopping to be more effective.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the Valmanway weapon from the Castlevania series, ironically, it is an evolution of the sword instead of a whip. The icon is similar to whip from Portrait of Ruin.
- The lifesteal effect may be a reference to Dark Metamorphosis spell from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, as it also heals 8 health when it "draws blood" (deals critical hits), which a whip can do. Instead of multiplying  Bloody Tear's lifesteal value by 2, Fuwalafuwaloo halves the delay instead, making it even more likely is an intentional reference.
- The name of this weapon appears to be a reference to the character Fuwalafuwalu from the video game Suikoden V.
- Fuwalafuwaloo is the first weapon evolved from uniting a weapon with an evolved weapon.
- The bonuses for continuously walking give up to 10  Amount to the weapon is changed in patch 0.8.0. In total, the player has to walk 1,000,000 units, divided by the base Amount of the weapon, which takes 125,000 units walked.
- Fuwalafuwaloo was the only evolved weapon to not have a rarity of 1, but rather one of its base weapon's rarity of 50. This is fixed in patch 0.7.3.
- In the same patch, it used to have +100%  Speed compared to maxed  Vento Sacro.
- Fuwalafuwaloo is the weapon that contains the longest word in its name.

Gale Force is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Julia Laforeze. Once the  Capra Gate is unlocked, the player can obtain it from defeating  Zephyr (enemy) in the middle of the Clock Tower on the Ode to Castlevania stage. It is unlocked by evolving it.
It can be evolve into  Pneuma Tempestas with Max level  Bracer.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effects
Being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Gale Force has a charge time before activation, which is indicated by the brightness of its created magic circle.
Gale Force summons a green magic circle in the horizontally-faced direction. Once activated, it stops in place and fires multiple light projectiles forward (affected by Amount) that curve backwards, piercing through and damaging enemies as they travel.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Obtains a counterpart of Gale Force that mirrors it.
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Gale Force bounces up to 3 times when hitting enemies, which can greatly change their traveling path.

Halts XP gain. Experience Gems turn into exploding projectiles. All Treasure Chests contain at least 3 items.
Game Killer (0) is one of the Arcanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by defeating  The Ender in Cappella Magna.
The  Fleaman [DLC] starts with this Arcana.
## Overview
While Game Killer (0) is active, all experience gained from  Experience Gems is halted, and instead, Experience Gems act as exploding projectiles that hurl themselves towards the closest enemy when collected. Additionally, all  Treasure Chests now contain at least three weapons or passive items.
 Growth multiplies the damage dealt by the gems and uses the  Stained Glass explosion effect.
## Tips
-  Gorgeous Moon can provide a periodic vacuum effect to collect all of the gems at once, while also creating one more gem when it kills an enemy. The  Crown is required to evolve the  Pentagram, so each gem will also do more damage due to the damage scaling with Growth.
- Game Killer (0) can benefit  Porta Ladonna,  Suor Clerici,  Sir Ambrojoe, and  Santa Ladonna due to their special level 1 stat bonuses. Pairing up with an Arcana that boost the effectiveness of one weapon only like  Beginning (X),  Silent Old Sanctuary (XX), and Arcanas that have the starting weapon listed can be a viable strategy. Clerici's area bonus notably applies to the Game Killer (0)'s explosions, allowing it to achieve a high DPS.
- If selected at level 1, purchasing weapons from the Master Librarian and Merchant can be extremely beneficial.
- Alternatively, in non-Limit Break runs, Game Killer (0) can be used with characters who have a level cap on their bonus ability, such as  Antonio Belpaese,  Arca Ladonna, and  Divano Thelma, as they do not gain any further benefit upon reaching a certain level.
- If needed, Game Killer (0) can be used to put a stop to the leveling of certain characters with infinitely scaling Curse, like  Gyorunton.
- Thanks to its ability to gain experience from gold coins,  Sammy [DLC] can continue leveling up even with Game Killer (0).
- If the player wants to obtain as many passives as they can, they can use this arcana alongside the Moonlight Bolero (VI), which can allow for the player to obtain black chests. Given that all treasure chests contain at least three items, players have a significantly higher chance at receiving passives they haven't obtained yet from these chests.
- Having the  Attractorb in hand, especially in a higher level, will allow for the player to pick up gems more easily, hence be able to attack enemies better.
- Picking up a  Vacuum will allow for the player to attract all of the gems and thus deal a burst of damage towards enemies.
- Game Killer stacks with its Darkana counterpart  Stake to Your Heart (0), as both Experience Gems and gold coins are generated from enemies when both Arcanas are selected.
## Trivia
- The name of this Arcana is a reference to the song "Vampire Killer", which is the theme song for the first level in Castlevania.
- Game Killer (0) can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "ilmatto", which means "the fool" in Italian.
- This makes Game Killer (0) a representation of The Fool Major Arcana card, symbolizing new beginnings, opportunities, freedom, innocence, curiosity, and hidden potential.
- This is reflected in its ability for the player to deviate from the standard gameplay formula of gaining experience and leveling up in favor of taking unknown chances from treasure chests.
- The Game Killer (0) as a standalone weapon creates a placeholder piano that aims straight at enemies. It can also be affected by  Amount and  Cooldown, which is not the case when it is an Arcana effect.

Garlic is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Poe Ratcho and  Bitterfly [DLC]. It is unlocked by picking up five  Floor Chicken.
Its evolution is  Soul Eater, which requires  Pummarola.
## Effects
Garlic places an aura of three rotating concentric circles around the player, dealing damage to enemies inside it.
 Cooldown acts similarly to Hitbox Delay for Garlic. Damage will be dealt instantly to an enemy if they have never been in the circle before, after which they cannot be hit by it again until the Garlic's Cooldown is over, even if they temporarily leave its area.
Enemies hit by Garlic will take more knockback and become more vulnerable to freeze. If the enemy is not immune to debuffs, each hit applies +0.3 knockback to the enemy until the maximum knockback they can take and -0.1 to freeze resistance until it reaches 0.
## Arcanas
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Garlic's  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows Garlic to deal extra flat damage based on  Armor.
-  Blood Astronomia (XXI) - Allows Garlic to place multiple damage zones on the ground.
## Levels
Garlic has 8 levels. At max level, Garlic has +10 Base Damage, +100% Area, and -0.3 seconds of Cooldown.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Damages nearby enemies. Reduces resistance to knockback and freeze.
| Level 2 | Base Area up by 40%. Base Damage up by 2.
| Level 3 | Cooldown reduced by 0.1 seconds. Base Damage up by 1.
| Level 4 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 1.
| Level 5 | Cooldown reduced by 0.1 seconds. Base Damage up by 2.
| Level 6 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 1.
| Level 7 | Cooldown reduced by 0.1 seconds. Base Damage up by 1.
| Level 8 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 2.

With Limit Break, Garlic can be further leveled up.

## Tips
- The debuffs applied by Garlic are its most useful ability late game. Strong enemies that take multiple hits to kill will be easier to keep at bay thanks to increased knockback, and some boss enemies can become vulnerable to freezing when kept in the circle for long enough.
- Combined with a weapon to constantly knock enemies away, such as  Unholy Vespers or  Mannajja, Garlic can enable the player to sit entirely still.
-  Clock Lancet has natural synergy with Garlic; Garlic decreases the enemy's resistance to freezing, allowing Clock Lancet to freeze bosses, and even very powerful frozen enemies can easily be killed by keeping Garlic's Area-of-Effect over them.
- If the player intends to stay idle, Garlic works well when paired with  Attractorb, as enemies that die instantly to Garlic may drop experience just out of reach of the player.
- Garlic's aura can kill most weak enemies instantly on low curse. Killing weak enemies quickly can lead to windfalls of experience and set up much earlier. Even in later waves, some swarms of enemies can still be instantly killed by it.
- This weapon can be quite effective against Bat Swarms and/or earlier bat enemies in Bat Country.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the garlic item from the Castlevania series. The weapon's sprite is extremely similar to the item and the effect is also similar as the item paralyzes and inflicts continuous minor damage to enemies.
- In the announcement trailer for online co-op, at the 5-second mark, in a fictional desktop OS, it is shown that the Garlic has its own desktop app called Garlic.exe. In that video, it is just a simple app that shows a GIF of a spinning, higher-resolution pixelated garlic.
- A recurring gag among the Vampire Survivors community is that the Garlic looks like a pair of testicles, so much so that poncle themselves have officially acknowledged this joke on their social media at least twice.
- poncle has a stress toy that is shaped like a garlic (different from the game) and has a "poncle" label on it.

Gatti Amari is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.5.0. It is the starting weapon of  Giovanna Grana. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes as Giovanna Grana.
Its evolution is  Vicious Hunger, which requires  Stone Mask.
## Effects
Gatti Amari summons cats from a hexagram on the edge of the screen. These cats mostly walk around in a straight line and may change direction after a while, and have a chance to attack with their claws when they are close to the enemies. They can also occasionally hurt the player character when they are close to it, dealing twice the usual damage. When a cat is close to another, they have a chance to start a fight, which creates a huge Area-of-Effect of cartoonish scuffle cloud that lasts for a while. If a cat walks over a Pickup on the screen, it gets automatically consumed, affecting the cat in different ways.
 Area affects both how big the claw attacks and the scuffle are.  Duration affects how long the cats remain on the screen as well as how long the scuffle lasts.
Gatti Amari's scratches have a 1 second Hitbox Delay and its scuffle has a 0.03 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second and 0.03 seconds respectively. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. This does not apply to claw attacks as they do not last long enough to hit twice.
## Interactions
Pickups consumed by the cats have varying effects on them:
-  Floor Chicken permanently increases the chance stat and Base Damage.
-  Nduja Fritta Tanto explodes the cat that consumed it.
- The explosion is the same as from  Heart of Fire (XIX).
-  Little Clover and  Gilded Clover make the cat that consumes them run twice as fast.
-  Orologion freezes the cat that consumed it. It can be used by the player instead.
-  Rosary and  Vacuum have no additional effects. It can be used by the player instead.
The chance for most interactions of the cats is affected by  Luck, multiplying the chance stat of the weapon.
- Increases the chance for the cats to attack enemies.
- Decreases the chance for the cats to attack the player.
- Increases the chance for them to start a scuffle.
- Increases the chance of Pickups that are not beneficial to the cats being used by the player instead.
## Floor Chicken
Floor Chicken, when collected by the cats, permanently increases the chance stat and attack damage of all cats. The chance stat is multiplied by 1.1 every time a chicken is collected. The Base Damage increase per chicken is calculated with the formula:
bonus damage per=1−min(0.95,C108),
where 'C' is the total amount of chicken collected. The minimum-function breaks even at 102 chickens, after which every chicken collected grants 0.05 Base Damage.
The total bonus damage, up to 102 chickens, can be calculated using the following equation:
total bonus damage=C×(215−C)216
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Flock Destroyer. It levels up as Gatti Amari does, it spawns three new types of cats and benefits from Limit Breaking.

## Tips
- Gatti Amari benefits from every stat bonus that can affect weapon stats. It is best with  Luck and  Floor Chicken.
- As the scuffle already has a big radius,  Candelabrador can increase its effectiveness by a lot.
-  Duration is also extremely effective, as it makes the cats and the scuffle last longer. Combined with reduced  Cooldown and  Amount increasing the number of cats on screen, it greatly increases the chance of them starting a fight.
- The scuffle deals damage at an extremely rapid pace. With enough stat bonuses to ensure constant catfights, and especially if the  Gemini (I) Arcana is selected, Gatti Amari is among the most powerful weapons in the game, outclassing most evolved weapons as well as its own evolution,  Vicious Hunger. Unless you specifically need gold, it is usually best to keep Gatti Amari unevolved.
- The cats need to consume at least 25 Floor Chicken to guarantee no negative effects will ever happen with no additional Luck from other sources.
- Gatti Amari's friendly fire can be used to trigger certain effects, such as the retaliatory explosion of  NO FUTURE or the effects of  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI).
- Unless you have high Luck, it is recommended to have some way of healing if you plan on picking up this weapon. If you have maxed out regeneration in the shop,  Sarabande of Healing (VI) can help your natural regeneration keep up with the cats' damage output.  Pummarola and  Bloody Tear can also help keep your health topped up.
- Gatti Amari and  Divine Bloodline (IX) should seldom be taken together until later due to Divine Bloodline increasing the friendly fire damage Gatti Amari.

## Trivia
- When level up options contain Gatti Amari, instead of raining  Experience Gems, it rains cats. It is probably a reference to the saying "raining cats and dogs".
- "Gatti Amari" is Italian for "bitter cats", although it resembles the expression "cazzi amari" ("bitter dicks") which colloquially means "shit gets real".
- With every level increase while playing as Giovanna Grana, her default background music increases slightly in pitch and tempo.
- The cats moving twice as fast when consuming  Little Clover or  Gilded Clover is a reference to when they consume catnip.
- Before  Bianca Ramba was added to the roadmap, there was a creature on all fours among the character silhouettes in her place. This caused speculation that the cats from Gatti Amari could have been planned to be released as a character originally. However, the speculation is debunked as it was the silhouette of  O'Sole Meeo, whom was released some weeks later.
- This weapon is individually featured as part of the  Giovanna Grana pin set.
- This is one of the three weapons where that is the case, with the two others being  Celestial Dusting and  Cross.
- In Episode 8 of Sopravvissuti ai vampiri,  Ameya Aisling mentions that she brought Lolo with her. Even though Lolo is supposed to be a black cat, it is depicted as a Gatti Amari in that video.

Gaze of Gaea is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.13. It is the starting weapon of  Gazebo. It is unlocked by not killing any chicken enemies and waiting for one minute in the starting area of The Coop.
Its evolution is  Embrace of Gaea, which requires  Parm Aegis.
## Effects
Upon triggering, Gaze of Gaea creates a teardrop-shaped damaging zone in the faced direction.
It has a 3% chance to defang enemies, which is affected by  Luck.
Gaze of Gaea has a 0.3 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.3 second by the same zone. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
Gaze of Gaea has 8 levels. At max level, Gaze of Gaea has +5 Base Damage, +30% Area, +2 to Amount, +0.4 seconds to Duration, and a 5% chance to defang enemies.

## Tips
- If the player is looking to unlock this weapon, they can either: select  Christine,  Gallo, or  Divano, go to The Coop, and click the Skip button when they are prompted with the level up screen, play as the  Fleaman [DLC] and avoid collecting  Experience Gem or play as  Ghost Lino [DLC]. This way, they can guarantee that they will not be able to deal damage to an incoming  Chickenfantry. Waiting in The Coop for one real-life minute will complete this unlock. The in-game timer will not count up until the Chickenfantry is defeated, but it does not matter for Gaze of Gaea's unlock.
## Trivia
- Gaze of Gaea represents the head of the  Avatar of Gaea [DLC], as it appears when the player spares the  Chickenfantry for a minute and grants this weapon as a boon. It also explains its innate chance of defanging enemies, as it is an inherently pacifistic act.

Listed weapons come with a counterpart.
Gemini (I) is one of the Arcanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by reaching level 50 while playing as  Pugnala Provola.
 Rinaldo Gandolfi [DLC] starts with this Arcana.
## Overview
While Gemini (I) is active, certain weapons are now accompanied by functionally identical counterparts and level up at the same time:
| Weapon | Counterpart of | Affected by Limit Break | Notes
| Base weapon | Evolution
| [A sprite icon representing Cygnus with no link] Cygnus | Peachone | Vandalier | Yes | Attacks slightly further outward than Peachone.
| [A sprite icon representing Zhar Ptytsia with no link] Zhar Ptytsia | Ebony Wings | Yes | Attacks slightly further outward than Ebony Wings.
| [A sprite icon representing Red Muscle with no link] Red Muscle | Phiera Der Tuphello | Phieraggi | Only with Phieraggi | It fires at a slightly different angle than Phiera Der Tuphello.
| [A sprite icon representing Twice Upon a Time with no link] Twice Upon a Time | Eight The Sparrow | It fires at a slightly different angle than Eight The Sparrow.
| [A sprite icon representing Flock Destroyer with no link] Flock Destroyer | Gatti Amari | Vicious Hunger | Yes | It spawns 3 different versions of cats.
| [A sprite icon representing Horse Cartridge with no link] Horse Cartridge | Ammo Appalate | Gunastrophe | No | It attacks behind the character.
| [A sprite icon representing Levelin'Eh with no link] Levelin'Eh | Santa Javelin | Seraphic Cry | No | It mirrors Santa Javelin, but replaces it when evolved into Seraphic Cry.
| [A sprite icon representing Silver Sliver with no link] Silver Sliver | Shadow Servant [DLC] | Ophion [DLC] | No | It spawns a silvery snake.
| [A sprite icon representing Party Pooper with no link] Party Pooper | Party Popper [DLC] | N/A | No | It attacks behind the character.
| [A sprite icon representing Silver Tongue with no link] Silver Tongue | Sharp Tongue [DLC] | Impostongue [DLC] | No | It attacks enemies behind the character.
| [A sprite icon representing Prism Damsel with no link] Prism Damsel | Prism Lass [DLC] | Time Warp [DLC] | No | It attacks behind the character, but replaces it when evolved into Time Warp.
| [A sprite icon representing Raging Fire with no link] Speculo Raging Fire | Raging Fire [DLC] | Salamender [DLC] | No | It mirrors Raging Fire and/or Salamender.
| [A sprite icon representing Ice Fang with no link] Speculo Ice Fang | Ice Fang [DLC] | Cocytus [DLC] | No | It mirrors Ice Fang and/or Cocytus.
| [A sprite icon representing Rock Riot with no link] Speculo Rock Riot | Rock Riot [DLC] | Gemma Torpor [DLC] | No | It mirrors Rock Riot and/or Gemma Torpor.
| [A sprite icon representing Gale Force with no link] Speculo Gale Force | Gale Force [DLC] | Pneuma Tempestas [DLC] | No | It is point symmetry to Gale Force and/or Pneuma Tempestas.
| [A sprite icon representing Fulgur with no link] Speculo Fulgur | Fulgur [DLC] | Tenebris Tonitrus [DLC] | No | It mirrors Fulgur, while duplicating Tenebris Tonitrus.
| [A sprite icon representing Keremet Bubbles with no link] Speculo Keremet Bubbles | Keremet Bubbles [DLC] | Keremet Morbus [DLC] | No | It is controlled oppositely by the character's movement, mirroring Keremet Bubbles and/or Keremet Morbus.
| [A sprite icon representing Refectio with no link] Speculo Refectio | Refectio [DLC] | Sanctuary [DLC] | No | Will create a moving Refectio, matching the player's movement at double the speed.
| [A sprite icon representing Hex with no link] Speculo Hex | Hex [DLC] | Nightmare [DLC] | No | It mirrors Hex and/or Nightmare.
| [A sprite icon representing Globus with no link] Speculo Globus | Globus [DLC] | Nitesco [DLC] | No | It fires behind the character.
| [A sprite icon representing Anura with no link] Speculo Anura | Anura [DLC] | Dark Frogamorphosis [DLC] | No | Creates a magic circle below the character, which summons purple frogs after fully charged.
The above counterparts do not take up weapon slots or show in the weapons list in the upper-left corner, cannot be evolved or united, and remain as independent weapons if their counterparts unite. If the Arcana is picked up with  Phieraggi,  Vicious Hunger,  Seraphic Cry,  Ophion,  Impostongue, and  Time Warp, the counterparts of their constituents are given at max level; with  Vandalier, both are given at the level of it and level up with Vandalier.
 Nduja Fritta Tanto and  Sorbetto create another stream of flame or frost from the back side of the character.
Only  Peachone,  Ebony Wings,  Vandalier, Phieraggi,  Gatti Amari, and Vicious Hunger can transfer their Limit Broken bonuses to their counterparts.
 Cygnus and  Zhar Ptytsia do not benefit from  Twilight Requiem (II), Cygnus benefits from  Jail of Crystal (XIV) and Zhar Ptytsia from  Heart of Fire (XIX).
 Prism Damsel [DLC] benefits from Jail of Crystal (XIV).
Unlike most of the evolved weapons, Vicious Hunger attacks with both its unevolved form Gatti Amari and  Flock Destroyer, instead of just the counterpart.
Weapons counterparts from  Belnades' Spellbook [DLC] gain the evolved weapon effects when the evolved spellbook is obtained. Skipping the base weapon (either from it being a starting weapon or through  Super Candybox II Turbo) will only give the player a copy of the evolved weapon.
Speculo Globus will still function the same if the player obtains  Nitesco [DLC] before obtaining Globus.
## Tips
- Since most of the counterparts cannot be evolved, their total average damage eventually becomes underwhelming compared to the evolved weapons, especially the  Phieraggi, which may make this Arcana a weak choice at high Curse levels.
- Gatti Amari is extremely strong for an unevolved weapon. Despite  Vicious Hunger gaining two Gatti Amaris with this Arcana, it competes with them by transmuting pickups like  Floor Chicken into  Gold Coin, hindering the growth of the cats. This is especially true for characters with high  Amount.
- Hidden weapons from character can also get their counterparts.
- Having multiple copies of certain weapon and Gemini (I) will only provide 1 counterpart. (For example,  Megalo Impostor Rina will only get 1 Silver Tongue.)
## Trivia
- The name of this Arcana is a reference to the song "Aquarius", which is the theme song for the Sunken City in Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse.
- The use of the Gemini zodiac in place of Aquarius also alludes to its ability to give counterparts.
- Gemini (I) can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "ilbagatto", which means "the magician" in Italian.
- This makes Gemini (I) a representation of The Magician Major Arcana card, symbolizing energy, talent, creativity, resourcefulness, the pursuit of one's desires, and the meeting of the physical and spiritual world.
- This is reflected in its ability to make counterparts of the player's weapons.
- The picture depicted in Gemini (I) is a reference to the Rubin vase, an optical illusion or ambiguous image created by Danish psychologist Edgar Rubin.
- Zhar Ptytsia is a reference to the Firebird of Slavic folklore.
- Cygnus is the name of the genus of swans and might be a reference to the constellation of the same name.
- Red Muscle, counterpart of Phiera Der Tuphello, is a reference to the song "Muscolo Rosso" by Hungarian-Italian singer Ilona Staller.
- Levelin'Eh is a reference to italian TV show host Ezio Greggio from "Striscia la notizia" calling out "Le veline!".
- "Speculo" is Latin for "Mirror".
- Most of the weapons that benefit from this Arcana are either ones that summon animals or spellbooks from Castlevania.

Gemma Torpor is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Rock Riot, requiring Max level  Stone Mask. Evolving it keeps Gemma Torpor as a hidden weapon.
It is the starting weapon of  Witch Actrise.
## Effects
Gemma Torpor summons a light green magic circle at a fixed location at the top of the screen in front of the player's character faced direction. Once activated, it drops large crystal projectiles from the top of the screen to the bottom of the screen. Enemies defeated have a chance to turn into jewels.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Obtains a counterpart of Gemma Torpor that mirrors it.
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Gemma Torpor bounces up to 3 times when hitting enemies.

# Gifts
Gifts are a type of item in Vampire Survivors. Typically, Gifts do not occupy weapon or passive weapon slots. Most Gifts are obtained via evolution, but  Pearl magatama [DLC] and  Velvet Dodecahedron [DLC] are obtained via level up or and  Arma Dio, instead.
Currently, there are 6 items classified as Gifts:
## From Evolution
| Condition(s) | | Source | | Gift
| Victory Sword | + | Max level: Torrona's Box | + | Treasure Chest | = | Sole Solution
| Candybox | | Treasure Chests must be able to grant Big Coin Bags | + | Treasure Chest | = | Super Candybox II Turbo
| Alucard Swords [DLC] | + | 6 passives (at max level) + 5 other evolutions (at max level) | + | Treasure Chest | = | Alucard Shield [DLC]
| Vol Luminatio [DLC] Vol Umbra [DLC] | | Vol Luminatio and Vol Umbra both must be at max level | + | Treasure Chest | = | Universitas [DLC]
## Passive Weapons
Aside from evolution, 2 passive weapons are considered Gifts: 
-  Pearl magatama [DLC]
-  Velvet Dodecahedron [DLC]
The above passives are always able to appear in level ups once unlocked, even if the player has maxed out their slots. While rare, these passive weapons can also appear in place of Limit Break levels.
Alternatively, once unlocked, these passives can be chosen in an  Arma Dio.
While there are other special passive weapons as part of other expansions, none are officially considered Gifts, even if they do not occupy slots, such as  Outer Saboteur [DLC].

The Glaive is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Lita Caryx. It is dropped by  Earth Dragon in Witchdom Pulchra (North-East world) in Emerald Diorama. It is unlocked by evolving it.
Its Evolution is the  Feather Spear, which requires the Divine Lancer tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Glaive summons glaives in the the faced direction. Can glimmer the "Divine Lancer" tech, which summons a single massive glaive in the faced direction.
Ignores Duration.

Glass Fandango is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  She-Moon Eeta. It is unlocked by getting it to level 7.
Its evolution is  Celestial Voulge, which requires  Wings at max level.
## Effect
Glass Fandango has two attack patterns which involve firing a short-ranged translucent blue blade: While moving, it attacks in the faced direction; while standing still, it will have the standard attack speed delay and attack in six directions around the character.
 Move Speed increases its overall fire rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.
It gains 2.5 times  Area during the time-freeze triggered by  Orologion. It deals triple damage to frozen enemies.
## Levels
Glass Fandango has 8 levels. At max level, Glass Fandango has +10 Base Damage, +30% Area, and +4 Amount.

## Tips
- Glass Fandango synergizes well with  Crystal Cries (XII) as it can deal extra damage to frozen enemies.
## Trivia
- Glass Fandango is the first weapon that is introduced along with a new map, with it being available to be picked up in the map itself.
- The unused spirit existed in the spritesheet since the very beginning with the name "Ice Spear" (current sprite is named "SpearIce" and the weapon's codename is ICELANCE). It got the current visual from Patch 1.6.0, the game engine update, and was released in the next content update. Its legacy is likely why it is the first new base game weapon after Version 1.0 that is not the evolution of bouncey weapons ( Anima of Mortaccio and  Yatta Daikarin).

Globus is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Saint Germain. It is unlocked by defeating 5,000 enemies with  Saint Germain.
It can be evolved into  Nitesco with Max level  Empty Tome. Evolving it also unlock  Julia Laforeze as a playable Character.
It can be selected when using the  Ebony Diabologue.
## Effects
Globus fires two purple ball projectiles that travel in diagonal directions, bouncing and damaging enemies they touch. Amount affects their Duration instead.

Godai Shuffle is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Four Seasons, requiring  Candelabrador at max level.
## Effects
Godai Shuffle makes a bunch of beads orbiting around the character far away. It causes five explosions instead of four, with rocks, bamboo leaves, fire, water crystal, and ball of air with a horizontal lightning; with the character 地 (earth), 風 (wind), 火 (fire), 水 (water), and 空 (void); in the top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right corner, and on the character respectively in that order.
Godai Shuffle gains more Base Damage and a lot more  Amount, which both increase Godai Shuffle's overall damage.
 Area causes the explosion to be bigger but not further away.  Amount and  Duration affect damage of Godai Shuffle instead; with the base damage formula (weapon's damage + Duration in seconds) x Amount.

## Trivia
- Godai (五大) refers to the Japanese translation of "panca-dhatavah," the five elements composing the universe in Indian philosophy. It is sometimes translated as Gorin (五輪). In the West, Godai became known through Miyamoto Musashi's "The Book of Five Rings (五輪書, Go Rin no Sho)," leading to the misconception that Godai originated in Japan.
- In the Japanese version of the game, further misunderstanding led to Godai Shuffle being translated as Gogyo Ranbu (五行乱舞). However, Gogyo is a term from Chinese philosophy, while Godai is from Indian philosophy; they are distinct concepts.

Gorgeous Moon is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Pentagram, and requires  Crown. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Venus Crescent [DLC], which also requires  Summon Spirit Tornado [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Similar to Pentagram, Gorgeous Moon erases enemies on the screen, but no longer destroys pickups. Instead, it generates additional experience. Gorgeous Moon Generation and Erasure phase always deal damage equal to the max health of the enemy. If it is lower than 660, the damage number is overwritten to display it between 655 and 665.
Gorgeous Moon's effect has three phases:
- Generation: This phase occurs 3 seconds after Cooldown. As the glyph of Gorgeous Moon appears on the ground, it pulses and chimes. It targets the closest enemies on the screen with a moon beam that can erase them, generating uniquely colored Experience Gems (orange, yellow, magenta) that yield 1 experience next to their usual gem drop. The attack frequency increases over time until the next phase.
- Attack frequency starts at 0.75 seconds for 8 beams, 0.375 seconds for 4 beams, and 0.2 seconds for 8 beams, for a total of 20 beams in 9.1 seconds.
- Erasure: This phase occurs 12.1 seconds after Cooldown. A waxing crescent symbol appears and shatters, erasing all enemies on the screen like Pentagram. This has a 0% chance of destroying items, and enemies erased also drop an extra Experience Gem.
- Vacuum: This phase occurs a brief moment after the previous phase. A waning crescent symbol mends from the shattered glyph and disappears, attracting all the gems on the level, identically to the Vacuum effect.
Gorgeous Moon can be affected by Cooldown bonuses, but there is a hardcoded limit of 15 seconds on how often Gorgeous Moon can trigger, which would make Gorgeous Moon active almost all of the time, going through its three phases.
Some enemies are completely unaffected by Gorgeous Moon.
Gorgeous Moon can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible Stalkers and Drowners in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, and The Bone Zone before minute 30, causing them to drop chests.

-  Blood Astronomia (XXI) - Allows Gorgeous Moon to place multiple instant kill zones on the ground.

## Tips
- Gorgeous Moon only benefits from  Cooldown.  Luck is obsolete as the chance stat of the weapon is already at 100% when evolved.
- Since Gorgeous Moon has a 0% chance of destroying Pickups, it is advised to evolve  Pentagram as soon as possible upon selecting it.
- Because some enemies, like  The Reaper or bosses at the 25th minute in most stages, are immune to Gorgeous Moon's effect, it cannot be relied on as your only tool of killing enemies.
- To reach Gorgeous Moon's 15 seconds cooldown limit, a Cooldown bonus of -75% is required.
- With  Game Killer (0), the vacuum effect can periodically collect all the  Experience Gems and hurl them at enemies. Since the damage of each gem is based of the experience amount, Gorgeous Moon needing  Crown to evolve increases the damage dealt by them, further increased by its Limit Break effect for gems generated by the moon beams.
- With Limit Break enabled Gorgeous Moon's  Amount can be leveled up. As with Pentagram and most other weapons when Gorgeous Moon is chosen to level up it will immediately be activated even if currently active. If Gorgeous Moon is the only weapon which can be upgraded through Limit Break, and  Growth is high enough, it can be caught in a self-perpetuating loop resulting in innumerable layered Gorgeous Moon attacks constantly firing. The only ways to break the loop once it's started are to avoid getting any experience and waiting for the game to catch up (  Game Killer (0) and/or  Stake to Your Heart (0) work) or for the character to die.
- The union of Gorgeous Moon and  Summon Spirit Tornado [DLC],  Venus Crescent [DLC], is not activated when levelled up by Limit Break so it cannot be chained like this. If it could it still has a maximum of +10 to  Amount from Limit Break so it could not chain infinitely.
## Trivia
- Gorgeous Moon bears some resemblance to, and may be inspired by the Moon Rune (which embodies destruction and compassion) from the Suikoden series.
- Gorgeous Moon most likely is a reference to the Sailor Moon series. The crescent symbol that appears on the ground strongly resembles one of the locket designs from the series. The chime sound effect during its Generation phase is reminiscent of the various sparkle sounds from the anime as well. The name references one of Sailor Moon's attacks, Moon Gorgeous Meditation.
- Its un-evolved form,  Pentagram, is the starting weapon of  Christine Davain, with her second sprite design and references being closely related to the Sailor Moon series.
- Its union,  Venus Crescent [DLC], references Sailor Venus's early signature attack, Venus Crescent Beam Smash, in the dub of the anime series. The large angel-like animation resembles the second sprite of Christine Davain with wings; in the anime a character gaining angel-like wings usually meant their power had grown exponentially.
- Gorgeous Moon's ID is a reference to the Power of Sire item in Castlevania: Symphony of The Night, which also deals screen-wide damage.
- Gorgeous Moon also serves as a counterpart to Pentagram, as the Eye of Ra is related to the Sun.
- Gorgeous Moon's Limit Break affected by base Amount was left out in patch 0.8.0 and was added back a few days later in a smaller patch.

 Grand Cross is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased and unlocked from the  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800. It is the starting weapon of  Tera [DLC].
Its union is  Arch Angle [DLC], which also requires  Heaven Sword.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
Grand Cross creates a light beam in the middle with wooden crosses that spiral across it in the middle of the screen and damage enemies it contacts.
Grand Cross has a 0.1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every tenth of a second by the same cross. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
It is the weapon version of the same effect from  Cross Crasher Tip [DLC].

Grand Cross has 8 levels. At max level, Grand Cross has +70 Base Damage, +3  Amount, and -18 seconds to  Cooldown.

Greatest Jubilee is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.0. It is unlocked by defeating  The Directer and watching the ending credits, however the player must obtain it during a run in a different map to unlock it in the Collection.
## Effects
Greatest Jubilee summons fireworks at the top half of the screen. The firework particles are attracted to the player, but the explosion hitbox is centered on where it originally explodes, expands in size instead of an instant Area-of-Effect, and can only hit the same enemy once. Until Greatest Jubilee's total  Amount reaches four, the first firework of each summon aims at the closest enemy, otherwise the firework explodes at the top half.
There is also a 1% chance to spawn four light sources around the player, affected by  Luck. The total amount of light sources on screen cannot exceed 10, with the old ones disappearing and being replaced by the newly summoned.
Upon reaching level 9, its finisher is also activated, causing a light show at the bottom of the screen which has a Base Damage of 15.
Only the light show is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 5% chance to occur. The chance and damage of the critical hits is affected by Luck.
Greatest Jubilee has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same light show. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Greatest Jubilee's light show's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
## Levels
Greatest Jubilee has 9 levels. At max level, Greatest Jubilee has +20 Base Damage, +50% Area, +4 Amount, -1.0 seconds of Cooldown, and a finisher effect.

## Tips
- Greatest Jubilee pairs up well with  Heart of Fire (XIX) since Greatest Jubilee causes more light sources to spawn around the character.
-  Hidden Anathema (III) pairs extremely well with Greatest Jubilee, as the light sources produced can generate  Floor Chicken, contributing an unlimited supply of stat bonuses that steadily ramps up in speed due to  Cooldown and  Luck bonuses.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) works particularly well when Greatest Jubilee is paired with Hidden Anathema, as it will allow Greatest Jubilee to further ramp up by increasing the  Speed stat.
- This weapon pairs well with  Penshin Fatcha, which transforms  Vacuum into Lavatrix Machina. Not only does Lavatrix Machina help collect the various pickups produced by Greatest Jubilee, but also, the spinning effect may be maintained potentially indefinitely, provided that the character's Cooldown and Luck are high enough that Jubilee generates Lavatrix Machinas faster than their effect can run out.
- Getting this weapon is highly recommended for  Secretino,  Jimbo [DLC],  Chicot [DLC],  Perkeo [DLC], and all other characters if  Survarocchi is enabled, as the light sources generated make it much easier to find  Survarots.
## Trivia
- The complete name "Greatest Jubilee" is a reference to the track "The Greatest Jubilee", the final boss theme of the 2009 action game Bayonetta.
- The damaging effect itself possibly references Jubilation Lee, aka "Jubilee", from the X-Men series. Her explosive energy blasts are often compared to fireworks. More prominently, Jubilee was featured in the 1992 X-Men: The Animated Series and the associated video games.
- Greatest Jubilee is one of the weapons that cannot be evolved along with  La Robba,  Party Popper [DLC],  Hats [DLC], and most item selectors (except  Candybox).

Gros Michel is a weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Chicot [DLC]. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its evolution is  Cavendish [DLC], which requires  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Gros Michel flings curving bananas in the faced direction, spreading out for each banana, which have a 1 in 6 chance to deal critical damage and explode. This chance is affected by  Luck.
Bananas that do not deal critical damage, and thus explode, have a chance to bounce once to a random enemy, speed up, reset its  Duration, and reroll the critical chance to deal critical damage and explode. Otherwise, the banana will simply disappear as its Duration expires.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Gros Michel's projectiles to bounce off enemies two more times.
-  Slash (XVI) - Gros Michel's critical hit multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Gros Michel has 9 levels. At max level, Gros Michel has +10 Base Damage, +60% Speed, +3 Amount, and -0.2 seconds of Cooldown.

## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the Gros Michel joker from Balatro.
- The effect, where it has a 1 in 6 chance to critically hit and explode in Vampire Survivors, is a reference to the effect of Gros Michel in Balatro, where it provides extra mult and has a 1 in 6 chance of going extinct after a played hand.
- The fact that Gros Michel evolves to the  Cavendish [DLC] is a reference to how the Cavendish becomes available after having an expired Gros Michel.

Guardian's Targe is a weapon from the Ode To Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Maria Renard. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 80,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Sacred Beasts Tower Shield with  Pummarola. Evolving it unlocks  Richter Belmont as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Once activated, Guardian's Targe summons a targe before the character horizontally. Whenever the targe touches an enemy or the character gets overhealed, it triggers a projectile that travels by a curve and damages all enemies it touches. This effect comes with a Hitbox Delay, which means the same enemies can only trigger this effect with a limited rate. It scales with all stat bonuses, and also benefits a lot from  Recovery and  Move Speed.

Gunastrophe is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the evolution of  Ammo Appalate, and requires  Bracer at max level.
## Effects
Gunastrophe spawns two bursts of a massive number of guns at the top corner of the screen where the character is facing which bounce around the screen.  Amount affects the number of bursts of guns per attack, base Amount from the weapon has no effect.
It is no longer affected by  Area, but can be affected by  Duration.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Horse Cartridge. It is functionally the same as Ammo Appalate at max level. It shoots bullets at the closest enemy away from where the character is facing.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Gunastrophe to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Gunastrophe's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.

Gungnir-Souris is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Trident [DLC], and requires  Duplicator at max level.
## Effects
Gungnir-Souris sends out a Gungnir ahead or slightly above and below in a V-shaped pattern, cycling between them in the faced direction. It only attacks to the left or the right of the character, never up, down, or diagonally. It gains significant amount of Base Damage and  Duration, more  Amount, and a slightly shorter  Cooldown.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which fire a beam of lightning, deal 2x damage, and have a 25% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Gungnir-Souris's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.

## Tips
- Because of how Gungnir-Souris attacks, it is challenging to play with in maps that require a lot of movement up and down, like Gallo Tower and Astral Stair.
## Trivia
- Gungnir-Souris is based on the Gungner from the Castlevania series. The icon is similar to the one from Dawn of Sorrow.
- The "-Souris" part of the weapon's name comes from the Chauve-souris, a weapon used by  Isaac [DLC] in Castlevania: Curse of Darkness.
- The codename TP_CHAUVE2 further reinforces this reference, and Chauve-souris requires a Trident to be created, similar to the evolution.
- On 15 November 2024, Gungnir-Souris was buffed to match max level  Trident [DLC] and increased critical hit chance by 10%.
- On 28 October 2025, Gungnir-Souris was buffed again for the same reason. In addition, it gets +20 Base Damage and -0.1 seconds to  Cooldown. Its critical chance is reduced by 15% but the critical damage multiplier is doubled. This update also removed the weapon's secondary damage which is twice the Base Damage, the critical lightning likely used it as it was one of the first weapons that triggers extra effects on critical hits and may have caused complications. Overall, the effect of losing secondary damage and the new critical damage multiplier cancel out; the extra Base Damage and shorter Cooldown compensate for the loss of critical chance, making it 6.7% stronger.

Hats is a weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Horse. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Horse is unlocked. It can also be obtained from  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000.
 Mini Horse will be added to the pool of available items upon leveling up as soon as the weapon reaches max level. Unlike other Emergency Meeting weapons, Mini Horse is not used to evolve Hats.
## Effects
Hats summons a pile of random hats on the character's head. Each hat projectile is then thrown at the closest enemy, randomly, and at the faced direction, cycling between the three options, getting slightly faster for each hat in a stack. The hat bounces onto other enemies or off the screen up to 2 times. When the pile of hats is depleted, a new pile appears. There can be a stack of at most 10 hats.
Hats are randomly assigned a hidden hat type which could have a special property:
- Bowler Hat deals max knockback of the enemy or a max of 10, whichever is lower.
- Pickle Haube (pickelhaube) always freeze enemies and last longer with  Duration.
- Baseball Cap increases bounce by 2.
- Top Hat has an acceleration 2.5 times that of the other hats after bouncing. The final hat of a stack will always be one because of the pun.
- Other hats that do not have special abilities are Fez, Cap, Hard Hat, and Normal.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows the hats to bounce off enemies up to three more times.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of cycling between 3 different modes, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Hats has 8 levels. At max level, Hats has +15 Base Damage, +30% Area, +50% Speed, +3 Amount, and +1.2 second of Duration.

Listed weapon projectiles explode on impact. Light sources explode. Character explodes when damaged.
Heart of Fire (XIX) is one of the Arcanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by reaching level 50 while playing as  Arca Ladonna.
 Avatar Infernas and  Julius Belmont [DLC] start with this Arcana.
## Overview
While Heart of Fire (XIX) is active, the projectiles from the following weapons create an explosion on impact, dealing 50% of base damage (weapons that already have an explosive effect will gain +50% explosive damage instead):
-  Fire Wand,  Hellfire,  Aura Blast [DLC] and  Kardía Phlegeton [DLC]
-  Valkyrie Turner,  Svarog Statue [DLC] and  Darkness Illusion [DLC]
-  Phiera Der Tuphello and  Red Muscle
-  Zhar Ptytsia
-  Tri-Bracelet and  Lapiste Tepisto [DLC]
-  Flames of Misspell and  Ashes of Muspell
-  FireFall [DLC],  FireBall [DLC],  FireWall [DLC] and  FireStall [DLC]
-  Ammo Appalate,  Horse Cartridge, and  Gunastrophe
-  Prismatic Missile [DLC] and  Luminaire [DLC]
-  Long Gun [DLC] and  Prototype A [DLC]
-  Short Gun [DLC] and  Prototype B [DLC]
-  Spread Shot [DLC] and  Prototype C [DLC]
-  Firearm [DLC] and  Fire-L3GS [DLC]
-  Homing Miss [DLC] and  Multistage Missiles [DLC]
-  Vanitas Whip [DLC] and  Aurablaster Tip [DLC]
-  Raging Fire [DLC],  Speculo Raging Fire [DLC], and  Salamender [DLC]
-  Hand Grenade [DLC] and  The RPG [DLC]
-  Dies Irae [DLC]
-  Punch [DLC],  Pressure Point [DLC] and  Gilded Hand [DLC]
-  Saber Machine Gun [DLC],  Hecaton Machine Gun [DLC] and  Divergence [DLC]
-  Super Missile [DLC],  Hydra Cannon [DLC] and  Hyperion Bazooka [DLC]
-  Spirit Rings [DLC] and  Rings of Calamity [DLC]
The damage caused by these explosions is counted as retaliatory damage, allowing  Armor to increase the damage of the explosions by +10% per point, and also allowing the explosions to increase the player's  Max Health when they defeat enemies if  Divine Bloodline (IX) is active.
- Note that the explosions caused by weapons are not the same as those triggered by receiving damage or destroying a light source, and thus have different sources of base damage.
Heart of Fire (XIX) also causes light sources to explode when destroyed and summons a retaliatory explosion when the player is damaged. When retaliating, it creates an explosion around the character and can retaliate every 0.5 seconds.
If none of the listed weapons are present, the explosion from destroying light sources and the retaliatory explosion deals the default base damage of 10. These explosions are affected by  Might and  Area
The base damage of Heart of Fire (XIX)'s retaliatory explosions will increase by 5 for every listed weapon held, starting from the second weapon.
Additionally, the drop weight of  Nduja Fritta Tantos will be multiplied by 4, making them drop considerably more often from light sources and  Hail from the Future (X).
## Tips
- Weapons that have low or no piercing, like the Fire Wand or Long Gun, benefit from this Arcana massively, as it allows them to deal area damage and multiplies their crowd damage output.
- Since the explosion happens per enemy contact, weapons with infinite pierce like Hellfire and Valkyrie Turner (and Gunastrophe) become even more powerful as they shred through enemies while also creating an explosion with each hit. The sheer amount of bullets and later pierce from Phiera Der Tuphello can also create a huge amount of explosions.
- Only the base damage of the weapon is used for the calculation of the explosion damage so Valkyrie Turner's charge up does not affect it.
- Light source and retaliatory explosions deal double damage for Phiera Der Tuphello as it starts with a base damage of 5, this bonus will be overridden by other weapons.
- With  Heir of Fate (XIX), explosions will make defeated enemies drop Scorched Souls that grant  Max Health and  Might when collected.
- All explosions are boosted by  Dario Bossi's ability, making this a highly valuable arcana when setting up a build with him.
## Trivia
- The name of this Arcana is a reference to the song "Heart of Fire", which is not only the theme of Stage 5 of Castlevania, but is also Julius Belmont's theme in Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow.
- Heart of Fire (XIX) can be unlocked in  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "ilsole", which means "the sun" in Italian.
- This makes Heart of Fire (XIX) a representation of The Sun Major Arcana card, symbolizing joy, satisfaction, vitality, radiance, success, optimism, and good health.
- This is reflected in a more literal interpretation of its ability to benefit fire weapons and create explosions from the player and light sources when hit.
- The explosion is also used by the  Gatti Amari when a cat uses a  Nduja Fritta Tanto, and it will explode at the item's location and despawn the cat that used it.
- The explosion as a standalone weapon creates an explosion at the player character similar to the retaliatory explosion. It can also be affected by  Amount and  Cooldown, which is not the case when it is an Arcana effect or other instances when it is used as they always explode only once.

Heaven Sword is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Cross, and requires  Clover. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Gains Boros.
Its union is  Arch Angle [DLC], which also requires  Grand Cross [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Heaven Sword throws a giant sword projectile at the closest enemy, which then starts spinning and boomerangs in the opposite direction it was thrown until it leaves the screen. Its  Speed is doubled and damage more than doubles. It gains an extreme amount of knockback to push enemies back to compensate for the  Amount and Pool Limit loss, and  Cooldown increase.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2.5x damage and have 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Heaven Sword's critical hit multiplier is doubled from 2.5x to 5x.
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows the Heaven Sword's projectiles to bounce off the edges of the screen twice. Upon bouncing, the sword completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them.

## Tips
- Heaven Sword can deal critical damage by default. The more  Luck the player has, the more likely they are to deal critical hits.
- Heaven Sword travels much further when initially thrown than Cross, regularly being tossed offscreen only to come flying back. It is still the most effective when there are a lot of enemies, to ensure it pierces through as many enemies on the return trip as possible.
- The automatic targeting nature of the weapon is both a blessing and a curse. While it removes the mental load of aiming, the closest enemy might not always be the enemy the player is trying to attack.
- Its Speed is much greater than Cross, meaning that  Bracer and the  Speed PowerUp will amplify it greatly. This is not necessarily beneficial if the intent is to have these projectiles stay on screen as long as possible.
## Trivia
- Heaven Sword is a reference to Heaven's Sword from the Castlevania series. The attack of Heaven's Sword is also boomerang-like. The special attack from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night even has the character summon multiple swords in an arc behind them that target enemies in the front.

The Hecaton Machine Gun is an evolved weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Saber Machine Gun.
Its Evolution is the  Divergence, which requires the Bombarding Fire tech. Fully evolving it unlocks  Eagle Gun starting weapon and solo skin for  Formina Franklyn.
## Effects
Hecaton Machine Gun fires a barrage of bullets rapidly in the faced direction. Bullets have limited duration and can pierce through enemies.
Can glimmer the "Bombarding Fire" tech.
Works best with Speed and Duration, which makes bullets reach further.
## Arcanas
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

Hellfire is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Fire Wand, and requires  Spinach. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Kardía Phlegeton [DLC], which also requires  Aura Blast [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Hellfire shoots large flaming meteors at nearby enemies that move slowly in a given direction and Pierce infinitely.
Hellfire gets an even higher Base Damage, but with slower Projectile Speed and reduced Amount and Pool Limit. Its Interval is increased substantially, spacing out the meteors much more. The meteors can now also pass through walls.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows the Hellfire's projectiles to bounce off the edges of the screen once. Upon bouncing, the projectiles completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them according to the edge.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows the Hellfire's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies, that it kills, drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
