## Tips
- Hellfire typically does a very large amount of damage, considering both its Base Damage and Spinach levels. Combined with its slow moving meteors, it can easily accrue millions of damage dealt in over the course of a run even with the base Amount decrease.
- Hellfire benefits greatly from Area bonuses because of the already large size of the meteors. Cooldown is another important stat for effective use, as the base Cooldown of the weapon is quite slow. Amount may not be the most beneficial with the small Pool Limit. Unlike the Fire Wand, Projectile Speed may not be beneficial if the player wants the meteors to stay on screen as long as possible.
- Since the meteors are still aimed randomly, they are not a reliable source of damage. It is better to use Hellfire as a supplemental weapon rather than a main damage dealer, or at least to have a weapon you can direct damage with in case it is uncooperative.
## Trivia
- Hellfire may be a reference to the Hellfire spell from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night.

Hex is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Elizabeth Bartley. It is unlocked by evolving it. Once  Serpent Gate is unlocked, it can be dropped by the Mummy boss located near the east exit of the Maze.
Its Evolution is  Nightmare, which requires the  Skull O'Maniac at max level.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effects
Being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Hex has a charge time before activation, which is indicated by the brightness of its created magic circle.
Hex summons a purple magic circle a fixed distance away from the character's faced direction. When fully charged, it summons a skull that damages enemies in its immediate area. It then fires, in bursts, multiple wavy horizontally-moving runic projectiles from its mouth that damage enemies they touch.  Curse further multiplies its damage.  Amount affects how many bursts it fires before disappearing.
Hex has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same projectile. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates a counterpart -  Speculo Hex. It levels up as Hex does and benefits from Limit Breaking. Speculo Hex mirrors its counterpart.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Hex's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on Curse.
## Levels
Nightmare has 8 levels. At max level, it gains +15 Base Damage, -1.5 seconds of Cooldown, +20% Speed, +20% Area, +1 second of Duration, and +3 Amount.

Holy Wand is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Magic Wand, and requires  Empty Tome. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Leda.
Its union is  Spirit of Light [DLC], which also requires  Summon Spirit [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Holy Wand fires non-piercing blue magic bolts at nearby enemies, and has half the  Cooldown and double the  Projectile Speed of its base form. Additional projectiles from  Amount will be fired in a sequence. The projectiles cannot pass through walls.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Gives Holy Wand's projectiles the capability to to bounce off of enemies up to three times.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by Holy Wand's projectiles will explode.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives Holy Wand a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by Holy Wand's projectiles will drop Crystallized Souls when killed.

## Tips
- Even if the sequence lasts longer than the  Cooldown, it does not prevent another volley to start shooting. Pool Limit is the only reason there is not more projectiles on screen.  Projectile Speed increase can make less projectiles stay on screen.
- The automatic targeting nature of the weapon is both a blessing and a curse. While it removes the mental load of aiming, the closest enemy might not always be the enemy the player is trying to attack. It should be considered a supporting weapon, and not necessarily a main damage dealer.
- If Holy Wand is targeting a further enemy and the player would like to it to target a closer one, they can wiggle a bit by doing small movements to update the target of the weapon.
- Holy Wand is one of the best options for single-target damage and keeping enemies at bay in the whole game because of its high  Amount and low Cooldown. However, its damage against multiple enemies is lacking even with the extra pierce,  Jail of Crystal (XIV) is recommended to increase the amount of enemies it can hit.

Homing Miss is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Stanley [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Stanley.
Its evolution is  Multistage Missiles [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Duplicator.
## Effects
Homing Miss fires multiple homing missiles in the faced direction. These missiles home in on a random enemy and explode on hit (or when their pierce runs out, on later levels), switching targets when the initial target dies.

Hydro Pump Climax is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Hydro Storm [DLC] at max level and  La Borra.
## Effects
Hydro Pump Climax starts a rain that damages all enemies on screen in waves, which also rains down bottles of holy water from the sky. They break upon impact with the ground, leaving puddles of water and blue flames that damage enemies. The bottles are dropped randomly. These puddles start in wildly different sizes, slowly creep towards the player, increase in size as they travel, and have a maximum size limit.
The rain has double the Base Damage, with it being multiplied by 2 again for the puddles specifically to match the Base Damage of La Borra. The rain loses  Duration and the puddles lose even more. Hitbox Delay uses the one from La Borra, which cuts more than half of the Hitbox Delay from the rain.
 Area,  Amount,  Cooldown, Interval, and Pool Limit uses ones from Hydro Storm, some of which heavily disaventages the puddles, but they are mostly circumvented by other means:
- Area appears to be greatly diminished for the puddles, but they are so randomized that, on average, they are bigger than La Borra's.
- Amount is lowered to one as the rain does not scale with it. However, each rain drops (calculatedAmount+9)*playerDuration bottles, exceeding the original Amount by a lot.
- Cooldown got 2.5 times longer for the puddles but the extra bottle Amount more than makes up for it.
- Interval is not that different between the two components, the bottles are dropped evenly within the full duration of the rain.
- Pool Limit would have been a benefit to the puddles as it is higher than La Borra's. Instead, it is limited to 100 for the puddles, the same as La Borra.
Duration makes rain last longer and  Speed divides its Hitbox Delay, then Duration divides by Hitbox Delay to determine how many waves of damage in one rain, rounded to an integer. Despite the shorter Duration, because it has a much shorter Hitbox Delay, it spawns five waves of damage without bonuses, two more than maxed Hydro Storm. Note that Speed dividing Hitbox Delay is only used to determine the number of damage waves and does not shorten it, so it does not benefit the puddles.
The puddles' speed and growth rate are based on multiple factors:
- With Speed and  Move Speed, the puddles move and grow faster. Both increase the growth rate by the same amount but Movement Speed increases the move speed of the puddles slightly more.
- If Hydro Pump Climax does not receive any Speed bonuses, the puddles still travel slowly but they do not grow larger.
- Negative Projectile Speed shrinks the puddles and makes it move away from the player, it may even grow once again after it shrinks to a single point.
- Movement Speed has a minimum cap on the base value. It does not shrink the pool, make them slower, or reverse direction, but can still counteract the speed and growth rate from a higher Projectile Speed.
- Duration slows down the growth rate of the puddle but not the speed, making them reach the max size when it ends. This stops an infinitely growing pool from lasting very long and covering the entire screen even when the character is moving.
- Duration being less than 100% causes it to grow faster. It being less than or equal to 0% ends the puddle immediately.
Hydro Pump Climax has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half a second by the same puddle or rain. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Hydro Pump Climax's  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Puddles aim at the nearest enemy instead of shooting randomly, will pool under them instead of under the player, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

## Trivia
- Hydro Pump Climax continues the crude joke that  La Borra has taken on the meaning of "semen" in Italian. Although "climax" can be taken as the peak form of  Santa Water, it is most likely referencing the vulgar meaning of the word "ejaculation", especially paired with "pump".
- "Hydro Pump" is a move from Pokémon.
- In the trailer for Ode to Castlevania, it shows that Hydro Pump Climax would have rain down Santa Waters, La Borras,  Hydro Storms [DLC],  Sorceress' Tears, and themselves when attacking. When it is released, it only rains down itself, but remnants of this feature still exist in the code and can be toggled on.
- Despite being bottles,  Apoplexy and  Antidote is not on the list.

Hydro Storm is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Atlantis Shrine Wizard, and can be purchased and unlocked from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Hydro Pump Climax [DLC], which also requires  La Borra.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effect
Hydro Storm starts a rain that damages all enemies on screen in waves.
 Duration makes rain last longer and  Speed divides its Hitbox Delay, then Duration divides by Hitbox Delay to determine how many waves of damage in one rain, rounded to an integer. Without bonuses, it spawns one wave of damage at Level 1 and three at max.
Hydro Storm has a 1.21 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1.21 seconds by the same rain. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
It is the weapon version of the same effect from  Hydrostormer Tip [DLC].
## Levels
Hydro Storm has 8 levels. At max level, Hydro Storm has +7 Base Damage, +50% Speed, and +1.5 seconds of Duration.

| Level 1 | Generates damaging waves based on Projectile Speed and Duration.

| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 1.

The Hydrostormer Tip is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the Evolution of the  Dragon Water Whip, requiring the  Attractorb.
## Effects
The Hydrostormer Tip adds an additional effect on top of its base weapon; every 13th activation triggers a hidden  Hydro Storm, a screen-filling sparkle of holy rain that harms all enemies which damage is affected by Speed and Duration and ignores Amount.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - The Hydrostormer Tip's whip attacks and dragon projectile have a 10% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by Luck. The hidden Hydro Storm is unaffected.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Hydrostormer Tip to critically hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.

## Tips
- The hidden Hydro Storm is better suited as a defensive attack a defensive item, effectively slowing down enemies with ticking damage and preventing them from approaching the character faster.
## Trivia
- The ability this tip provides is in reference to the Hydro Storm item crash from Castlevania: Rondo Of Blood and Dracula X. Richter activates this item crash by holding the Holy Water subweapon.

Ice Fang is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Sypha Belnades. Ice Fang can be dropped from Brachyura in the stairwell area of the Ode to Castlevania stage. It is unlocked by evolving it.
It can be evolved into  Cocytus with Max level  Spellbinder.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effects
Being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Ice Fang has a charge time before activation, which is indicated by the brightness of its created magic circle.
Ice Fang summons a blue magic circle in the character's horizontally-faced direction, When fully charged, it stops in place and summons two parallel sets of blue magical circles perpendicular to itself. These circles then summon teeth-like icicles (affected by Amount/Duration/Area) that bite down and pierce enemies within its area.

Icebrand is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Ninth Circle [DLC], which also requires  Unholy Vespers.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
It is the starting weapon of  Frozenshade [DLC].
## Effects
Icebrand summons snowflakes around the character that form into icicles, they point in a direction and fire after a delay, rotating 30 degrees counterclockwise after each activation similar to  Clock Lancet.  Duration extends how long the icicles are stationary before firing and they have a chance to freeze enemies.
Icebrand has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same icicle. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
Icebrand has a 5% chance to freeze enemies.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Increases the chance to freeze enemies from 5% to 35%. This chance is affected by  Luck.

Impostongue is an evolved weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Sharp Tongue, requiring  Mini Impostor at max level.
## Effects
Impostongue fires seeking pink tongues in lines from the character to stab at nearby enemies in front of them, some are fired as red tongues which can aim at anywhere on screen. It periodically blasts a red flash at the strongest on-screen enemy and all other enemies in a horizontal area centered on the original target with high damage. The damage of this weapon is multiplied by (1 + Recovery).
Impostongue gains a bit of Base Damage and Projectile Speed, while having a lower Cooldown and Interval.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 4x damage and have 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - creates a counterpart,  Silver Tongue, that is functionally the same as Sharp Tongue. It fires silver and more curvy tongues which prioritizes enemies behind the character but does not benefit from Limit Breaking.
-  Slash (XVI) - doubles the damage of Impostongue critical hits, causing it to deal 8x damage.

## Tips
- It is best to combine Impostongue into builds that utilize Pummarola and Metaglio Left as they increase the Recovery stat.
- Due to gaining +1 Recovery per level, Cosmo is able to quickly turn Impostongue into a powerful weapon. By level 30 Impostongue will deal 1,700+ damage per hit when factoring in the Recovery, Might, and Omni Powerups.
## Trivia
- Impostongue is based on the background of the death animation in Among Us, where a red, flame-like flash appear from left to right as the death occurs from the point of view of the victim. It is also way the enemies targeted by it receives a lethal amount of damage as it only takes one attack from the Impostor to kill a crewmate.

Incineration is a weapon from the Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Ashtart.
Its evolution is  Dust to Dust, which requires max level  Candelabrador.
## Effects
Incineration will occaisionally spawn a magic circle in the player's faced direction. After one second has elapsed, Incineration will release a wave of ash that is guaranteed to instantly defeat any enemy it passes through if they do not possess instant kill resistance. If an enemy does possess instant kill resistance, then they will instead take normal damage.
 Area will increase the size of the wave of ash and how far it travels before expiring.
Incineration deals  Hell damage.
- Currently, it is bugged to not display the "HELL" tag when playing as  Baal'Thasar [DLC] or  Baal'Thamut [DLC].
Incineration has a 0.05 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.05 seconds by the same wave of ash. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

Infernolatro is a weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Jimbo [DLC]. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its evolution is  NaneInferno [DLC], which requires  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Infernolatro creates a zone of flames in the faced direction, and it gets increased Base Damage,  Area, and  Duration by killing more enemies by any means, resetting when the weapon's duration ends. A counter will show the number of enemies killed during that instance of the weapon. Only one flame zone can be triggered at the same time. The Base Damage increase follows the formula:
BaseDamage+0.5KillsWhileProjectileActive
KillsWhileProjectileActive≡total number of enemies killed during that instance of Infernolatro from any source
Infernolatro has a 1.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1.5 seconds by the same damage zone. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcana
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Damage zones deal extra contact damage, dealing half of the base damage in an area.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - Defeated enemies drop  Scorched Souls, giving bonus  Max Health and  Might.

## Tips
-  Curse and  Charm can help increase the scaling of this weapon by increasing the number of enemies spawned.
-  Skull O'Maniac,  Torrona's Box, and  Karoma's Mana all provide these stats.
- Infernolatro does not have to get kills to benefit from them. The player can take other weapons for safety.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the scoring system in Balatro, where if the player scores more than the goal score in a blind, the score on the left panel will display a fiery effect.
- Since this weapon is red, it is specifically a reference to mult from Balatro.
- It dealing more damage as more enemies are killed might be referencing that the fiery effect gets bigger and more intense as the score exceeds the goal more and more.

Infinite Corridor is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Clock Lancet, and requires  Silver Ring and  Gold Ring at max level.
It is the starting weapon of  Chaos [DLC].
## Effects
Infinite Corridor fires a white beam around the player in twelve directions clockwise one at a time. The beam does no damage, but will freeze any enemy it hits. After the freezing beam has completed one full rotation and it fires upwards in the 12 o'clock direction, it creates a spinning, shining rainbow aura around the player, halving the health of every enemy on screen.
Infinite Corridor can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible  Stalkers and  Drowners in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, and The Bone Zone before minute 30, causing them to drop  Treasure Chests.
## Arcanas
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Enemies frozen by Infinite Corridor will explode.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - Enemies frozen by Infinite Corridor will drop  Crystallized Souls when killed.

## Tips
- The freezing beam travels around the player like a clock, shooting out at "12 o'clock," then at "1 o'clock," and so on. This means the freezing beam only has 12 directions it can fire. This also makes the freezing beam very predictable.
- It is possible to keep freezing the same enemy multiple times. This is especially useful for bosses and  The Reaper.
- Frozen enemies cannot damage the player, so it is safe to touch them.
- Enemies become more vulnerable to freezing if the character has  Garlic or  Soul Eater.
- Thanks to its health-halving effect, the Infinite Corridor can help characters without a way to increase their Might to remain relevant on Endless and during high  Curse as stronger enemies start coming in.
- Infinite Corridor's health halving effect works on the Reaper, making quick work to lower their health to an amount that is viable to be killed by any character when combined with the  Laurel or the  Crimson Shroud.
- In fact, using this weapon against the Reaper is one of the only ways for it to drop  Golden Eggs (and summon the  White Hand), the other being the use of the Crimson Shroud.
- While using both weapons is ideal, you can kill the Reaper using Infinite Corridor alone without its counterpart, although this means any hit from the Reaper can still be fatal if one fails to consistently keep freezing it. The mirages from the  Mirage Robe or  J'Odore can serve as a backup way of keeping the Reaper away from the character.
- Infinite Corridor is also the easiest way to defeat  Sketamari in The Bone Zone, as it is vulnerable to its health halving effect and it helps counteract its constant healing.
## Trivia
- The name is a reference to the Infinite Corridor from Castlevania: Curse of Darkness. In the animated series, it is an alternate realm that gives access to many different lands separated from this world's space and time, which is referenced by the rainbow aura's codename "SPACETIME".

Insatiable is a weapon introduced in the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the hidden starting weapon of  Je-Ne-Viv, and it can also be obtained with any character after equipping  Victorian Horror (XVIII).
## Effects
Insatiable creates a black, skull-shaped forcefield centered slightly above the character, similar to  Blood Astronomia (XXI).
When given by Je-Ne-Viv, its damage is just multiplied by  Greed. And, like  Blood Astronomia (XXI), its zone's size is equal to  Magnet, not being affected by  Area.
However, if  Victorian Horror (XVIII) is in use, Insatiable's damage will also be multiplied by one tenth of the player's  Amount (when above +10 Amount) and the zone's size will also be affected by Area.

Intuition is a weapon selector from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Mr. S, and an optional starting weapon for  Ameya Aisling. It allows the player to select one of the Emerald Diorama weapons, which includes:

## Unlocking
Intuition is unlocked by fully evolving  Sanguine Star, which means evolving Sanguine Star and maxing its evolution ( Blood Chalice) out.

The Iron Ball is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  John Morris. It is unlocked by getting the Iron Ball to level 4.
Its Evolution is the  Wrecking Ball, which requires the  Armor. Evolving it and  Alucard Spear unlocks  Shanoa as playable character.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
The Iron Ball works similar with Axe, throwing iron balls above the character which drop downward. The primary difference is that these projectile, when falling to the the bottom, screen shake the ground tremendously and bounce off the bottom before disappearing. Iron Ball's damage is affected by Armor.
Another effect is that (possibly) if the player character receives damage from an enemy, that amount of damage is stored in an iron ball in retaliation.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Iron Ball's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of being thrown upwards, and gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Iron Shield is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Vincent Dorin. It is unlocked by dealing a total of 70,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Dark Iron Shield with  Parm Aegis. Evolving it unlocks  Mina Hakuba as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Upon triggering, Iron Shield summons a shield in front of the player. When touching an enemy, it fires multiple shield-shape projectiles that fan out in a conical pattern. After traveling a certain distance, the projectiles stop and spin in place, damaging any enemies they touch. It also trigger projectiles as Retaliate when taking damage while the shield is up, Amount for this weapon is doubled when triggered through retaliation.
## Arcanas
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Killing enemies with Iron Shield's retaliate attack increases  Max Health by 0.5.

## Notes
- If the character also holds  Guardian's Targe or  Sacred Beasts Tower Shield, Iron Shield will be summoned behind the character instead.

J'Odore is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Mirage Robe, requiring  Attractorb at max level.
## Effects
J'Odore shoots out mirages which look like the afterimage of the character and freeze enemies. Enemies may get confused by some mirages and chase it instead of the player.
J'Odore has more Base Damage,  Amount, can pierce through some enemies, higher chance to explode, and higher Pool Limit. It has a smaller  Area,  Duration is lowered, and a longer Interval.
 Area increases the size of the explosion.  Duration will add to the time enemies are frozen.  Speed and  Move Speed increases how fast the mirage move.
Depending on the  Luck stat, there is a chance for the mirage to explode.
While playing with a keyboard, the mirages are only able to be shot out in eight directions: the cardinal and ordinal directions. When playing with a mouse or gamepad, the mirages are able to be fired in any direction.
## Arcanas
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - allows the mirage to always create explosions when they hit enemies.
## Levels
With Limit Break, J'Odore can be further leveled up.

Javelin is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Jonathan Morris [DLC]. It is unlocked by getting it to level 3.
Its evolution is  Long Inus [DLC], which requires  Spellbinder.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
Javelin throws a javelin in the direction the character is facing horizontally. It flies in a fixed parabolic curve and can pierce enemies. Unlike most projectile weapons with low pierce, javelin has a limited  Duration.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Javelin's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Javelin has 8 level. At max level, it has +20 Base Damage, +3 Amount, and +8 Pierce.

- On 15 November 2024, Javelin was buffed. The base  Duration is increased by 0.25 seconds, while the Duration bonuses from leveling up were removed and replaced with Base Damage increases, and all +1 Pierce bonuses are increased to +2. In total, max level Javelin got 20 Base Damage, +3 Pierce, but -0.25 seconds of Duration.
- On 28 October 2025, Javelin was buffed again, increasing knockback by 3 and reducing  Cooldown by 1 second.

Jet Black Whip is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Christopher Belmont. It is unlocked by Surviving 14 minutes as Christopher.
It can be evolved into  Mormegil Tip with  Stone Mask. Evolving it unlocks  Simon Belmont as playable character.
As a magic whip, it can be picked from  Morning Star.
## Effects
The Jet Black Whip lingers on the ground for a few moments before attacking with a large, vertical wave of projectiles. The wave is affected by Amount and Area, but not Duration, and lingers based on the weapon's projectiles.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Projectiles explode when they expire.
-  Slash (XVI) - Enables deal critical damage.

The Jetstream is an evolved weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Khukuri.
## Effects
Critical hits may give temporary invulnerability. Can glimmer the "Kaleidoscope" tech, which creates kaleidoscopic damaging areas under enemies hit by the bouncing clones.
Jetstream summons a Shadow clone that strike nearby enemies. The clone's distance travelled is affected by the character's base Move Speed, unaffected by stat increases from weapons and passive items.
## Levels
The Jetstream has 8 levels. At max level, the Jetstream has +2.5 Base Damage, +75%  Area and -1.5 seconds of  Cooldown.

## Tips
- The invincibility granted by Jetstream protects from all sources of damage, making it incredibly powerful for survivability. With high  Luck and low  Cooldown, it can even be used to protect against  The Reaper in lieu of the  Crimson Shroud.
- Jetstream is an incredibly powerful weapon for any character with scaling  Luck, such as  Smith IV,  Cosmo Pavone and  Keitha Muort, as at high enough levels every hit will be a critical hit, leading to them being permanently invincible.
-  Stellar Blade and Jetstream form an incredibly powerful combo, as the invulnerability that Jetstream grants ensures that Stellar Blade will deal critical hits, without the need for the player to get damaged.

Just Vent is a weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Shapeshifter Nino. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Shapeshifter.
It can be evolved into  Unjust Ejection with  Mini Shapeshifter at max level. The passive item will be added to the pool of available items upon leveling up as soon as the weapon reaches level 2.
## Effects
Just Vent creates a vent underneath the character with a black circular aura as the trap zone. Normal enemies who entered are killed instantly upon entering the vent, while especially strong enemies and bosses take high damage instead. Once a set number of enemies based on Amount have fallen into the vent, the vent disappears and generates experience gems.
## Levels
Just Vent has 8 levels. At max level, Just Vent has +100% Area, +7 Amount, and -1 second of Cooldown.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | "Destroys or heavily damages enemies. Amount affects how many times it can trigger."
| Level 2 | Vent uses increased by 1.
| Level 3 | Base Area up by 50%.
| Level 4 | Vent uses increased by 2.
| Level 5 | Cooldown reduced by 1 seconds.
| Level 6 | Vent uses increased by 2.
| Level 7 | Base Area up by 50%.
| Level 8 | Vent uses increased by 2.

## Trivia
- Just Vent has the highest base damage of any weapon at 200.
- Just Vent is based on the mechanic of venting in Among Us, wherein the Imposter player can use the vent to teleport around the map, allowing them to sneak a quick kill and move away to create an alibi, or escape from the room with a sabotaged door.
- The vents acting like a trap to kill enemies and spiting out resources (experience gems) after they are at capacity is similar to Bloon Trap in Bloons TD 5 or Bloons TD 6.

Kaiser Knuckle is a weapon introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Morris Baldwin [DLC]. It can be purchased from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Lapiste Tepisto, which also requires  Tri-Bracelet.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Kaiser Knuckle rapidly throws close-ranged punches in the horizontally-faced direction.
 Amount acts similarly to  Duration, increasing how long punches are thrown.
Kaiser Knuckle has a 0.15 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.15 seconds by the same flurry of punches. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
Kaiser Knuckle has 8 levels. At max level, Kaiser Knuckle has +20 Base Damage, +3  Amount, +50%  Area, and -0.6 seconds of  Cooldown.

| Level 6 | Base Area up by 20%.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 8 | Base Area up by 10%. Cooldown reduced by 0.3 seconds.

Kardía Phlegeton is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Aura Blast [DLC] at max level and  Hellfire.
## Effects
Kardía Phlegeton creates a massive volcanic eruption at the player's location. This volcano deals damage to enemies upon contact and shoots out the same meteors as Hellfire. These meteors are fired chaotically and arc downwards, piercing enemies infinitely. These meteors also have their damage multiplied by 3, compared to Hellfire. The hitbox of the volcano will only cover the upper half of the screen.
Kardía Phlegeton has decreased  Area and a slower  Cooldown compared to Aura Blast. However, the effective Area is much higher.
Kardía Phlegeton has a hitbox delay of 0.5 seconds, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than twice every second by the same volcano. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Kardía Phlegeton's meteors to bounce on the edges of the screen 3 times.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Kardía Phlegeton's volcano and meteors to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing 1.5x their base damage in an area.
- Unlike Hellfire, which only does half of its base damage in an area, Kardía Phlegeton multiplies the damage of Heart of Fire by 3.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of randomly, and gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

## Trivia
- Kardía Phlegeton is a reference to Phlegeton, the Dual Crush of Charlotte Aulin from Castlevania: Harmony of Despair, while the animation is taken from Volcano, another Dual Crush from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin.
- "Kardía" is Greek which translates to "heart", and is a cognate of "cardia", commonly seen in medical terms for the heart; "Phlegeton" is a corruption of "Phlegethon", one of the five rivers in the infernal regions of the underworld in Greek mythology, its literal meaning is "flaming". Together, as Greek can use postpositive adjectives, the name can be translated as "Flaming Heart", or "Heart of Fire", its name is an elaborate play on the song "Heart of Fire".

Keremet Bubbles is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Rinaldo Gandolfi. It is unlocked by evolving it.
Keremet Bubbles can be obtained by killing  Keremet after activating his rune in the North West of the Ode to Castlevania Map.
Keremet Bubbles can be evolved into  Keremet Morbus with Max level  Armor.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effects
Being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Keremet Bubbles has a charge time before activation, which is indicated by the brightness of its created magic circle.
Keremet Bubbles summons a green magic circle behind the character at the center end of the screen, its angle can be controlled by the character's movement, starting at the left end of the screen and moving in the direction the character is moving until it reaches the right end of the screen. Once Charged, it fires green bubbles in waves that travel towards the character, damaging enemies they touch and continuing to travel until they eventually pop (affected by Duration).
Amount affects the number of bubbles per wave. Duration affects the number of waves and the distance the bubbles can travel before popping.

Keremet Morbus is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Keremet Bubbles, requiring Max level  Armor. Evolving it keeps Keremet Bubbles as a hidden weapon.
It is the starting weapon of  Keremet.
## Effects
Keremet Morbus fires fast, homing projectiles that chase down and pierce through enemies. The green magic circle is controlled just like Keremet Bubbles.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - creates a counterpart - Speculo Keremet Bubbles, which affects hidden Keremet Bubbles only.
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Keremet Morbus' Cooldown while moving.

The Khukuri is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Macha Alter Ego and  Kugutsu "Komachi" skin. It is dropped by  Iron Maiden in Avalon (South-West world) in Emerald Diorama.
Its Evolution is the  Jetstream, which requires the  Parm Aegis and Moonfall Slash tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Khukuri summons a Shadow clone that strikes nearby enemies. The clone's distance travelled is affected by the character's base Move Speed, unaffected by stat increases from weapons and passive items.
Can glimmer the "Moonfall Slash" tech, which creates a moving shadow clone that explodes every time it hits an enemy

The Kick is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the second optional starting weapon of  Bonnie Blair. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its Evolution is the  Triangle Kick, which requires the  Pummarola and Thunder Kick tech. Fully evolving it (into max level  Triangle Kick) unlocks  Formina Franklyn as playable character.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Kick attacks in a circular pattern in front of the character and deals more damage when at full health. It ignores Speed and Duration.
Can glimmer the "Thunder Kick" tech, summoning a lightning bolt diagonally upwards, then turns sharply. Time of turning affected by Amount.

King Bible is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Dommario. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Unholy Vespers, which requires  Spellbinder.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms [DLC].
## Effects
King Bible spawns a ring of blue bibles around the player that occasionally has pages fall out of it. The bibles spin clockwise around the player and deal damage to any enemy it touches.
Additional bibles from  Amount are added to the circle and spaced evenly.  Speed affects how fast the books rotate,  Duration affects how long they rotate before cooling down, and  Area affects how far away from the player they spin which has a cap in size and increases the size of the bibles.
The  Cooldown of King Bible depends on the weapon's Duration, meaning that its Cooldown is extended by its Duration of 3 seconds to 6 seconds total. The extension will increase with level-ups as they change the base weapon's stats, but it is not affected by other Duration bonuses.
King Bible has a 1.7 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1.7 seconds by the same bible. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows King Bible's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on  Curse.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows King Bible to deal extra flat damage based on  Armor.
## Levels
King Bible has 8 levels. At max level, it has +20 Base Damage, +50% Area, +60% Speed, +3 Amount, and +1 second to Duration.

## Tips
- King Bible works with every passive item that can affect weapon stats. The Collection Tab description says that it works best with  Speed,  Duration, and  Area.
- Bigger Area for King Bible may be detrimental because they are further apart. If the enemies pushed through the "barrier" will probably not leave it again, especially when there is a swamp of enemies constantly pushing more in.
- Normally there cannot be multiple layers of bibles active at once as its full Cooldown is based on the weapon's Duration added to its Cooldown. However, with the character's Duration bonuses from  Spellbinder or Duration PowerUp, it is possible to achieve this as the increase to Cooldown depends only on the weapon's Duration.
- Combined with the knockback resistance reduction of  Garlic or  Soul Eater, King Bible can completely prevent enemies from reaching the player, all the way until the end of the game, if paired with other similar large scale area denial weapons.
- Since King Bible rotates clockwise, damaging enemies by moving in counterclockwise circles will hit them more often.
- Projectile Speed allows King Bible to hit more consistently and is very beneficial early on, but due to the weapon's high Hitbox Delay, it starts to have less benefit after its bibles can complete a full revolution before it refreshes.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the Bible sub-weapon from the Castlevania series. Both cycle the player and pages of the bible fall out of it.
- King Bible in Italian is translated to "Re Bibbia", which literally translate to "King Bible".
- In an interview, Luca revealed that the name was a pun on the Rebibbia underground station in Rome.

Knife is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Gennaro Belpaese, and one of the optional starting weapons of  Zephyr [DLC]. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Thousand Edge, which requires  Bracer.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms [DLC].
## Effects
Knife throws projectiles in the direction the player is moving or last moved. It ignores  Duration and has limited benefit from  Area.
Multiple knives from  Amount are fired in short volleys in parallel. The firing Interval is decreased on levels 4, 6 and 8, grouping each volley of knives closer together. Each knife can initially hit one enemy before dissipating. They cannot pass through walls.
While playing with a keyboard, the knives can only be shot out in eight cardinal and ordinal directions. When playing with a mouse or gamepad, the knives can be fired in any direction.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Knife's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Knife to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 6x damage and have 30% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Knife has 8 levels. At max level, Knife has +10 Base Damage, +5 Amount, +2 Pierce, and -0.06 seconds of Interval.

## Tips
- Knife can deal critical damage after  Slash (XVI) is picked. The more  Luck you have, the more likely you are to deal critical hits. Luck can be increased with  Clover,  Little Clovers, or the Luck PowerUp.
- No matter how you control, Knife is one of the best options for single target damage and keeping enemies at bay in the whole game because of its ability to direct the knives, its unlimited range, and its high  Amount and low  Cooldown.

Kyra-Stones is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the evolution of  Magi-Stone, and requires  Karoma's Mana. It is the starting weapon of  Secretino Dagsson.
Its union is  Shimmering Sands [DLC], which also requires  Descent Into Misery [DLC].
## Effects
Kyra-Stones drops colorful gems from the top of the screen, dealing fixed damage in an area which increases when the character levels up past 80 . It gains  Area,  Speed, and  Amount, and reduces  Cooldown and Interval.
 Amount affects this weapon differently, alternating between increasing the number of large crystals or increasing the number of small fragments.
Kyra-Stones gains +1 Amount per 80 enemies on-screen, with no theoretical limit to this bonus. However, since only 500 enemies can be on-screen at once, this weapon will never gain more than 6.25 Amount.

-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

La Borra is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Santa Water, and requires  Attractorb. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Hydro Pump Climax [DLC], which also requires  Hydro Storm [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
La Borra rains down bottles of holy water from the sky, which break upon impact with the ground, leaving puddles of water and blue flames that damage enemies. The bottles are dropped in a clockwise, roughly circular pattern. These puddles then slowly creep towards the character, increase in size as they travel, and have a maximum size limit.
Its puddle have a bigger  Area, increased  Duration, and lower  Cooldown. More pools can be on screen at once with a high Pool Limit.
The puddles' speed and growth rate are based on multiple factors:
- With  Speed and  Move Speed, the puddles move and grow faster. Both increase the growth rate by the same amount but Movement Speed increases the move speed of the puddles slightly more.
- If La Borra does not receive any Speed bonuses, the puddles still travel slowly but they do not grow larger.
- Negative Projectile Speed shrinks the puddles and makes it move away from the player, it may even grow once again after it shrinks to a single point.
- Movement Speed has a minimum cap on the base value. It does not shrink the pool, make them slower, or reverse direction, but can still counteract the speed and growth rate from a higher Projectile Speed.
- Duration slows down the growth rate of the puddle but not the speed, making them reach the max size when it ends. This stops an infinitely growing pool from lasting very long and covering the entire screen even when the character is moving.
- Duration being less than 100% causes it to grow faster. It being less than or equal to 0% ends the puddle immediately.
La Borra has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half a second by the same puddle. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces La Borra's  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of shooting randomly, will pool under them instead of under the player, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

## Tips
- With enough  Duration and  Cooldown bonuses, La Borra will replace itself fast enough to be persistent. With enough  Amount bonuses, it can reach the Pool Limit. Combining all three, you can create a circle of La Borras around the player that never goes away.
- A particularly effective strategy is to combine this with the  King Bible and  Garlic. Enemies will practically never be able to reach the player.
- La Borra works effectively while moving, as the puddles will be able to move and catch enemies moving closer to the player, if they are off-screen, it will still damages some enemies that the player cannot reach; It also works well while staying still, because the puddles are capable of stacking on top of each other, each damaging enemies separately and staggering them.
## Trivia
- In update 0.5.0,  Move Speed no longer affects La Borra at all and a cap in size has been added. 0.5.1 reverted the Movement Speed changes but made its effect less pronounced compared to how it originally was, which used to be about twice as much as Projectile Speed. The cap in size still exists but it has been increased to almost double the radius compared to 0.5.0.
- This weapon is inspired by the Holy Water sub-weapon from the Castlevania series with similar lingering Area-of-Effect damage.
- The noun "borra", originally meaning "Pellet" (bird of prey's puked leftovers) has quickly become an Italian meme after TV conductor Antonella Clerici misunderstood the word for sborra (a pejorative term for "semen") [Cf. the verb "sborrare", i.e. "to ejaculate" (also in vernacular fashion).]
- The character with  Santa Water as the starting weapon is also a  Clerici.

La Robba is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.7.3. It is the starting weapon of  Sir Ambrojoe. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Sir Ambrojoe is unlocked. It can also be obtained from the  Merchant in-game by spending 1,000, or by selecting it from the  Candybox.
## Effects
La Robba rains down furniture from the top middle of the screen, bouncing off of enemies until the end of its duration or disappears off-screen.

## Trivia
- La Robba is based on the Kinder Surprise Egg, a chocolate treat that comes with toys.
- "La Robba" means "stuff" in Italian. It is also rather similar to  La Borra but they are not related in any other way.
- There is a translation error in both Simplified and Traditional Chinese that uses La Borra's name for both weapons.
- The name "La Robba" is a reference to Giovanni Verga's novel "La Roba"
- The name "La Robba" (literally "The stuff" in Roman dialect) is a common euphemism for "drugs", as further implied by the Kinder Egg shape (drugs are frequently hidden in the hermetic-sealing plastic capsules found in Kinder Eggs, to avoid detection by police dogs and for easier concealment). It is also infamously illegal in the United States of America due to concerns that children may choke on the plastic capsules.
- When used by  Juste Belmont [DLC], La Robba will summon an unique set of furniture from Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance.
- La Robba is one of the weapons that cannot be evolved along with  Greatest Jubilee,  108 Bocce [DLC],  Party Popper [DLC],  Hats [DLC], and most item selectors (except  Candybox).

Lapiste Tepisto is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Kaiser Knuckle [DLC] and  Tri-Bracelet at max level.
## Effects
Lapiste Tepisto launches a burst of stony fists, punching and launching them at random enemies. Fists have a short delay between being fired and launched out. Unlike Tri-Bracelet, fists do not linger on the edge of the screen. Every 14 activations, 2 large stone fists will close in on the player, moving in from the player's left and right. These large fists deal 5 times the damage of the smaller fists to anything in their path.
Compared to Kaiser Knuckle, Lapiste Tepisto has higher Base Damage and faster  Cooldown, but lower  Area and Knockback.
- Note that the effective area of Lapiste Tepisto is much higher than that of Kaiser Knuckle, despite having a lower Area internally.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Fists explode when they expire. Explosion damage is increased by  Curse.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives a 50% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Projectiles explode on hit, dealing half of Lapiste Tepisto's base damage in an area.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Fists now aim at the nearest enemy. Gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Laurel is a non-damaging weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Divano Thelma. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Crimson Shroud, which requires  Metaglio Left and  Metaglio Right at maximum level.
## Effects
Upon triggering, Laurel creates a shield. The next time the player takes damage, the shield loses a charge instead and briefly makes the player invulnerable. When the shield is out of charge, it breaks. The shield's color changes based on the remaining charges: one is blue, two is green, and three is yellow. Taking a hit during Laurel's invulnerability window does not trigger the shield.
Laurel only benefits from bonuses to  Cooldown. Unlike most weapons, Laurel does not benefit from Limit Break.
## Arcanas
-  Blood Astronomia (XXI) - Allows Laurel to place a damaging zone on the ground. The zone deals heavy damage.
## Levels
Laurel has 7 levels. At level 7, Laurel has -2 seconds of Cooldown, +0.8 seconds of invulnerability, and 2 additional charges.

## Tips
- With -87.5%  Cooldown and Laurel at Level 6+, the Cooldown is fast enough to recharge the shield before the invulnerability ends effectively making the character invincible.
- Laurel is a great weapon to take when you already have 4 or 5 good weapons and you are set for the run. Its extra protection may seem useless if you are already killing everything before you take damage, but its automatic nature protects from mistakes and being overwhelmed.
- Laurel used to prevent retaliation explosions from  NO FUTURE and  Heart of Fire (XIX). Since 0.6.1, as one of the effect from  Crimson Shroud is triggering an explosion when a charge is used, all of them are changed to remove this anti-synergy.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the Laurel item from the Castlevania series. It also provides invulnerability and the icon is similar to Herb from Castlevania Chronicles.
- Despite having a value for damage, it is not used for anything.
- Laurel used to have a placeholder evolution with the codename "THORNS". Its Area is increased by 10% compared to Laurel and presumably will deal retaliation damage while in contact with enemies. This has been removed in the 0.6.1 update and replaced by  Crimson Shroud as the actual evolution.
- Laurel and  Clock Lancet are the only weapons with a max level of 7 instead of the usual 8.
-  Pentagram used to have 7 levels only as well but one more level was added when  Gorgeous Moon was introduced.

Legacy of Death: Soul River is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Dark Rift [DLC] at max level and  Death Spiral.
## Effects
Legacy of Death: Soul River retains the firing pattern of  Death Spiral, summoning  Death's scythes instead of  The Reaper's. Legacy of Death: Soul River also summons 3 skulls from the player every 0.1 seconds, spiraling out towards the edges of the screen, damaging any enemy they come into contact with, with each skull having unlimited pierce. Each skull will deal half of Legacy of Death: Soul River's damage, multiplied by the lower value between 1 and  Area (if Area is below +0%). The number of skulls this weapon summons is fixed at 3, and cannot be increased by  Amount.
Compared to  Dark Rift, Legacy of Death: Soul River has a slower  Cooldown, but increased Knockback and  Amount.
Legacy of Death: Soul River has a lower  Area cap than other weapons, with its maximum effect being reached at +400% instead of +900%.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Legacy of Death: Soul River's scythe projectiles to bounce off of the edges of the screen once. Upon bouncing, the projectile completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them according to the edge.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Legacy of Death: Soul River to critical hit. Critical chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Legacy of Death: Soul River's scythes now aim at nearest enemy instead of shooting around the player, and Legacy of Death: Soul River gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Legionnaire is an evolved weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the Evolution of the  Eskizzibur, requiring the  Armor at max level.
## Effects
Legionnaire creates sword swings around the character, and also clones of the character traveling in the direction the player is moving or last moved. It may also strike at the ground every fifth attack, cracking it for a huge Area-of-Effect damage. When retaliating, it attacks immediately again and can retaliate every 1.5 seconds. The clones are considered retaliatory damage to be boosted by Armor and triggers Divine Bloodline (IX).
Legionnaire have a bigger Area and lower critical chance when using Slash (XVI). It also has a higher Pool Limit.
The clones' movement speed is affected by Speed, Move Speed, and Duration. Consecutive swing from increased Amount alternate between firing towards and away from the direction the character is facing; it also adds to the legion of clones, adding one more to the ring that surrounds the middle one.
## Arcanas
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - The projectiles created by the Legionnaire activates the Arcana's Max Health Boost.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Legionnaire to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.

## Tips
- This weapon has a unique interaction with the Divine Bloodline (IX) Arcana. because the constant stream of clones created by the weapon are considered dealing retaliatory damage, this activates the Arcana's ability with every kill from these clone projectiles. Combined with the fact that current health is not restored at the same time, this also translates to a flat damage increase per enemy killed by the clones provided there's nothing healing the character. With Boogaloo of Illusions (XVIII) that can allows the clones to cover the whole screen and the weapon can wipe out bosses with ease.

Lifesign Scan is a weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Ghost Lino. It is unlocked by getting itself to level 7. It is also a stage item on Polus Replica.
It can be evolved into  Paranormal Scan with  Mini Ghost at max level. The passive item will be added to the pool of available items upon leveling up as soon as the weapon reaches level 2.
## Effects
Lifesign Scan creates a green elliptic grid that scans the character from bottom to top, after which a big green circle flashes around the character and healing every player in it in Co-op mode, the radius is increased by Area. Its healing effect is multiplied by Amount and Recovery.

-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - allows Lifesign Scan to heal double amount of health and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) - damage is increased by the healing generated by Lifesign Scan.

Lightning Ring is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Porta Ladonna and  Wood Rod [DLC]. It is unlocked by defeating a total of 5,000 enemies.
Its evolution is  Thunder Loop, which requires  Duplicator.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms [DLC].
## Effects
Lightning Ring summons lightning strikes from the sky to deal damage to random enemies. When the lightning strikes the ground, it creates a hitbox that deals damage, rather than the lightning bolts themselves.
Bonuses to  Area affect how large this hitbox is.
## Arcanas
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Lightning Ring's  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Lightning Ring's strikes to explode one more time with a different effect. The damage of these explosions is based on  Curse.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows Lightning Ring's strikes to deal extra flat damage based on  Armor.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

## Tips
-  Candelabrador is one of the most effective ways to increase the power of Lightning Ring. With enough area, each bolt can hit dozens of enemies at once. This is magnified further with bonuses to  Amount, which adds more lightning bolts.
- Lightning Ring is extremely versatile, being able to work well with many weapons in many types of builds. It can also be considered a primary damage dealer, due to how much damage it can deal to many enemies at once. However, due to the random nature of the weapon, picking it up early is not advised.
## Trivia
- This weapon may be inspired by the Agunea sub-weapon from the Castlevania series.

Long Gun is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Bill Rizer [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Bill Rizer.
Its evolution is  Prototype A [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC].
## Effects
As a classic videogame-style machine gun, Long Gun rapidly fires small, weak bullet projectiles in the faced direction of the character.
Long Gun scales uniquely with  Amount - rather than add extra projectiles, it will instead decrease the cooldown of the weapon further. However, this bonus cannot allow it to exceed its minimum cooldown.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Long Gun's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Long Gun has 8 Levels. At max level, Long Gun has +5 Base Damage, +1 Pierce, and -0.1 seconds of Cooldown.

## Tips
- Due to Long Gun's rather poor crowd control but rapid firing, pairing it with  Heart of Fire (XIX) is a good idea. This in turn creates possible combos with  Divine Bloodline (IX) and  Heir of Fate (XIX), either of which will help boost Long Gun's damage and give it extremely high DPS.
- Only one of the two proposed combo arcanas should be picked, as their abilities do not work well together: Divine Bloodline's bonus damage will not get amplified by  Might, while Heir's Scorched Souls would provide too much healing and hinder the bonus damage of the former.

Long Inus is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Javelin, and requires  Spellbinder.
## Effects
Long Inus throws Longinus in the direction the character is facing horizontally. The Longinus fans out with each throw; they are affected by gravity and can pierce virtually infinite enemies. Longinus screen wraps for its  Duration instead of disappearing like javelins.

-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Lucky Swipe is a weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Engineer Gino. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Engineer.
It can be evolved into  Crossed Wires with  Mini Engineer at max level. The passive item will be added to the pool of available items upon leveling up as soon as the weapon reaches level 2.
## Effects
Lucky Swipe creates an ID card that is being swiped from left to right over the player faster and faster. Amount and Luck lower than 100% increase the number of times the card being swiped, with the swiping speed accelerating.
## Levels
Lucky Swipe has 8 levels. At max level, Lucky Swipe has +25 Base Damage, +50% Area, +30% Projectile Speed, +3 Amount, and -0.07 seconds of Interval.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | "The amount of attacks is affected by Amount and by low luck."
| Level 2 | Base Area up by 25%.
| Level 3 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 10%.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Area up by 25%.

## Tips
- As a lower luck stat makes this weapon more effective, disabling Luck in power up tab makes this weapon swipes more. This is especially useful for Engineer Gino as they start with the weapon.
## Trivia
- Lucky Swipe is based on the Swipe Card task in Among Us, wherein the player must swipe an ID card at just the correct speed.
- The character on the ID card is Antonio Belpaese. The text on the ID card reads as follows: "HELLO WORLD this a test of really low resolution text that is mostly not readable so wouldn't need localisation but we could still hide easter eggs"

Luminaire is an evolved weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Prismatic Missile [DLC], and requires  Crown at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Luminaire creates orange, yellow, blue, and magenta beams that strike at every enemy vertically. It also makes a few intricate circles rotating counter-clockwise and periodically rains down white beams, both of which are purely cosmetic. The beams can explode with the effects of  Twilight Requiem (II),  Jail of Crystal (XIV), or  Heart of Fire (XIX) (Bug: Should only apply the first chosen Arcana, but will only apply the last if the Arcana are obtained before); selecting these Arcanas in a run will enhance their respective effects.
Luminaire has a higher base damage and Pool Limit, shorter interval, but lower  Area and longer  Cooldown. It is no longer affected by  Speed.
Every time Luminaire attacks, it set the value of  Experience Gems and  Gold Coins/ Coin Bags by the following formula:
totalAmount+ln⁡(x)x
x≡total number of EXP gems and coin/coin bags in the screen
It also updates the sprite of the gold items to reflect their value and randomizes the color of the experience gems to one of 11 different colors.
Luminaire can attack and defeat The Blinder in Abyss Foscari, causing it to drop  Treasure Chests. However, this does not work for other Reaper variants.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows the beam to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives the beam a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows the beam to explode again when it hits the ground. Extra explosion's damage is affected by  Curse.
## Levels

## Tips
- Luminaire ability to increase the value of  Experience Gems and  Gold Coins/ Coin Bags is valuable in gold runs; pair them with  Crown and  Stone Mask for the best effects.
- With each attack, every Experience Gem get blessed and in total gains the natural log of the number of items more experience, spread across each gem evenly. Thus, the more gems on the ground, the stronger each blessing is. The same applies to Gold Coins and Coin Bags.
## Trivia
- The center of the concentric circles is where  Luminaire Foscari [DLC] stays when  Eleanor Uziron [DLC] fights  Je-Ne-Viv.

Luminatio (means Illumination in Latin) is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Lisa Tepes. It is unlocked by defeating 3000 enemies with Lisa.
It can be evolved into  Vol Luminatio with Max level  Crown. Evolving it unlocks  Shaft as playable character.
It can be selected when using the  Ebony Diabologue.
## Effects
Luminatio summons a pair of yellow light ball projectiles that spin downward around the character (counter-clockwise when the character facing left, clockwise when facing right) and damage enemies they contact.

LunarBight is a weapon in Vampire Survivors.  Gekkojin [DLC] can choose to start with it via skin selection.
Its union is  LunarFlight [DLC], which also requires  LunarMight [DLC] and  LunarSight [DLC] at max level.
LunarBight can be unlocked by getting it to level 6 after obtaining it by overhealing by 64 health as  Spiritoso [DLC].
## Effects
LunarBight creates a beam of light that orbits a set distance from where the player was when LunarBight activated; much like LunarSight, active beams will not follow the player. Enemies hit by these beams will take damage.
Enemies that don't have debuff resistance, when hit by LunarBight, will be slowed. As LunarBight's level increases, the amount of slow it applies will also increase.
- On older versions, LunarBight is bugged to not apply any slow.
LunarBight has a base 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same beam. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
LunarBight has 6 levels. At max level, LunarBight has +25 Base Damage, +1 second of Duration, and -0.2 seconds of Hitbox Delay.

LunarFlight is a weapon in Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  LunarMight [DLC],  LunarSight [DLC], and  LunarBight [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
LunarFlight retains the effects of its constituent parts, with an extra, larger damage zone being encompassing all of them, arranged concentrically. 
Instead of damage zones lingering in place, they will constantly follow the player. The  Might bonus provided by LunarMight will also increase to +30%.
LunarFlight will retain any upgrades given to LunarMight, LunarSight, and LunarBight given by Limit Break.
Depending on the player's  Cooldown, but at a minimum of every 22 seconds, LunarFlight will being to crescendo. During this time, notes will play before it unleashes its singularity, dealing damage equal to 10 times LunarFlight's damage to any enemy hit. Damage done by the singularity is indicated with a special, blue damage number. If the player has Weapons ScreenShake enabled, then the screen will briefly zoom out during the singularity, before quickly zooming back in.
LunarFlight has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the singularity. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

LunarMight is a weapon in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by getting it to level 6. It is the starting weapon of  Spiritoso [DLC] and one of the starting weapons of  Gekkojin [DLC].
Its union is  LunarFlight [DLC], which also requires  LunarSight [DLC] and  LunarBight [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
LunarMight creates a magic circle at the character's location, damaging enemies that it contacts. The zones created by LunarMight will last for a base of 2.5 seconds, increasing with  Duration.
At level 1, LunarMight will increase the  Might of any character within it by +5%. At levels 3 and 6, this increases to +10% and +20%, respectively. This Might bonus is increased by other sources of Might, excluding  Silent Old Sanctuary (XX), as its Might is added separately, and  Divine Bloodline (IX), as, even though its flat damage bonus is displayed as Might, it does not give Might.
- For example, the base amount of Might from PowerUps, +35%, leads to LunarMight giving +27% Might at level 6.
LunarMight has a base 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.5 seconds by the same zone. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
LunarMight has 6 levels. At max level, LunarMight has +10 Base Damage, -1 second of Cooldown, +0.5 seconds of Duration, and -0.25 seconds of Hitbox Delay.

| Level 1 | Generates a damaging zone that slightly increases Might.
| Level 2 | Base Damage up by 5.

| Level 4 | Duration up by 0.5 seconds.
| Level 5 | Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds. Hitbox delay reduced by 0.125 seconds.
| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 5.

LunarSight is a weapon in Vampire Survivors.  Gekkojin [DLC] can choose to start with it via skin selection.
Its union is  LunarFlight [DLC], which also requires  LunarMight [DLC] and  LunarBight [DLC] at max level.
LunarSight can be unlocked by getting it to level 6 after obtaining it by overhealing by 64 health as  Spiritoso [DLC].
## Effects
LunarSight creates up to 8 damaging zones, depicting the 8 phases of the moon, around the player, in a counter-clockwise pattern based on their current position. New zones will be created based on the player's current position, but old zones will not follow the player. Enemies that contact these zones will take damage.
LunarSight has a 0.25 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.25 seconds by the same lunar phase. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
LunarSight has 6 levels. At max level, LunarSight has +20 Base Damage and +2 seconds of Duration.

| Level 2 | Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 3 | Effect lasts 1 seconds longer.

| Level 6 | Base Damage up by 10.

Mace is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Hector. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 50,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Stamazza with max level  Hollow Heart. Evolving it after obtaining  Black Disk unlocks  Isaac as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Mace summons a mace that spin around the character, damaging enemies it touches. Duration affects how far the mace travels around the character.

Magi-Stone is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the starting weapon of  Chula-Reh.
Magi-Stone can be found as stage item in Westwoods. It is unlocked by upgrading it to level 7.
Its evolution is  Kyra-Stones, which requires  Karoma's Mana. Evolving it will unlock 500 as reward.
## Effects
Magi-Stone drops red, blue, and yellow bipyramid gems from the top of the screen that break into smaller gems upon hitting their target. The base damage of this weapon is increased by 10 every level. It ignores  Might and  Duration.
There is zero hitbox delay between the large gem and smaller pieces it breaks into. The smaller gems deal half the base damage of the larger gem.
 Amount affects this weapon differently, alternating between increasing the number of large crystals or increasing the number of small fragments.
## Arcanas
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Gains a chance to fire more than twice when activated.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Magi-Stone has 8 levels. At max level, it has +40% Area, +40% Projectile Speed, +2 Amount, and -0.4 seconds of Cooldown.

Magic Wand is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Imelda Belpaese, and one of the starting weapons of  Wood Rod [DLC]. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Holy Wand, which requires  Empty Tome.
## Effects
Magic Wand shoots a blue magic missile that is fired at the closest enemy to the player.
Additional projectiles from  Amount will be fired in a sequence. Each missile can initially hit one enemy before dissipating. The missiles cannot pass through walls.
## Arcanas
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - Allows Magic Wand's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by Magic Wand's projectiles will explode.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives Magic Wand a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by Magic Wand's projectiles will drop  Crystallized Souls when killed.
## Levels
Magic Wand has 8 levels. At max level, Magic Wand has +20 Base Damage, +3 Amount, +1 Pierce, and -0.2 seconds of Cooldown.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Fires at the nearest enemy.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Cooldown reduced by 0.2 seconds.

## Tips
- The automatic targeting nature of the weapon is both a blessing and a curse. While it removes the mental load of aiming, the closest enemy might not always be the enemy the player trying to attack. It should be considered a supporting weapon, and not necessarily a main damage dealer.
- If Magic Wand is targeting a further enemy and you would like to it to target a closer one, you can wiggle the character a bit by doing small movements to update the target of the weapon.
- Magic Wand is one of the best options for single target damage and keeping enemies at bay in the whole game because of its high  Amount and low  Cooldown. However, its damage against multiple enemies is lacking even with the extra pierce;  Waltz of Pearls (XI) is recommended to increase the amount of enemies it can hit.

Mannajja is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Song of Mana, and requires  Skull O'Maniac. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Dies Irae [DLC], which also requires  Arrow of Goth [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Mannajja releases a pulsing wave of sparkling purple particles outwards from the player in the shape of five concentric circles similar to a sound wave. The particles are positioned relative to the player in a vertical column around them, and follow their movement. The Mannajja covers a much wider Area but has a slightly longer Cooldown.
Enemies hit by the Mannajja are slowed down permanently. If the enemy is not immune to debuffs, each hit reduces the Movement Speed of the affected enemy by an additional 5%, until it reaches a minimum of 20% of their original speed after 16 hits. The slow effect stacks multiplicatively with other Movement Speed modifications.
The Mannajja has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than once every second by the same pulse. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Blood Astronomia (XXI) - Allows the Mannajja to emit special damaging zones. These zones take the form of several planets orbiting around a point.

## Tips
-  Area affects how wide the hitbox is, so  Candelabrador is one of the most effective ways to increase the power of this weapon.
-  Duration is also extremely effective as it maintains the column for a longer time. Combined with reduced  Cooldown from items like  Empty Tome and  Spellbinder, multiple columns can be active at once.
- With weapons that have incredible stalling potential like  Garlic,  King Bible, and  Clock Lancet, the slowing debuff from it can be added to the build.
## Trivia
- The music score used for Mannajja is the same as the page that falls out of  Unholy Vespers.
- Mannajja contains a word similar to "Mana". Its English pronunciation is similar to an Italian exclamation "Mannaggia" meaning "Damn" or "Darnit".
- This weapon may be inspired by the Hymn sub-weapon from the Castlevania series.
