The Mazo Familiar is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.9.0. It is the evolution of  Pako Battiliar, and requires the  Hollow Heart at max level.
It is the starting weapon of  Bats Bats Bats.
## Effects
The Mazo Familiar spawns a group of bigger bats with purple afterimages which fly in a straight line across the screen, starting at randomly off-screen and pass through the center of the screen relative to where they spawned. Each bat will deal damage to enemies it will encounter up to its Pierce and then disappear. When retaliating, it spawn another group of bats and can retaliate every ~1.8 seconds.
The Mazo Familiar gains Amount, Pierce, and a small bit of Interval, no longer causing all the bats to spawn at once. It loses half of its Pool Limit.
The Mazo Familiar's Base Damage and Amount is affected by Max Health, it gains +0.05 damage per +1 Max Health and +1 Amount per +20 Max Health.
## Arcanas
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Increases Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed with retaliatory damage.

## Trivia
- The Mazo Familiar is a reference to the Bat Swarm map event.
- "Mazo Familiar" is a pun on "...ammazzo famiglia" (literally "I kill family", a phrase racistically attributed to Romanian immigrants in Italy, meaning "...I kill family"). The full idiom would be "Spacco bottiglia, ammazzo famiglia" ("I break bottle, I kill family"), where the first part appears here as "Pako Battiliar"

Meal Ticket is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Wine Glass, and requires  Tirajisú at max level.
## Effects
Meal Ticket throws a ticket at the nearest enemy, which then produces a small explosion on contact and summons four damaging food items on the ground. Its Base Damage and  Area is slightly increased. It no longer multiples base  Amount by 4.
Food spawned by Meal Ticket can also be collected to heal the player by 1 health, multiplied by  Recovery, but disappears 1 second later and cannot be extended by  Duration. When the food deals damage or is collected, it creates a yellow beam towards the top of the screen.
The damage is calculated by (baseDamage+bloodlineFlatDamage)*currentRevival, and will decrease when a  Revival is used. This does not scale with  Might.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Meal Ticket's food to heal double their amount and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Hidden Anathema (III) - Food summoned by Meal Ticket provides a single random stat increase.

- This weapon is based on the Meal Ticket from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, which makes random food items appear and can be collected to heal.
- Most of the food from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night has a chance of appearing, with the exception of Peanuts (used for  Pile of Secrets [DLC]), Pot Roast (used for  Wall Chicken [DLC]), Turkey (likely too similar to Wall Chicken), and Delicious Meal and Smelly Rice (both being Saturn-only, likely not a coincidence).
- Because of how damage is calculated for this weapon, the flat damage from  Divine Bloodline (IX) also scales with  Revival.

Metal Claw is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Colonel Bahamut [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Colonel Bahamut.
Its evolution is  Big Fuzzy Fist [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Hollow Heart.
## Effects
Metal Claw slashes horizontally both ways around the player. Additional slashes granted by  Amount will move further and further away, increasing the weapon's reach.
Metal Claw's  Cooldown is affected by a percentage of missing health: The more health the player character loses, the faster it attacks.

Metal Claw has 8 Levels. At max level, Metal Claw has +15 Base Damage, +150% Area, +4 Amount, and -1 second of Cooldown.

## Tips
- Despite not having retaliatory damage, Metal Claw synergizes particularly well with the  Divine Bloodline (IX) arcana, as both of them give you benefits for being low on health. Divine Bloodline's bonus damage in combination with Metal Claw's attack speed bonus can turn the latter into a high-DPS horde shredder.
- Considering  Hollow Heart is nearly essential for Divine Bloodline builds, if going for this specific combo, one should consider either sealing  Big Fuzzy Fist in the collection, banishing Metal Claw before level 8, or avoiding picking up the  Weapon Power-Up to not accidentally evolve Metal Claw.
## Trivia
- This weapon was called "the Power Glove" in Contra: Hard Corps.

- While the game has several rare weapons paired with characters that are unlocked by killing a certain number of a certain enemy, Mille Bolle Blu is the only one of these that can be evolved normally.
- Mille Bolle Blu is the name of an Italian comedy film from 1993, it's also similar to "Le Mille Bolle Blu", a 1961 song from Italian pop singer Mina. Its literal translation is "Thousand blue bubbles".

Million Cut is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Valmanway [DLC] at max level and  Thousand Edge.
## Effects
Million Cut slashes at faced direction which travels across the screen.
Million Cut's Base Damage is almost the sum of Valmanway and Thousand Edge, and uses the  Cooldown, Interval, and knockback of Thousand Edge, which means it slashes a lot faster but the knockback is dramatically lower compared to Valmanway.
 Move Speed increases its overall attack rate when moving; when the character stops, it returns to its default  Cooldown.
Continuous movement increases the  Area of the slashes by +10% per second, up to a max of +100%; when the character stops, it gradually loses the bonus, at a rate of -25% per second, instead of completely resetting.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Million Cut's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Million Cut to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 6x damage and have 30% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Millionaire is an evolved weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Flash Arrow [DLC], requiring  Bracer at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Millionaire shoots an arrow in the direction the player is moving or last moved. It can pierce through many enemies. When collecting Coins and Coin Bags or defeating enemies with the arrow, yellow bullets rains down on the screen from the top corner away from where the player is looking.
It has a bigger  Area and Pool Limit, and infinite pierce.
 Amount multiplies Millionaire's damage instead of providing more arrows, and also multiplies how many bullets rain down when collecting Coins (which scales with the value of the pickup) or defeating enemies with the arrow, the base amount being 1 and 4 respectively. The bullets are queued up and released every 0.1 seconds.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have a 20% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Doubles the damage of Millionaire's critical hits, causing them to deal 4x damage.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows the arrows to bounce off the edges of the screen three times. Upon bouncing, the arrow completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them according to the edge.

## Tips
-  Greed does not affect the amount of raining arrows when collecting  Gold Coins or Coin Bags.
-  Luminaire [DLC] increases the base value of Coin pickups to increase the number of bullets fired. It also synergizes well with an already Coin-focused run.
-  Disco of Gold (XV) can trigger a Gold Fever that will let the player queue enough arrows to fire without stopping for a few minutes.
-  Vicious Hunger allows consistent acquisition of coins from enemies, thus causing arrows to essentially rain nonstop.
## Trivia
- Millionaire is a reference to a strong late-game tech of the same name in multiple SaGa games that hits all enemies.

Miracle of Multiplication is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It can be selected from  Penshin Fatcha after evolving six or more times.
## Effects
Miracle of Multiplication attacks with all the previously selected tuna forms at once, splitting the levels across each one evenly. For example, if two tuna forms are picked and evolve a total of seven times before Miracle of Multiplication is picked, 42 total levels are available; each weapon will receive 21 levels even if the first one is picked six times and the other weapon just once, effectively boosting the stats based on their own six levels three times over with an extra three levels. Previous forms can be evolved infinitely before Miracle of Multiplication is picked.
It can no longer level up normally and be evolved, locking in its stat boost from the previous choices.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) adds a chance for all of this weapon's tuna forms to freeze enemies.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) gives a chance for all of this weapon's tuna forms to fire twice. The chance is increased by  Luck.

Mirage Robe is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Babi-Onna. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Babi-Onna.
Mirage Robe can be evolved into  J'Odore with  Attractorb at max level. Evolving it unlocks  McCoy-Oni as a playable character.
## Effects
Mirage Robe creates mirage around the character, which looks like the after image of the character and freezes enemies.
 Area increases the size of the explosion.  Duration will add to the time enemies are frozen and how long the mirage last.
Depending on its level and the  Luck stat, there is a chance for the mirage to explode.
## Arcanas
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Allows the mirage to always create explosions when they hit enemies.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy like  J'Odore, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Mirage Robe has 8 Levels. At max level, Mirage Robe has +40 Base Damage, +4.0 seconds to effect  Duration, and 60% chance to explode.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | "Generates freezing mines with a chance to explode."
| Level 2 | Effect lasts 1 seconds longer.
| Level 3 | Effect lasts 1 seconds longer. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 4 | 10% chance to explode.
| Level 5 | Effect lasts 1 seconds longer.
| Level 6 | Effect lasts 1 seconds longer. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 7 | 20% chance to explode.
| Level 8 | Base Damage up by 20.
## Limit Break
With Limit Break, Mirage Robe can be further leveled up.
| Description | Rarity | Max Total
| Might +1% | 10 | -
| Area +2.5% | 10 | 1000%
| Duration +100ms | 1 | 9.0 seconds
| Amount +1 | 1 | 20
- ↑ Base Damage +0.5
## Tips
- If you are trying to kill The Reaper, but don't want to waste a spot on  Laurel in your freeze-based build, Mirage Robe can serve as a substitute by protecting you against Reaper attacks from all sides. It is best left unevolved, however, as  J'Odore lacks Mirage Robe's 360 coverage.

Mormegil Tip is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Jet Black Whip, requiring  Stone Mask.
## Effects
Being a tip, the Mormegil Tip evolution does not change the weapon's function, but simply adds to it. Every 7th activation of the Jet Black Whip triggers  Dark Rift effect, summoning large pillars of purple fire (affected by Area/not affected by Duration) that harm foes that walk near it, lingering for a long time and pushing back enemies. They spawn at the bottom of their hitbox, centered on where your character is standing at the time of activation.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Projectiles explode when they expire. Does not affect the Dark Rift effect.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Jet Black Whip to deal critical damage. Has no effect on special attack.

## Tips
- With the width of the Mormegil Tip's ability, and its height, all being affected by Area, this tip is best suited for northern travel, as the pillars of fire cannot go or spawn downward.
- Weapons that pair well with the Mormegil Tip include the Iron Ball and its evolution, the Wrecking Ball, as well as the Axe. All three weapons also benefit from the Candelabrador, with the Axe also requiring it to evolve.
## Trivia
- The Mormegil Tip is named after the Mormegil weapon that appears in several Castlevania games, which in turn is directly named after the name orcs and elves gave the character Túrin in Lord of the Rings. In Symphony of the Night, it is one of only two swords with the Dark attribute, though it has no special attacks.

The Morning Star is a weapon selector from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by evolving all 8 magic whips, though this does not have to be done in a single stage.
## Effects
The Morning Star allows the player to select one of the Ode to Castlevania magic whips, which includes:
-  Alchemy Whip
-  Wind Whip
-  Platinum Whip
-  Dragon Water Whip
-  Sonic Whip
-  Jet Black Whip
-  Vibhuti Whip
-  Vanitas Whip
## Eligible characters
-  Leon Belmont [DLC]
-  Sonia Belmont [DLC]
-  Trevor Belmont [DLC]
-  Christopher Belmont [DLC]
-  Simon Belmont [DLC]
-  Juste Belmont [DLC]

-  Julius Belmont [DLC]

-  Jonathan Morris [DLC]
-  Reinhardt Schneider [DLC]
-  Nathan Graves [DLC]
-  Jonathan & Charlotte [DLC]
## Tips
- The Morning Star only requires that the player evolves each of the magic whips. It does not require the player to unlock the magic whips. Though the usefulness of evolving a magic whip and not unlocking it somewhat reduces the utility of the Morning Star.
## Trivia
- The name and the icon are a reference to The Morning Star, which is often portrayed as the most powerful form of the Vampire Killer whip, with the icon being the whip powerup item in Classicvania games.

Multistage Missiles is an evolved weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Homing Miss, requiring  Weapon Power-Up and  Duplicator. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Multistage Missiles behave nearly identically to their unevolved form, with the major difference being trading away their pierce for the ability to split into extra smaller missiles upon exploding. These smaller missiles will seek out and explode on enemies the same way as the main projectiles, although their turning is much more sharp, and their  Speed is greatly increased.

Muramasa is an evolved weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Night Sword, requiring  Stone Mask at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Muramasa creates a series of slashes at the closest enemies. When retaliating, it slashes six times around the character and can retaliate every 0.6 seconds.
Muramasa's Base Damage is doubled and has a lower  Cooldown and Interval, compared to Night Sword. The  Amount of slashes for each attack is lowered.
Muramasa's damage is multiplied by 2 x  Greed above base Greed (+0%).
Muramasa has a 10% chance to generate little hearts that heal 1 point of health upon killing an enemy, which is 10 times more than its base form. This chance is affected by  Luck.
It also gains a finisher, causing every fifth slash to become vertical, covering a large area.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 10% chance to occur. The chance is affected by Luck.
Muramasa drains a max of 4 health per activation, decreasing as the player's health reaches 25%. At this point, it only drains 1 health.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Muramasa's Little Hearts to heal double their amount and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Slash (XVI) - Muramasa's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Increases  Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed with retaliatory damage.
-  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) - Damage is increased by the healing generated by Muramasa. The draining effect counts as taking damage.
## Levels

## Tips
- Muramasa's ability to drain the character's health is useful for builds that are based on  Sarabande of Healing (VI),  Divine Bloodline (IX), or  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI).
- For example, there is a synergy between it and  Soul Eater; Soul Eater's power increases by healing missing health but enemies cannot reach the player because they are defeated too quickly, Muramasa provides that opportunity to heal up.
- The health drained by Muramasa will also activate retaliatory damage from weapons, including itself. This can synergize with Divine Bloodline (IX) in order to scale Max Health even when enemies are no longer capable of damaging the player.
- Due to the way it scales with  Greed, Muramasa is a great pick for characters with scaling Greed or high native Greed.
- Characters with immunity to Health Drain, such as  Alucard, are immune to its health drain, but this can be a drawback as this means they cannot use it in combination with Wandering the Jet Black,  Mazo Familiar and other weapons and items that require the character to be losing health.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by Muramasa. They were a famous swordsmith and the blades were favored by the shogen Tokugawa Ieyasu, but the katana gradually became a symbol of the anti-Tokugawa movement. Furthermore, in lore and popular culture since the 18th century, the sword has been regarded as yōtō (妖刀, "wicked katana"). Sometimes, the blade is depicted with a blood-red color like the icon. Hence, the blade's curse causes the character to lose health when using it.
- The base weapon and health-draining mechanic of Muramasa could also be a potential reference to the magic sword Nightblood from Brandon Sanderson's novels. Whenever that blade is drawn, it starts consuming the soul of the wielder.
- Continuing the similarities to  Victory Sword from Night Sword, the addition of finisher and critical hit is very similar to the effect of Level 8 Victory Sword; the damage increase and cooldown reduction from the evolution also resemble the effects from Level 9 to 12.
- The amount of health Muramasa drains used to be a percentage of the character's Max Health, making it a poor choice for characters that were able to obtain huge amounts of Max Health, like  Miang Moonspell [DLC] or builds using Divine Bloodline (IX). However, this is no longer the case, making this weapon a must-pick for Divine Bloodline builds.

Myo Lift is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors
Its union is  Clock Tower, which requires  Endo Gears,  Peri Pendulum, and  Epi Head at max level.
## Effects
Myo Lift summons pale blue lifts on the both sides of the screen that repeatedly traveling up and down and damaging enemies they contact, with its damage being increased by  Amount and found  Orologion. Being a Clockwork weapon, Myo Lift also triggers other Clockwork weapons.
- Myo Lift gains a +(1/3)x damage multiplier per +1 Amount, up to a max of x3.333... at +10 Amount
- Myo Lift gains a damage bonus in accordance to log(OrologionsFound), meaning they gain +1 Damage for every 10x in Orologions found, starting with +1 Base Damage at 10 Orologions.
Myo Lift has a 2.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every two and a half seconds by the same lift. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Increases the likelihood of finding Orologions, which increase Myo Lift's damage.
-  Hail from the Future (X) - Occasionally spawns Orologions whenever the character levels up, indirectly increasing Myo Lift's damage.
## Levels
Myo Lift has 9 levels. At max level, Myo Lift has +40 Base damage and +200% Speed.

NaneInferno is an evolved weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Infernolatro [DLC], requiring  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
NaneInferno adds a second zone of blue flame behind the faced direction, which moves slower than the front one, and they get increased Base Damage,  Area, and  Duration by killing more enemies by any means, resetting when the weapon's duration ends. Each zone has an individual kill counter. As the red one touches the blue one when the player turns around, they merge into one zone that covers more of the screen. After combining, every 10 kills translates to 1 order of magnitude more score for each zone (e.g. 180 kills turns into e18). It has a longer  Cooldown and Duration, and the Area decreased.
NaneInferno follows a similar formula to Infernolatro:
BaseDamage+xKillsWhileProjectileActive
KillsWhileProjectileActive≡total number of enemies killed during that instance of NaneInferno from any source
Note that the value of x is dependent on if the counters have been combined, defaulting to 0.05 if they have not been, but 0.125 if they have. This means the base damage will scale 2.5 times faster when the counters are combined.
Upon reaching a 1,540 to 1,550 kills, approximately e154 or e155 for each counter which multiply to 1.8e308, the word "naneinf" will flash up, and an image of Jimbo will appear. At this point, a  Rosary and  Vacuum will be triggered, and extra  Gold Coins will be summoned.
NaneInferno has a 1.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1.5 seconds by the same damage zone. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
Upon evolving Infernolatro into NaneInferno, Outer Saboteur is removed from the passive slot and turns into Inner Saboteur, placed over the character's face and can still evolve other Ante Chamber DLC weapons. Obtaining NaneInferno from a  Super Candybox II Turbo will give the player the option of obtaining Outer Saboteur via a Level Up.
## Arcana
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Damage zones deal extra contact damage, dealing half of the base damage in an area.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - Defeated enemies drop  Scorched Souls, giving bonus  Max Health and  Might.

## Tips
-  Curse and  Charm can help increase the scaling of this weapon by increasing the number of enemies spawned.
-  Skull O'Maniac,  Torrona's Box, and  Karoma's Mana all provide these stats.
- NaneInferno does not have to get kills to benefit from them. The player can take other weapons for safety.
- The player should consistently move in the same direction, either clockwise or counter-clockwise, if they wish to combine the damage zones of this weapon.
- Zones move faster as more enemies are killed, making the blue one harder to catch up, and excess lag can prevent the damage zones from combining.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the "Naneinf" score in Balatro, which is essentially the maximum possible score that can be obtained in the game. The name of this weapon, NaneInferno, contains the notation "naneinf", which is derived from that notation.
- 1.8e308 is the largest number that can be depicted in double-precision floating-point format, the point at which a "naneinf" is obtained in Balatro (reaching it will lead to game crushing, ironically). Thus, reaching it triggers the special effects of NaneInferno.
- The blue part of the weapon icon refers to chips and the red part refers to mult. Their value gets multiplied to get an initial score before other multipliers kick in, which is referenced by how the zones of flame of the weapon work. The infinite symbol again references the Naneinf score.

Nduja Fritta Tanto is an item pickup in Vampire Survivors that has a chance to drop from light sources. Its drop rate is affected by Luck.
## Effects
Upon picking up Nduja Fritta Tanto, the player's character begins to breathe fire in the direction they are facing, similar to  Knife for 10 seconds. The flame will grow in size as they travel. It is coded to be a temporary weapon, so it can be affected by different stat increases.
## Tips
- Nduja Fritta Tanto benefits from every stat increase.
-  Duration extends how long the full effect and each flame last. It is not limited by the 400% Duration cap from a  Golden Egg.
-  Area makes the expanding flames grow even faster.
-  Speed increases the range of the flames.
- When it is used by a cat from  Gatti Amari the Pickup itself will explode and despawn the cat that used it. The explosion is the same as the ones from  Heart of Fire (XIX).
- Nduja Fritta Tanto is affected by  Gemini (I), which causes fire breath both forward and backward.
- If this weapon is aimed directly at bosses and/or other enemies with high health, it will be able to kill them, or at least cause significant damage.
- Picking  Heart of Fire (XIX) will make Nduja Fritta Tanto much more common, as its weight will be multiplied by 4.
- The player can pick up the  Heir of Fate (XIX) to trigger an Nduja Fritta Tanto when they reach low health.
## Trivia
- Nduja Fritta Tanto is named after the 'nduja, a spicy, spreadable pork sausage from the Italian Calabria region. "Fritta Tanto" translates to "fried a lot/fried too much" in Italian. A property of capsaicin is that when it is exposed to heat, it increases its potency, so if a person overcooks 'nduja, it would result in a spicy dish.
- Nduja Fritta Tanto's effects might be a reference to Superspicy Curry from the Kirby and Super Smash Bros. game series.
- Nduja Fritta Tanto can be shortened to the initialism "NFT", as the developer is making a joke on adding NFT (non-fungible token) features to the game while simultaneously denouncing them.

Negative Space is an evolved weapon from the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Celestial Booster [DLC], requiring  Outer Saboteur [DLC] at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 77,777 as reward.
## Effects
Negative Space instantly grants all of the planets summoned by Celestial Booster while additionally revealing secret planets (Planet X, Ceres, and Eris) that act as extra projectiles. Its Base Damage is slightly increased, with  Amount reset to 1 as all the planets are always active and the weapon no longer benefits from it.
Every 15−5*(1−playerCooldown) seconds, all planets will become negative, gaining +10 Base Damage, and increased  Area and  Speed for 5+1*playerDuration seconds. The orbits of each planet will tilt up, which can be slowly controlled by moving left or right to rotate the orbits clockwise or counterclockwise, respectively.
Negative Space's damage increases with the amount of gold the player has collected during that run:
- Below 10,000, Negative Space will gain 0.0005 Base Damage, per Gold collected, up to +5 Base Damage at 10,000.
- Above 10,000, Negative Space's bonus base damage will follow the formula:
2.5*log100(runCoins)
runCoins≡total amount of gold collected during the run
Effectively, Negative Space will gain another +2.5 Base Damage for every 100x increase in gold above 10,000.
Upon evolving Celestial Booster into Negative Space, Outer Saboteur is removed from the passive slot and turns into Inner Saboteur, placed over the character's face and can still evolve other Ante Chamber DLC weapons. Obtaining Negative Space from a  Super Candybox II Turbo will give the player the option of obtaining Outer Saboteur via a Level Up.

With Limit Break, Negative Space can be further leveled up.

## Tips
- Various sources of Gold, such as  Disco of Gold (XV),  Hail from the Future (X), and  Survarots, can greatly increase this weapon's performance.
## Trivia
- The term "Negative" in Balatro is a property that allows for players to gain an extra slot for jokers or consumables, since players cannot otherwise have more than 5 jokers or 2 consumables at once.
- It is also fitting that this weapon is associated with  Perkeo [DLC], given that in Balatro, Perkeo creates a negative copy of a consumable.*It gains damage with more coins collected because Celestial Packs are bought with money in Balatro, thus getting more Planet Cards and powering up their associated hands.
- Secret planets are a reference to secret planet cards that are revealed when the player plays a Poker Hand that is impossible in real poker, but is possible in Balatro. The "planets" introduced are not classified as real planets, with Ceres and Eris being dwarf planets (including Pluto), and Planet X is theoretical.
- Negative Space works similarly to Blood  Song of Mana or  Mannajja weapon from  Blood Astronomia (XXI).

Night Sword is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by finding it in Mt.Moonspell. It is the starting weapon of  Megalo Syuuto Moonspell [DLC].
Its evolution is  Muramasa [DLC], which requires  Stone Mask at max level.
## Effects
Night Sword creates a series of slashes at the closest enemies. When retaliating, it slashes six times around the character and can retaliate every 0.6 seconds.
Night Sword's retaliatory damage is multiplied by 2 x  Greed above 100% and cannot go negative.
Night Sword has a 1% chance to generate little hearts that heal 1 point of health upon killing an enemy. This chance is affected by  Luck.
## Arcanas
-  Sarabande of Healing (VI) - Allows Night Sword's Little Hearts to heal double their amount and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Increases  Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed with retaliatory damage.
-  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) - Damage is increased by the healing generated by Night Sword.
## Levels
Night Sword has 8 Levels. At max level, Night Sword has +35 Base Damage, +60% Area, and +3 Amount.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Retaliates with a bonus damage affected by Greed. Might steal hearts.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 5 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 7 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 8 | Base Damage up by 10.

## Tips
- Unlike most retaliatory weapons, Night Sword has a healing effect already built in, making it a good starting point without having to choose a specific passive items to survive longer. On top of it, the Little Hearts it generates benefit from  Recovery, with these utilities it can easily help form builds based on  Sarabande of Healing (VI),  Divine Bloodline (IX), or  Wandering the Jet Black (XXI).
## Trivia
- Night Sword behaves extremely similarly to  Victory Sword. Besides some stat differences, the only mechanical differences are its life steal effect, its Level 8 is the same as Level 9 Victory Sword, does not enable critical hits and combo finisher, and has no access to Level 10 to 12 of Victory Sword.

Nightmare is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Hex, requiring Max level  Skull O'Maniac. Evolving it keeps Hex as a hidden weapon.
It is the starting weapon of  Succubus.
## Effects
Nightmare summons a green plague ball from the faced direction that slowly moves towards and past the player's position, damaging enemies it touches. Stepping in it will increase the character's  Curse by 100%. Stepping in multiple plague balls can stack Curse bonuses up (+100% each).
- Note that Curse has no effect on Nightmare itself, only Hex.
Damage is further multiplied by  Duration, up to 5x at +400%.
Nightmare has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same Curse zone. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Nightmare summons twice the number of Curse zones. If Hex is possessed, then a copy of it,  Speculo Hex, is also granted.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Nightmare's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on Curse.

Ninth Circle is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Icebrand [DLC] at max level and  Unholy Vespers.
## Effects
Ninth Circle functions nearly identically to  Unholy Vespers, spawning a rotating ring of icicles around the character, dealing damage to enemies they come in contact with, with a chance to freeze enemies. A secondary ring of runes, lasting for 1 second, is summoned between the player and the ring of icicles. When Ninth Circle expires, an  Amount-based number of icicles are shot out evenly.
Compared to  Icebrand, Ninth Circle has increased base damage,  Area, and decreased  Cooldown compared to Icebrand and Unholy Vespers. Its knockback is decreased to match that of Unholy Vespers.
Ninth Circle has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same icicle. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
Ninth Circle has a 5% chance to freeze enemies.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Ninth Circle's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is affected by  Curse
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Increases the chance to freeze enemies from 5% to 35%. This chance is affected by  Luck.

NO FUTURE is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Runetracer, and requires  Armor. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Gyoruntin.
Its union is  Carnage Heart [DLC], which also requires  Troll Bomb [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
NO FUTURE fires a ricocheting cyan laser in random directions. It has infinite Pierce and bounces off the edge of the screen or obstacles, damaging enemies they hit. The explosion radius has a translucent test pattern, surrounded by a circle of purple particles. When retaliating, it creates an explosion around the character and can retaliate every 0.5 seconds.
It has a much higher  Speed, lower  Amount, slightly lower  Duration and no Interval compared to the Runetracer. However, its Cooldown depends on the weapon's Duration, meaning that its Cooldown is extended by its Duration of 3 seconds to 4 seconds total. Each  Armor also increase the retaliatory explosion damage by 10% additively.
NO FUTURE has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half a second by the same laser. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses or bounces off a wall, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows its retaliatory damage to increase  Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed by it.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Gives the NO FUTURE a 25% chance to freeze enemies. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by the NO FUTURE's projectiles will explode.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by the NO FUTURE's projectiles will drop  Crystallized Soul when killed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - NO FUTURE aims at nearest enemy instead of in random directions, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

## Tips
- NO FUTURE benefits from every passive item. It is best with  Speed,  Duration, and  Amount.  Area increases both the width of the laser and size of explosions.
- Normally there cannot be multiple sets of laser active at once as its  Cooldown is based on the weapon's Duration added to its Cooldown. However, with the character's Duration bonuses from the  Spellbinder or Duration PowerUp, it is possible to achieve this as the increase to Cooldown depends only on the weapon's Duration.
## Trivia
- NO FUTURE resembles Genocide/Heretical Heart, the final boss of T260G's story in the PSX game SaGa Frontier. The boss has a phase-change attack called Carnage in which the text "NO FUTURE" is displayed. This may be the source of the weapon's name.
- The test patterns that appear when bouncing off of walls are a reference to the screens that Genocide/Heretical Heart bounces lasers off when using Carnage. The lasers are also cyan and magenta, which represent the lasers and the attacking effect of Carnage..
- The video that initially showcased the weapon is titled "ℕ𝕆 𝔽𝕌𝕋𝕌ℝ𝔼," referencing the font used during Carnage in SaGa Frontier.
- The video description includes Genocide/Heretical Heart's follow-up message, "Now at Security Level 4."
- There used to be an oversight where the explosions from hitting the edge would also benefit from  Armor. This was fixed in patch 0.11.2.
- The name "Carnage Heart" when combined with "Troll Bomb" is most likely a reference to the attack of Genocide Heart.

Ophion is an evolved weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Shadow Servant [DLC], requiring  Skull O'Maniac at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Ophion summons stationary dark energy orbs with purple smoke and an ouroboros spinning in the middle. When it expires, it explodes and extends a bit beyond its normal area. Ophion has a higher Pool Limit, smaller Area, and a small interval between each attack.
The orbs have a 1% chance to instantly kill an enemy just like a  Rosary, affected by  Luck, replacing the 50% chance to slow down enemies.
Ophion has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same orb. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates a counterpart -  Silver Sliver - that is functionally the same as Shadow Servant at max level. It only spawns the silvery snakes, and does not benefit from Limit Breaking.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of shooting randomly, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Optical Shot is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Albus. It is unlocked by defeating 2,000 enemies with Albus.
It can be evolved into  Acerbatus with Max level  Karoma's Mana. Evolving it will also unlock  Barlowe as a playable character.
It can be selected when using the  Ebony Diabologue.
## Effects
Optical Shot fires a twisting light and dark piercing projectile (despite being described as 'two projectiles') and aims at faced direction. It ignores Duration. Area affects the width of piercing projectile.

Freezing enemies generates explosions. Orologions are easier to find. Sorbettos could also be found.
Out of Bounds (XII) is one of the Arcanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by reaching the 31:00 mark in Gallo Tower.
 Saint Germain [DLC] starts with this Arcana.
## Overview
While Out of Bounds (XII) is active, freezing enemies will also summon explosions, and  Orologions are easier to find.  Sorbettos also become able to be found through normal pickup sources.
The explosions have a Base Damage of 10. They deal an increasing amount of damage based on time survived in a run with the formula (SecondsSurvived / 30), which translates to +2 damage every minute. The value is not quantized so the damage will increase gradually.
Out of Bounds (XII) doubles the spawn weight of Orologions, effectively giving them a weight of 4. Out of Bounds (XII) also multiplies the weight of Sorbettos by 4, giving them a drop weight of 4 alongside letting them appear in light sources.
This Arcana applies to the following items:
-  Clock Lancet and  Infinite Corridor (unlisted)
-  Celestial Voulge has a 5% chance of critical hitting and freezing enemies hit.
-  Mirage Robe [DLC] and  J'Odore [DLC]
-  Prism Lass [DLC],  Prism Damsel [DLC],  Time Warp [DLC]
-  Icebrand [DLC](unlisted)
-  Fleuret [DLC],  Dress Sword [DLC], and  Espada Ropera [DLC]
-  Orologion pickup
-  Sorbetto pickup
When paired with the Arcana Jail of Crystal (XIV), the following weapons also benefit:
-  Magic Wand and  Holy Wand
-  Runetracer and  NO FUTURE
-  Eight The Sparrow and  Twice Upon a Time
-  Cygnus
-  Bracelet,  Bi-Bracelet, and  Tri-Bracelet
-  Prismatic Missile [DLC] and  Luminaire [DLC]
-  C-U-Laser [DLC] and  Pronto Beam [DLC]
-  Dragon Water Whip [DLC] and  Hydrostormer Tip [DLC]
-  Ice Fang [DLC],  Speculo Ice Fang [DLC], and  Cocytus [DLC]
-  Hydro Storm [DLC]
-  Hydra Cannon [DLC] and  Hyperion Bazooka [DLC]
-  Spirit Rings [DLC] and  Rings of Calamity [DLC]
## Tips
- This Arcana pairs excellently with  Jail of Crystal (XIV), as it allows more weapons to freeze enemies and trigger cold explosions.
- This Arcana also synergizes very well with  Crystal Cries (XII), which causes defeated frozen enemies to drop  Crystallized Souls that boost  Growth,  Recovery, and  Max Health when collected.
- If  The Reaper is defeated with  Infinite Corridor or  Crimson Shroud prior to 31:00, Out of Bounds (XII) can still be unlocked as the timer will automatically be set to 31:00 during the  White Hand sequence.
## Trivia
- The name of this Arcana is a reference to the song "Out of Time", which is the theme song of the Clock Tower in Castlevania.
- Out of Bounds (XII) can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "lappeso", which means "the hanged man" in Italian.
- This makes Out of Bounds (XII) a representation of The Hanged Man Major Arcana card, symbolizing pause, suspense, surrender, indecision, self-sacrifice, and contemplation.
- This is reflected in its ability to make freezing pickups more common, as well as creating explosions upon freezing enemies that has damage scaled around time.
- Out of Bounds' original name was Out of Time. This fits it affecting Clock Lancet and Orologions, along with dealing more damage based on time.
- Out of Bounds refers to how the coffin of  Concetta Caciotta is not within the Gallo Tower itself, and requires a teleporting mirror to enter the room with it.
- The explosions as a standalone weapon creates an explosion at the player character. It can also be affected by  Amount and  Cooldown, which is not the case when it is an Arcana effect as they always explode only once.
- There used to be an oversight where the cold explosions will also benefit from  Armor, likely due to copying the code from  Heart of Fire (XIX)'s explosions. This has been fixed in patch 0.11.0.

The Pako Battiliar is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.9.0. It is unlocked by defeating a total of 161,616  bats.
Its evolution is the  Mazo Familiar, which requires the  Hollow Heart at max level.
It is the starting weapon of  Bat Robbert.
## Effects
The Pako Battiliar spawns a group of bats with red afterimages which flies in a straight line across the screen, starting at a random location off-screen and passes through the center of the screen relative to where they spawned. Each bat deals damage to enemies it encounters up to its Pierce and then disappears. When retaliating, it spawns another group of bats and can retaliate every ~1.8 seconds.
## Arcanas
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - increases Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed with retaliatory damage.
## Levels
Pako Battiliar has 8 levels. At max level, Pako Battiliar has +20 Base Damage, +60% Projectile Speed, +5 Amount, +6 Pierce, and -1 second of Cooldown.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | "May retaliate when losing health."
| Level 2 | Passes through 1 more enemy. Base Speed up by 30%.
| Level 3 | Fires 1 more projectiles. Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectiles. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 5 | Passes through 2 more enemies. Base Speed up by 30%.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectiles. Cooldown reduced by 0.5 seconds.
| Level 7 | Fires 1 more projectiles. Passes through 3 more enemies.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectiles. Base Damage up by 10.

## Trivia
- The Pako Battiliar is a reference to Bat Swarm, the first map event of the game.
- "Pako Battiliar" is a pun on "Spacco bottiglia..." (a phrase racistically attributed to Romanian immigrants in Italy, meaning "I break bottle..."). The idiom continues with "...ammazzo famiglia" (literally "I kill family"), appearing in the weapon's evolution Mazo Familiar.

Paranormal Scan is an evolved weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Lifesign Scan, requiring  Mini Ghost at max level.
## Effects
Paranormal Scan creates a cyan elliptic grid that scans the character from bottom to top, after which a big cyan circle flashes around the character and healing every player in it in Co-op mode, the radius is increased by Area. Its healing effect is multiplied by Amount and Recovery. It also grants a boost to a random stat that lasts until the end of the run.

## Tips
- This weapon can greatly enhance nearly every build in game due to providing large amount of stats similar to Golden Eggs. It is therefore recommended to obtain this weapon early in runs to maximizing the stat boosting benefits.
- This weapon benefits massively from the Darkana Sapphire Mist (I) as it causes the Paranormal Scan to boost two stats if it triggers. This functions best on characters with high Luck or those taking Wicked Season (XIII) as their starting arcana.
- Bats Bats Bats' followers and Familiar’s are considered as teammates, they can be healed by the scan and have their stats buffed if they are in range of the circle.

Party Popper is a weapon from the Tides of the Foscari DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Rottin'Ghoul [DLC]. Other characters have a small chance to obtain it after Rottin'Ghoul is unlocked. It can also be purchased from the  Merchant for 1,000.
## Effects
Party Popper shoots confetti upward diagonally based on where the character is facing, which arcs downward seemingly affected by gravity.
Party Popper can bounce on an enemy once, has 10 Pierce.
Party Popper has a 0.5 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half a second by the same confetti. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses or bounces off a wall, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Party Pooper. It levels up as the Party Popper does, shooting confetti of the opposite color away from where the character is facing, but does not benefit from Limit Break.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Gains a chance to fire more than twice every activation.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy instead of the faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Party Popper has 8 Levels. At max level, Party Popper has +20 Base Damage, +40% Speed, and +2.0 seconds to Duration.

Peachone is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Toastie. It is unlocked by surviving for 10 minutes in a stage as any character.
Its union is  Vandalier, which also requires  Ebony Wings at max level.
## Effects
Peachone is a bird that flies around the player and bombards a circling zone with projectiles. The zone revolves clockwise around the player. The bird moves behind the player at a slower speed, but the bombarding circle will always stay in a position relative to the player.
By default, Peachone fires 4 sets of 4 projectiles. Each set fires all of its projectiles at about the same spot, set by the position of the visible zone at the instant that set starts. A set firing is on a different timer to the zone being active, so the first set can start firing up to a second after the zone lights up. This means that the number of sets per activation can vary by 1.
 Duration increases the time bombards are active, with 1 second roughly equal to 1 set by default.  Area increases the Area-of-Effect of the projectiles, but not the size of the bombarding circle itself.  Speed increases how fast the circle moves.  Amount increases how many projectiles are fired per set.  Cooldown bonuses reduce the time between each activation, the time between each set of projectiles, and the time between each projectile within a set.  Move Speed improves Peachone's movement but has virtually no effect on its capability.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Cygnus. It levels up as Peachone does and benefits from Limit Breaking. Its bombardment area is slightly further than Peachone's.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Peachone's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on Curse.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Bombarding zone now locks on nearest enemy. Gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Peachone has 8 levels. At max level, Peachone has +20 Base Damage, +120% Area, +7 Amount, and -0.5 seconds of Cooldown.

## Tips
- Peachone benefits the most from  Cooldown and  Duration bonuses, increasing the active duration and attacking more often when so.
- Peachone should not be considered a main damage dealer, but rather supplementary damage. It works the best in large crowds of enemies. The projectiles have infinite pierce.
- Peachone has an interesting interaction with  Chaos in the Dark Night (V), where every 10 seconds the circular zone slows down, stops, changes direction, then accelerates rapidly, and every 10 seconds starting :05 its speed doubles and halves alternately, in total causing its speed to increase every 20 seconds.
## Trivia
-  Move Speed used to increase the bombarding circles' speed, like  Speed. However, this was not intended and was fixed eventually.
- Peachone's zone circles counterclockwise, which is the opposite of  Ebony Wings.
- This weapon is inspired by Maria Renard's doves weapon from the Castlevania series.
- Peachone has a similar pronunciation to "piccione" (IPA: /pitˈʧone/, pronounced peach-AW-ne), the Italian word for "pigeon".

Penshin Fatcha is a weapon selector from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  Para Kooleo. It allows the player to select one of the tuna forms, which includes:
-  Tonno Subito
-  Tonnado
-  Tonn'omoto
-  Tonn'oddeeo
-  Tonne
-  Unsurpassed
-  Miracle of Multiplication (6+ evolutions)
Its evolution is itself, allowing the player to pick one of the six tuna forms. At six or more evolutions, it can be evolved into  Miracle of Multiplication.
At first, only  Tonno Subito can be selected, with the next option stating "Evolve Tonno Subito to unlock this form". When it evolves, it unlocks the next form and changes the next option from "???" to "Evolve ... to unlock this form" accordingly, following the order of the list above until all six forms are unlocked. Unlike other weapon selectors, the player is not given a choice in skipping weapons. Furthermore, the previous options can be picked again immediately, stacking the stats bonuses from leveling up. All six forms have a max level of six, and do not require passive items to evolve.
When Penshin Fatcha is picked again or evolved into, unlocked options can be picked immediately without having to start from Tonno Subito.
At the sixth evolution (which does not require unlocking all the options), a unique option appears.  Miracle of Multiplication attacks with all the options the players have picked at once and averages the levels for each weapon, but it stops gaining normal levels and the ability to evolve.
After evolving once, collecting  Vacuums while any of the Penshin Fatcha forms is present also transforms them into  Lavatrix Machinas. Lavatrix Machinas pull all items on the map into a vortex, slowly being collected by the character. It spins enemies around and can collect  Treasure Chests, light sources, stage items, and pickups.
All of the Penshin Fatcha forms, including the  Miracle of Multiplication, can be affected by  Jail of Crystal (XIV) and  Sapphire Mist (I).
## Unlocking
Penshin Fatcha is unlocked by evolving it once. It can be found as a stage item in The Lycaeum.
## Trivia
- The name Penshin Fatcha is a wordplay on "a pesci in faccia", an idiom in Italian that means "a fish to the face", which means humiliating someone or treating them with malice or insensitivity.
- "Tonno" means tuna in Italian. The first evolutions are all wordplays on that.
- "Tonno Subito" means "instant tuna", it also sound similar to "Torno subito" which means "I'll be right back" in Italian.
- "Tonnado" is a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "tornado".
- "Tonn'omoto" can be a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "terremoto", Italian for "earthquake".
- "Tonn'oddeeo" can be a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "oddeeo", which in English sounds like the Italian "Oddio!", meaning "Oh God!" or "Oh my goodness!"
- "Tonne" is also a wordplay on the word "tonno" and the short form of the word "tonnellate", or "tons" in Italian.
- "Unsurpassed" is a pun quoting "Tonno Insuperabile" (literally "Unsurpassed Tuna"), an Italian brand of canned tuna fish which had a very famous advertising in the '80s.

Pentagram is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.2.0. It is the starting weapon of  Christine Davain. It is unlocked by surviving for 20 minutes in a stage as any character.
Its evolution is  Gorgeous Moon, which requires  Crown.
## Effects
Pentagram summons a purple glyph with golden lining, visual details of which increase as Pentagram levels up. After summoning, the glyph shatters, instantly erasing every enemy, their drops, and all items on the screen, except for stage items. Pentagram always deals damage equal to the max health of the enemy. If it is lower than 660, the damage number is overwritten to display it between 655 and 665.
Aside from the visibility of items, one way the player can observe if the Pentagram erased items or not, for each time it is activated, is if they have "Damage Numbers" enabled in the Options. An indication of damage numbers through enemies means the Pentagram did not erase items, while no indication of damage numbers means it erased the items.
Pentagram's symbol gets progressively more complex as its level increases:
- At Level 1, the golden linings are an Eye of Ra in the middle within a hexagram symbol having some missing lines from being two completed ones, a ring of small symbols, and three concentric rings on top of a purple circle. The inner ring is in the purple circle and close to its perimeter, and the outer ones are very similar in size, they are bigger than the purple circle. The smallest and the middle ring have a straight line connecting them at 12 points, similar to a clock.
- At Level 4, another golden ring is added and connects to the points at the hexagram, the symbols are much bigger and clearly form words instead of being evenly spaced.
- At Level 5, the hexagram is replaced with a triangle with circles at the tips, each circle has a symbol in it. The triangle is partially covering another two rings with more symbols between them, also clearly forming words.
- At Level 7, two concentric hexagons are added to encompass the inner set of rings and symbols and touch the outer set. The lines connecting the outermost two rings in the cardinal direction are replaced with two lines spreading out from the outer ring, similar to a compass with arrows pointing out.
- At Level 8, the triangle with circle tips is replaced by three concentric hexagons, which are rotated by 30 degrees from the original two. The smallest one is similar in size to the middle one. The biggest hexagon and the middle hexagon have lines connecting between the vertices. Between those two hexagons, each of the six sections has symbols, seemingly replaced and fused with the inner set of circles and symbols. The biggest hexagon's vertices touch the only set of circles and symbols left.
Depending on its level and the Luck stat, there is a chance for a blue symbol to appear instead, which only erases enemies and not the drops and items, similar to the effect of the Rosary. Pentagram can be affected by Cooldown, but there is a hard-coded limit of 15 seconds on how often Pentagram can trigger.
To reach Pentagram's 15-second Cooldown limit, a Cooldown bonus of:
- -83.33% is required at level 1
- -81.25% is required at level 2
- -78.57% is required at level 4
- -76.92% is required at level 6
- -75% is required at level 8
Some enemies are completely unaffected by Pentagram.
Pentagram can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible Stalkers and Drowners in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, and The Bone Zone before minute 30. However, they do not drop chests from the blast even if it does not erase any items.
## Chance to not destroy items
Pentagram initially has a 10% chance to not destroy items, which is increased at levels 3, 5 and 7. This chance is affected by the character's Luck.
For general purposes, the total chance to not erase items can be calculated as:
chanceWithLuck=chance⋅totalLuck
In more detail, the random number generation for the Pentagram is handled via the following procedure:
- First, a random number x is generated from the standard uniform distribution: x ~ U[0,1]. This is rounded to 2 decimal places.
- Next, x is scaled down by the character's total Luck to become x/totalLuck.
- Lastly, the result is compared with the current Pentagram activation threshold, and triggers item destruction if x/totalLuck > Threshold.
For example, assume a level 5 Pentagram, with x = 0.5. This leads to a threshold of 0.45.
- With +0% Luck (=100% total Luck), 0.5/1 = 0.5 is greater than 0.45, hence item destruction is triggered.
- With +60% Luck (=160% total Luck), 0.5/1.6 = 0.31 is less than 0.45, hence item destruction is not triggered.
With enough Luck, it is possible to ensure that items will not be destroyed even with the max roll of x = 1:
- At level 1, the threshold is 10%, +900% Luck is required (=1000% total Luck) as beyond 1/10 is always less than 0.1.
- At level 3, the threshold is 25%, +300% Luck is required (=400% total Luck) as beyond 1/4 is always less than 0.25.
- At level 5, the threshold is 45%, +123% Luck is required (=223% total Luck) as beyond 1/2.2 is always less than 0.45.
- At level 7, the threshold is 65%, +54% Luck is required (=154% total Luck) as beyond 1.538461 is less less than 0.65.

## Tips
- Luck increases the chance of not destroying items, so  Clover is recommended unless destroying them is the intent of getting it.
- Since Pentagram has the ability to destroy Pickups and Treasure Chests, it is inadvisable to select it too early to evolve it into Gorgeous Moon. Even with Crown making up for the experience loss, Treasure Chests are not easily replaceable.
- Destroying Pickups could be beneficial in niche circumstances, for example, in no movement challenges once there are enough experience gems built up, a red one that consolidates extra experience will form, and the character with limited Magnet cannot collect any more gems to level up. After a purple Pentagram is summoned, enemy kills can generate experience gems to be collected again.
- Upgrading  Cooldown while Pentagram is in lower levels is inadvisable, as it would trigger the Pentagram a bit more frequently, thus making the destruction of items statistically a bit more frequent.
-  Mad Groove (VIII) should be avoided as well, at least while the Pentagram is still in the lower levels, as pickups and Treasure Chests risk being destroyed too.
- If the player is near or surrounded by the items gathered by the Mad Groove and they are in the Level Up screen, the player should avoid leveling up the Pentagram if it is an option, especially if it is in a lower level. Doing so would trigger the Pentagram immediately after leveling it up and likely cause the destruction of items, especially at lower levels.
- Even though Pentagram erases Treasure Chests, if a boss that would have dropped one is erased, the Treasure Chest is then dropped by a different enemy. However, if the boss has no guarantee of dropping a chest, there is still a chance of receiving nothing.
- You can mitigate the loss of items from this weapon by timing the activation, if you have not had the circle pop for a while or using a table with Cooldown accurately calculated, move elsewhere and keep your gems and chest off-screen, wait for the Pentagram to trigger and then move back in to collect the stuff you wanted before. With a little bit of luck, you will get to keep the gems from the enemies you screen wipe as well.
- Because some enemies like The Reaper or bosses at the 25th minute (in some stages) are immune to Pentagram's instant kill effect, it cannot be relied on as your only tool for killing enemies.
- Pentagram is a great weapon to take near the end of a run when you already have 4 or 5 good weapons and you do not need anything else. Since you do not need more experience, its main downside is meaningless.
- As with other weapons, taking or upgrading Pentagram, either from leveling up or upgrading it from a Treasure Chest - will instantly activate it. This can be used to your advantage, as it allows you to clear multiple screens in succession in the late game, or to save yourself from a pinch. However, be mindful that picking it with bad timing may destroy your valuables.
- The Pentagram can be quite helpful in severely damaging or even entirely wiping off enemies that surround a  Coffin.
## Trivia
- Pentagram dealing damage to enemies with less than 660 health will never reach the number 666, the Devil's number.
- There was an update which was supposed to increase the base chance from 5% to 10%. However, due to an oversight, it remained at 5% as it was hardcoded. The increases stayed at 20%, 40% and 60% because upgrading adds a fixed value to the total instead of being hardcoded as the wording may suggest. It was fixed in update 0.3.1.
- With the update that Gorgeous Moon comes with, the max level of Pentagram is increased by one from seven to eight. However, the new level simply splits the original level 6 effect of reducing Cooldown by 10 seconds to 5 at levels 6 and 8.
- Compared to other weapons that still have only 7 levels like Laurel and Clock Lancet, Pentagram originally might not have had an evolution planned for it, but maybe it was deemed not powerful enough with its downsides. Later, Laurel and Clock Lancet are given unique evolutions using new passive items from Yellow Sign, further divorcing the original trio.
- In patch 0.8.0, Limit Breaking Pentagram to have a 100% chance of saving items and getting one more level up afterwards, will hardlock the game and require the player to close the game to restart. This has been patched in a follow-up patch a few days later.
- If the player has reached the 100% chance of saving items since the small patch, every level up prompts the Gold Bag or Floor Chicken choice, despite the player choosing the "always" options to not hardlock the game. There is no remedy if you have limited yourself to one weapon only and did not get Crown to evolve it into Gorgeous Moon. It is eventually fixed.
- If the player has Pentagram available, then collects a Gold Finger, Pentagram will be used the moment Gold Finger's effect begins, regardless of the cooldown of Pentagram.

Peri Pendulum is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors
Its union is  Clock Tower, which requires  Endo Gears,  Myo Lift, and  Epi Head at max level.
## Effects
Peri Pendulum summons pendulums that swinging on screen and damaging enemies they contact, with its damage being increased by  Amount and found  Orologion. Being a Clockwork weapon, Peri Pendulum also triggers other Clockwork weapons.
- Peri Pendulum gains a +(1/3)x damage multiplier per +1 Amount, up to a max of x3.333... at +10 Amount
- Peri Pendulum gains a damage bonus in accordance to log(OrologionsFound), meaning they gain +1 Damage for every 10x in Orologions found, starting with +1 Base Damage at 10 Orologions.
Peri Pendulum has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half a second by the same pendulum. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

## Tips
- Increasing Amount and collecting Orologions greatly increases this weapon's damage.
- Greatest Jubilee can be a great pairing with Clockwork weapons due to its ability to spawn Light sources, which can drop Orologions.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) and  Hail from the Future (X) make it easier to find Orologions, and therefore contribute to the Clockwork weapons' unique ability of gaining damage from Orologions found.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the clockwork machinery found in the Clock Towers of games in the Castlevania series.

Phas3r is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.9.0. It is the starting weapon of  Space Dude. It is unlocked by getting it to level 7.
Its evolution is  Photonstorm, which requires  Empty Tome at max level.
## Effects
Phas3r emits horizontal colorful beams of light centered around an enemy, starting with red, then yellow, blue, magenta, with orange replacing red when it is not the first shot of the sequence. The red beams can target enemies from further away and fire in a big burst, the max  Amount of the burst is increased at certain levels; the remaining beams split up the leftover Amount for the sequence, usually only firing up to 1 or 2 at once as each level also increases how many shots is fired for each sequence in the same amount of time. Each time the weapon shoots, it plays a note. As the weapon levels up, the fire rate increases and makes the melody it plays more apparent.
 Area only affects the beams horizontally. Amount is multiplied by 4 for this weapon.
## Levels
Phas3r has 8 levels. At max level, Phas3r has +10 Base Damage, +150% Area, and +4 Amount.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Generates thin damaging zones. High Amount scaling.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Base Area up by 50%. Base Damage up by 3.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 5 | Base Area up by 50%. Base Damage up by 3.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 7 | Base Area up by 50%. Base Damage up by 4.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectile.
Note: While not directly implemented into the level up stats, it is apparent that the Interval is shortened each level. It is likely a measure to ensure the melody it plays is under the control of the weapon's programming rather than through normal stat changes from the level up system.
## Limit Break

## Tips
- As this weapon scales extremely well with  Amount, it can shoot a lot of beams to deal a massive amount of damage, making it one of the best weapons in the game.
## Trivia
- The name of the weapon is a reference to the video game framework Phaser, which Vampire Survivors was based on until version 1.6. The pseudonym of the Phaser engine's creator, Photonstorm, is also the name of the weapon's evolution.
- The "e" has been replaced by a "3", similar to the online community character modification system leetspeak.
- A phaser is also a common weapon seen in Star Trek.
- The song played by each projectile is the backing track of "I Feel Love" by Donna Summer. The riff was composed by Italian composer and record producer Giorgio Moroder. Its evolution,  Photonstorm uses a similar synth to the actual song.
- As the attack sequence is programmed to end before the next sequence starts, and there is a bigger gap between them and the normal Interval, there is no way to make Phas3r play its song continuously.
- The beams it shoots are identical to the ones from  Luminaire [DLC] except they are horizontal.

Phiera Der Tuphello is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.3.2. It is one of the starting weapons of  Pugnala Provola. It is unlocked by surviving 10 minutes as Pugnala Provola.
Its union is  Phieraggi, which requires both  Eight The Sparrow at max level and  Tirajisú.
## Effects
Phiera Der Tuphello shoots a circular red energy bullet in the four ordinal directions of the character. Each bullet can initially hit one enemy before dissipating. The bullets cannot pass through walls.
Amount affects all four bullet streams, granting four bullets total per point in Amount.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterpart  Red Muscle. It levels up as Phiera Der Tuphello does and the angles it shoots at is slightly more vertical, but does not benefit from Limit Breaking.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Phiera Der Tuphello's projectiles to bounce off of enemies once, occasionally have infinite pierce, and pass through walls. Upon bouncing, the bullet completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed returning to the direction it came from.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Phiera Der Tuphello's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
## Levels
Phiera Der Tuphello has 8 levels. At max level, Phiera Der Tuphello has +10 Base Damage, +50% Projectile Speed, +2 Amount, and +6 Pierce.
| Level | Description

| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Passes through 2 more enemies.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 6 | Passes through 2 more enemies.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 5. Base Speed up by 50%.
| Level 8 | Passes through 2 more enemies.

## Tips
- Phiera Der Tuphello already has a low Cooldown, and having more Cooldown reduction can turn the weapon into a stream of bullets, especially when combined with Eight The Sparrow.
- By moving in a single direction, with high Pierce and Amount, bullets can stay on screen forever. This can result in relatively high damage per second on group control.
## Trivia
- Phiera Der Tuphello, along with Eight The Sparrow and Phieraggi have values in the attributes of "critChance" and "critMul" like any other weapons that can deal critical damage, but they do not have the ability.
- This weapon is very similar to Knife, level ups increase base damage by 10, with focuses on Amount and Pierce. They also fire in relatively fixed directions.
- Replacing "ph" to be "f" in its name literally translate to "Tufello's Fair", an event in the city near Rome and is not a safe place for outsiders. It is also similar to a joke song written by Italian comic duo "Lillo & Greg", "Alla Fiera Der Tufello". It may also be a reference to Bayonetta's guns Scarborough Fair.
- This weapon may be inspired by the bullets from the Touhou series. With the sheer Amount comparable to what the enemies from that series spawn, circular red bullets on the edge and fading into white in the middle.

Phieraggi is a weapon union from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.3.2. It is the union of  Phiera Der Tuphello and  Eight The Sparrow, and requires  Tirajisú. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
## Effects
Phieraggi shoot four blue lasers that rotate clockwise around the character. It retracts when not firing. Its  Speed is lowered and  Amount is increased. There is a slight decrease in Interval and Knockback. The lasers can now also pass through walls.
With enough  Cooldown, the lasers permanently stay up, and more than one can be stacked on each laser if Cooldown is low enough even if it cannot be clearly seen. The uptime is not affected by  Duration.  Area increases the width of the lasers. Amount affects how many lasers are fired at once.
Each  Revival gives Phieraggi +1 Amount and +1 Base Damage, caps at +10 each.
Phieraggi has a 0.2 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.2 seconds by the same laser. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterparts  Red Muscle and  Twice Upon a Time. They are functionally the same as Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow at max level and they do benefit from Limit Breaking.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - When paired with Gemini (I), enemies have a 25% chance to freeze when hit with  Twice Upon a Time.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - When paired with Jail of Crystal (XIV) and Gemini (I), enemies frozen by Twice Upon a Time's projectiles will explode.
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - When paired with Gemini (I),  Red Muscle and  Twice Upon a Time will bounce up to 3 Times and might pass through enemies and walls.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - When paired with Gemini (I), the projectiles of  Red Muscle will explode.
## Levels
With Limit Break, Phieraggi can be further leveled up.

| Speed +5% | 10 | 300%

| Pierce +1 | 5 | 10

## Tips
- The threshold for permanent uptime starts at -42% Cooldown. Negative speed makes it spin counterclockwise.
- Phieraggi still only has a Pierce of 7, it cannot attack all the enemies at the same time even though the lasers looks like an Area-of-Effect.
- Phieraggi is capable of dealing much, much more damage than either Phiera Der Tuphello or Eight The Sparrow, due to it spinning around to hit more enemies and benefiting from Amount more. It is much more viable as a main damage option.
- The lasers does not start at the character and is a little bit away, forming a circle of a blind spot. Make sure to pay attention when enemies breach through your weapons.
- Once Phieraggi is acquired, the character opens up an additional "base weapon" slot in their inventory (as Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow are combined into one item), allowing more room in the build in the late game.
- Using up Revivals and Tirajisú (after successful evolution) will decrease the number of laser fired and its damage. Based on the situation, such as using up Revivals for Awake (IV), this might still be a worthwhile trade for another passive item.
-  Duplicator for example can provide the same Amount bonus to Phieraggi as the two additional Revivals from Tirajisú, but will also boost the Amount of every other of your weapons (which may also make up for the +2 Base Damage that you would miss out on).
- Phieraggi does not benefit from Iron Blue Will (VII), but even without Awake (IV), Phieraggi is still better than one of the guns and worth it to free up a slot if you have both.
## Trivia
- Phieraggi, along with Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow have values in the attributes of "critChance" and "critMul" like any other weapons that can deal critical damage, but they do not have the ability.
- The name appears to be a portmanteau of Phiera and Raggi (rahjji), which means rays in Italian.

Photonstorm is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.9.0. It is the evolution of  Phas3r, and requires  Empty Tome at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Space Dette.
## Effects
Photonstorm fires multiple horizontal rainbow-colored beams of light across the screen. Each sequence still starts with a burst of beams. It gains a bonus to Base Damage and  Amount, and a shorter Interval. Each time the weapon shoots, it plays a note which makes a melody.
 Luck increases the Amount of beams it can shoot, up to 5 times.  Area makes the beams wider.
## Levels

## Tips
- As this weapon scales extremely well with  Amount, it can shoot a lot of beams to deal a massive amount of damage, making it one of the best weapon in the game. It can scale even better with  Luck to shoot even more beams by default, on top of Arcanas like  Beginning (X) and  Sapphire Mist (I) and the natural synergy with the passive effect from  Space Dude.
## Trivia
- Photonstorm's name is a reference to Richard Davey, the creator of Vampire Survivors' previous engine, Phaser. His online pseudonym is Photonstorm.
- The weapon resembles Photonstorm's profile avatar, which is a pixelated blue bird with a yellow beak.
- Just as its predecessor  Phas3r did, the song played by each projectile is the backing track of "I Feel Love" by Donna Summer. The riff was composed by Italian composer and record producer Giorgio Moroder.

The Platinum Whip is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Richter Belmont. It is unlocked by Surviving 18 minutes with Richter.
Its Evolution is the  Cross Crasher Tip, which requires the  Clover.
As a magic whip, it can be picked from  Morning Star.
## Effects
The Platinum Whip attacks horizontally within a short range. Every 3rd activation, a phantom projectile of Richter fires in the cardinal directions (up, down, left, and right). With increased Amount, Platinum Whip attacks rapidly in a burst, and more phantoms are created.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Platinum Whip to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
## Levels
The Platinum Whip has 8 levels. At max level, the Platinum Whip has +30 Base Damage, +20% Area, -1.0 second Cooldown, and +2 Amount.
| Level | Description
| Level 1 | Every 3rd activation fires projectiles in fixed directions.
| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile. Passes through 2 more enemies.
| Level 3 | Base Area up by 20%. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile. Passes through 2 more enemies.
| Level 5 | Base Damage up by 10. Base Speed up by 20%.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile. Passes through 2 more enemies.
| Level 7 | Cooldown reduced by 1 seconds. Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 8 | Passes through 6 more enemies.

Pneuma Tempestas is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Gale Force [DLC], requiring Max level  Bracer. Evolving it keeps Gale Force as a hidden weapon.
It is the starting weapon of  Stella Lecarde [DLC].
## Effects
Pneuma Tempestas summons a magic circle under the character, just like Gale Force. Once charged, Pneuma Tempestas fires a large cluster of piercing projectiles upwards, spinning around, damaging enemies they touch and returning to the character.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates a counterpart, Speculo Gale Force, which mirrors Pneuma Tempestas downwards.
-  Waltz of Pearls (XI) - This arcana lists Pneuma Tempestas as an affected weapon, but it does almost nothing, as the weapon has a strictly fixed traveling path.
