The Spirit Rings is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Ameya Aisling.
Its Evolution is the  Rings of Calamity, which requires any 5 passives to be at max level.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Triggers additional techs when Area, Speed, Duration, and/or Growth bonuses are at or above 155% (+55% on the stats screen).
Spirit Rings does not deal damage directly, but instead attacks through techs. It starts with the Sunlight tech, which summons several light pillars that move around.
Each stat grants a Glimmer tech when it reaches +55%:
- Area grants Vermillion Sands, which summons a red tornado that targets the most powerful enemy in sight.
- Speed grants Heaven's Thunder, which rains a few thunders on foes similar to  Lightning Ring.
- Duration grants Aqua Spheres, which summons a water sphere that bounces around enemies.
- Growth grants Hypergravity, which summons an orb of gravity damages the entire screen.
## Arcanas
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

## Tips
- Spirit Rings' glimmer techniques do not trigger abilities that rely on glimmering new techs, such as Kugutsu's Revive and Growth increase. This also applies to Rings of Calamity. This is likely because the techniques of these weapons are technically their base attack and begin to trigger immediately when the conditions are met, without needing to be activated by Luck.
- As Spirit Rings' techniques do not have a glimmer activation scene, you may not notice them becoming activated at first until you spot one being used. You can also keep an eye on the technique carousel (right side of screen) to see if any of them are performed.
- Torrona's Box is a handy way to increase Area, Duration, and Speed to the appropriate levels if you've fully levelled these stats in the PowerUps menu. Area will still only reach +45%, however; But Candelabrador, or better, Silver Ring can give you the amount to access to Vermillion Sands. This is still half the amount of passive items you would need to directly increase these bonuses to 55%, freeing up several slots for other items.
- As Spirit Rings' evolution requires so many levels in passives, it may be wise to prioritize levelling other weapons first, as they will evolve sooner. While Spirit Rings' level bonuses are strong (when applied to 3 or 4 techniques), they are not as strong as a weapon evolution.
## Trivia
- The five colors of the Spirit Rings icon correspond to the five colors of the Magic: The Gathering card game and are arranged in the same pattern, although the order is flipped left-to-right.

The Spirit Tornado Tip is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the Evolution of  Wind Whip, requiring the  Crown.
## Effects
The Spirit Tornado Tip adds an additional effect on top of its base weapon; every 7th activation triggers a hidden  Summon Spirit Tornado, it unleashes spirits that run around the screen to collect XP gems, and fling them to the player character with a sparkling effect. Gems collected in this way also also explode within a radius.  Speed and  Duration affect these secondary projectiles.
## Arcanas
-  Wicked Season (XIII) - Increases in Growth will increase the Spirit Tornado Tip's damage. On intervals with Growth, the Spirit Tornado Tip's damage is doubled accordingly.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Spirit Tornado Tip to critical hit. Critical hits deal 4x damage and have 20% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck. Does not affect the hidden Summon Spirit Tornado.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - Increases to Growth will increase the Spirit Tornado Tip's damage.

Spread Shot is a weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Ariana [DLC]. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Ariana.
Its evolution is  Prototype C [DLC], which requires  Weapon Power-Up [DLC] and  Empty Tome.
## Effects
Spread Shot fires a spread (with fixed interval angle) of red bullet projectiles based on where the player is facing, having 8 fixed directions in which it can fire.
 Amount will only increase the quantity of projectiles on odd intervals - 3, 5, 7, etc. Those increases will always add exactly 2 extra projectiles.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows Spread Shot's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
## Levels
Spread Shot has 8 Levels. At max level, Spread Shot has +25 Base Damage, +8 Amount, +150% Speed and -0.6 seconds Cooldown.

Stained Glass is a destructible, akin to light sources, that can be found in Cappella Magna. It also functions as a special weapon.
In the stage, there are window frames with a cross in predetermined locations in the tileset, where the Stained Glass can spawn. When the player deals 50 damage to a flashy window, it explodes into vertical beams of light. Any enemies that are caught in the explosion are dealt 130 Base Damage.
## Trivia
- The explosion is also used by Game Killer (0) when an experience gem explodes on an enemy.
- As a weapon, Stained Glass can also be affected by Amount and Cooldown. However, it is not possible to obtain it in this form in an unmodded game. Whether as an Arcana effect or one of the other instances it is used for in the game, it always explodes only once.

## Tips
- The critical attack will linger as long as the weapon's attack that fired the critical hit remains, allowing the weapon to shred enemies like nothing if the player is lucky enough.
- Only the head of the hammer, not the handle, can deal the critical hits. This means that increasing the weapon's Area too much may leave the player vulnerable to enemies that may spawn close to them, such as Atlanteans.
- Hammers that deal critical hits will always be slightly red, which can help with knowing when massive damage can be dealt.
## Trivia
- The name is Italian dialectal contraction for "questa mazza" literally meaning "this mace". In the slang the meaning is more akin to "this cock" or "my cock", in a confrontational, aggressive or exclamatory way.

Star Flail is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Sara Trantoul. It is unlocked by dealing a total of 60,000 damage with it.
It can be evolved into  Moon Rod with  Pummarola at max level. Evolving it unlocks  Rinaldo Gandolfi as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Star Flail fires a close-range green triangle projectile with short Duration at faced direction, which damages enemies it touches, with a long Cooldown. Its damage is affected by recovery. Extra projectiles with Amount will have fixed interval angle. Its short range, long Cooldown, short Duration and aiming mechanic makes it a terrible starting weapon.

Summon Night is a weapon from the Legacy of the Moonspell DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Syuuto Moonspell. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes with Syuuto.
Summon Night can be evolved into  Echo Night with  Duplicator at max level. Evolving it unlocks  Babi-Onna as a playable character.
## Effects
Summon Night summons claws above the character from the top of the screen, leaving behind a lingering damage zone of dark clouds.
 Area extends how far down the claws reach.
Summon Night has a 0.45 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same dark cloud. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
Summon Night has 8 Levels. At max level, Summon Night has +10 Base Damage, +0.5 seconds to  Duration and +3  Amount.

| Level 4 | Base Damage up by 5.

| Level 6 | Effect lasts 0.3 seconds longer.
| Level 7 | Base Damage up by 5.
| Level 8 | Fires 1 more projectile.

Summon Spirit is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased and unlocked from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800. It is the starting weapon of  Blackmore [DLC].
Its union is  Spirit of Light [DLC], which also requires  Holy Wand.
## Effects
Summon Spirit creates a small black hole above the character, which fires a homing spirit.
Summon Spirit has a 0.5 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every half of a second by the same spirit. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Levels
Summon Spirit has 8 levels. At max level, Summon Spirit has +20 Base Damage, -0.2 seconds of Cooldown, and +4 Pierce.

Summon Spirit Tornado is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Persephone, and it can be purchased and unlocked from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Venus Crescent [DLC], which also requires  Gorgeous Moon.
As a spell, it can be picked from  Belnades' Spellbook.
## Effect
Summon Spirit Tornado summons spirits that dash around the screen collecting experience gems for the character. The gems collected fly towards the player and deal damage to any enemies in their path, and explode similarly to  Game Killer (0), both eventually do less damage than the spirits themselves as they do not increase in power as Summon Spirit Tornado levels up.
It is the weapon version of the same effect from  Spirit Tornado Tip [DLC].
## Levels
Summon Spirit Tornado has 8 levels. At max level, Summon Spirit Tornado has +20 Base Damage, +100% Speed, and +2 Amount, and +1 second of Duration.

## Tips
- This weapon is a good supplement for builds when used purely for its  Experience Gem collection.
-  Game Killer (0) pairs well with this weapon since it collects Experience Gems for the player.
## Trivia
- This weapon is a reference to the Red Crystal in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
- Despite being a Belnades' Spellbook weapon, Summon Spirit Tornado is the only one of its type to not have a magic circle/charge mechanic.

Super Candybox II Turbo is a weapon selector and a gift from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.11.3. It is the gift of  Candybox.
## Effects
Obtaining Super Candybox II Turbo opens a list of most evolutions (that were already evolved at least once in previous runs) remaining to be obtained in the run. Its rarity is multiplied by  Luck.
Obtaining Super Candybox II Turbo requires fully upgraded weapons and passive items (so that Coin Bags spawn in chests), as well as obtaining  Candybox at some point in the run. Once these conditions are met, Super Candybox II Turbo has a very small luck-based chance to appear in any  Treasure Chest the player opens, in place of a Big Coin Bag. Treasure Chests containing five items guarantee spawning a Super Candybox II Turbo with the above condition maxed.
Certain evolutions cannot be obtained by Super Candybox II Turbo, which include:
- All middle stages of multi-stage evolutions, like  Bi-Bracelet and  Vol Confodere [DLC]. Only the final stages are available.
- All Morphs ( Anima of Mortaccio,  Yatta Daikarin,  Carrozza!, and  Profusione D'Amore).
- All Gifts ( Sole Solution,  Universitas [DLC], and  Alucard Shield [DLC]).
-  Infinite Corridor and  Crimson Shroud
-  Ashes of Muspell
-  Wicked Ruler
-  Clock Tower [DLC]
- All Unions and Evolutions of weapons sold by the  Master Librarian [DLC]
- May be a bug.

## Tips
- Super Candybox II Turbo is one of the few ways to obtain more than 6 weapons outside of specific characters with hidden weapons, playing as characters who gain weapons from leveling up, or picking up stage weapons. As it replaces the character's base weapons when selecting its evolved version, pick one that does not evolve any of your weapons to have one more.
- Since Candybox can be obtained more than once through  Hail from the Future (X) (7 total) and Random Events (unlimited), each one can gift a Super Candybox II Turbo once with enough Treasure Chests and Luck.
- It is possible to unlock achievements for evolving weapons without having to manually evolve the base weapon by obtaining its evolution from Super Candybox II Turbo.
- Base weapons that are part of Unions will be fused into the Union they are associated with upon being obtained from Super Candybox II Turbo. For example, if the player has  Vento Sacro upon obtaining  Fuwalafuwaloo, it will be fused into Fuwalafuwaloo once it is obtained.
## Trivia
- Super Candybox II Turbo is a reference to the game Super Street Fighter II Turbo from the Street Fighter series.

The Super Missile is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Diva No. 5. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its Evolution is the  Hydra Cannon, which requires the Ballistic Missiles tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Super Missile fires a missile in the faced direction that explodes on impact. It increases in speed as it travels.
Can glimmer the "Ballistic Missiles" tech, firing 2 clusters of missiles upward diagonally, which will travel downward soon, forming a wing-shaped pattern.

Svarog Statue is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased (and unlocked) from  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
Its union is  Darkness Illusion [DLC], which also requires  Valkyrie Turner.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
Svarog Statue leaves a trail of fire on the ground, which damages enemies they touch.
 Move Speed increases its overall spawn rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.
Svarog Statue has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same flame. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows for the fire trail to explode on contact, dealing half of the weapon's base damage in an area.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels
Svarog Statue has 8 levels. At max level, Svarog Statue has +5 Base Damage, +60%  Area, +1.0 seconds of  Duration, and -2.0 seconds to  Cooldown.

Sword Brothers is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased and unlocked from the  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.
 Alucard [DLC] starts with a hidden version of this weapon that is activated upon reaching critical HP.
Its union is  Vjaya Sisters [DLC], which also requires  Thunder Loop.
## Effects
Sword Brothers summons a Sword Familiar from above that swings around the character for 2 rounds and damages enemies it contact. After that, it deals minor damage (around 1/5 of base damage) to all enemies on screen and gives temporary invulnerability to the character.
The weapon gives 5 seconds of invulnerability, which does not scale with  Duration.  Parm Aegis adds to the invulnerability period, bringing it up to 5.25 seconds. It takes -64.2%  Cooldown to become permanently invulnerable at max level (when the cooldown is 14 seconds), and -62.5% when Parm Aegis is maxed. At base, it takes -75% and -73.7%, respectively.

Take Us Away, also called the Laborratory Train, is a stage mechanic activated by walking over levers found near the bottom of the map on Laborratory. It has the appearance of a steam engine train followed by coal and tank cars. It also functions as a special weapon, and can also be summoned by  Carrozza!.
Dealing a total of 25,120 damage with Take Us Away unlocks the bonus stage, Carlo Cart.
## Effects
Take Us Away is summoned by flipping over levers found near the platform above the train track or on the walkway below, in the Laborratory stage. After a lever has been flipped, a train arrives from the left side of the screen, followed by train cars, which alternate between a coal car and a tank car. All enemies that collide with the train receive 200 damage, which scales with Might.
Amount increases the total number of train cars by 1 for each Amount stat. Additional Area will not increase the size of the cars, but having decreased Area will reduce the hitbox size of the train cars. Projectile Speed affects how fast the train moves. Duration affects how long it would take before a train cart despawns once it is off-screen; having very low Duration may cause the summoned train cars to despawn off-screen before they even reach the player's view.
Additionally, Take Us Away receives +0.1, +0.4, and +1 bonus flat damage per 1% of Area, Speed, and Duration respectively.
## Sprite
 - 
 [Full image sprite of Take Us Away]
 Full image sprite of Take Us Away
## Demonstration
 - 
## Trivia
- Take Us Away despawns after a while once it leaves the player's screen, but won't disappear regardless of its duration as long as it is within view. With high enough Movement Speed, achievable with Golden Eggs or characters with infinitely-increasing MoveSpeed stat, the player can catch up with the movement of Take Us Away, making it persist indefinitely.
- The name for Take Us Away may be based on a short conversation in Final Fantasy VIII, where party member Selphie can sing a short song while on a train ride: "Train, train, take us away~/Take us away, far away~/To the future we will go~/Where it leads no one knows~"

The RPG is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Hand Grenade, requiring  Candelabrador at max level.
It is the starting weapon of  Hammer [DLC].
## Effects
The RPG fires a warhead projectile at a random enemy when standing still, or at the faced direction when moving. Upon hitting an enemy, the warhead explodes and creates a cluster of pillar-shaped explosions that form a cone shape, dealing damage in a large area, like  Silver Revolver and  Jewel Gun.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Increases explosive damage.

With Limit Break, The RPG can be further leveled up.

Thousand Edge is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Knife, and requires  Bracer. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Boon Marrabbio.
Its union is  Million Cut [DLC], which also requires  Valmanway [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Thousand Edge continuously fires a never-ending stream of knife projectiles in the direction the player is moving or last moved.
Thousand Edge shoots three times faster with a sizable increase to  Speed, with a small increase to Interval. The projectiles cannot pass through walls.
While playing with a keyboard, the knives can only be shot out in eight cardinal and ordinal directions. When playing with a mouse or gamepad, the knives can be fired in any direction.
## Arcanas
-  Iron Blue Will (VII) - Allows Thousand Edge's projectiles to bounce off enemies up to three times, occasionally have infinite Pierce, and pass through walls.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Thousand Edge to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 6x damage and have 30% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy instead of faced direction, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

## Tips
- Even if each volley of knives lasts longer than the  Cooldown, it does not prevent another volley from shooting. Pool Limit is the only reason there are not more projectiles on screen.  Speed increase can make less projectiles stay on screen.
- Thousand Edge can deal critical damage after  Slash (XVI) is picked. The more  Luck the player has, the more likely they are to deal critical hits.
- When playing as  Boon Marrabbio, it is possible to obtain  Knife in addition to Thousand Edge. However, it cannot be evolved into Thousand Edge.

## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the Item Crash of the Dagger sub-weapon from the Castlevania series. It is usually throwing a large number of daggers continuously just like the weapon.
- If the player is playing as  Malphas [DLC], the projectile will be replaced by a stream of black and blue feathers. The weapon is functionally the same.

Thunder Loop is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Lightning Ring, and requires  Duplicator. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Vjaya Sisters [DLC], which also requires  Sword Brothers [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Thunder Loop summons lightning strikes from the sky to deal damage to random enemies, and the lightning strikes again in the same location after a small delay, effectively doubling the attack rate. When the lightning strikes the ground, it creates an orange circle that sparkles red, orange, and yellow. That hitbox lingers and is visible with another circle slowly closing in until the second strike. The lightning bolts themselves do not deal damage. The pattern of the lightning strikes is also more complex.
Thunder Loop does not attack with a small Interval between each strike anymore.
Bonuses to  Area affect how large this hitbox is.
## Arcanas
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Thunder Loop's  Cooldown when the character is moving. It is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Thunder Loop's strikes to explode one more time with a different effect. The damage of these explosions is based on  Curse.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

## Tips
-  Candelabrador is one of the most effective ways to increase the power of Thunder Loop. With enough area, each bolt can hit dozens of enemies at once. This is magnified further with bonuses to  Amount, which adds more lightning bolts.
- Thunder Loop is extremely versatile, being able to work well with many weapons in many types of builds. It can also be considered a primary damage dealer, due to how much damage it can deal to many enemies at once.
- Despite being an evolution, it introduces a new downside because of the removal of the interval between each lightning strike, as each strike must target a different enemy without it. This drastically lowers the single-target damage it can deal and makes it less effective against bosses.

Time Warp is an evolved weapon from the Operation Guns DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is evolved from  Prism Lass with  Weapon Power-Up and  Wings. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Instead of firing projectiles like its base weapon Prism Lass, Time Warp swings around and creates large blue circles around the character which rapidly damage enemies in an area around the player while active. Time Warp has a chance to freeze, slow down, or DeFang enemies it hits, the chance of which is based on Luck.  Amount will cause extra rings to generate with each cast, increasing the weapon's effective  Area and drastically increasing the hit-rate of the weapon.
## Arcana
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Causes enemies frozen by Time Warp to explode in an area.
-  Crystal Cries (XII) - Killing frozen enemies will generate Crystallized Souls that will heal and grant bonuses to  Max Health,  Recovery and  Growth.
## Limit Break
With Limit Break, Time Warp can be further leveled up.

## Tips
- Time Warp is incredibly powerful defensively due to its ability to defang and freeze enemies as well as being able to stun enemies in place due to how fast it hits.
- Time Warp benefits greatly from Limit Break and its Might, Area and Amount Limit Breaks should often be prioritized over other options.
- Despite having a Speed limit break, increasing speed does not do anything other than make the Time Warp rings spin faster.

Tonn'oddeeo is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  Para Kooleo. It is unlocked as a starting option for  Penshin Fatcha by evolving  Tonn'omoto.
Its evolution is  Penshin Fatcha, which does not require any passive item. It cannot evolve when Para Kooleo starts with Tonn'oddeeo.
As a tuna form, it can be picked from  Penshin Fatcha.
## Effects
Tonn'oddeeo rains down tunas from the top right, causing them to land on the floor and creating a lingering blue zone that spawns bubbles. They spin when falling and after they land, bounce to the left and stop, in which they can still damage enemies besides the zone.
Tonn'oddeeo has a 0.75 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.75 seconds by the same zone and tuna. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) adds a chance for this weapon to freeze enemies.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) gives a chance for this weapon to fire twice. The chance is increased by  Luck.
## Levels
Tonn'oddeeo has 6 levels. At max level, Tonn'oddeeo has +10 Base Damage, +10% Area, and +4 Amount.

| Level 2 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 3 | Base Damage up by 10.
| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile.
| Level 5 | Base Area up by 10%.
| Level 6 | Fires 2 more projectiles.

Tonn'omoto is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  Para Kooleo. It is unlocked as a starting option for  Penshin Fatcha by evolving  Tonnado.
Its evolution is  Penshin Fatcha, which does not require any passive item. It cannot evolve when Para Kooleo starts with Tonn'omoto.
As a tuna form, it can be picked from  Penshin Fatcha.
## Effects
Tonn'omoto fires tuna diagonally upwards from the bottom of the screen to whichever side the character is facing away from. Once they reach the sides of the screen, they bounce diagonally upwards again. When they climb up, whiter bubbles comes out of them until they lose upward momentum. The tuna does not move relative to the character, and the player can move such that they can keep bouncing between the sides without falling off the bottom of the screen again until the  Duration runs out.

## Trivia
- The name "Tonne" is a pun on metric ton (one thousand kilograms). In many languages, tuna (fish) has an initial part for ton (thousand) even though this generally is not to refer the weight or anything else countable (despite a singular Atlantic bluefin tuna fish more than often weighting over one thousand pounds alongside being worth thousands of monetary currency). Some examples include:
- In Finnish, tuna is "tonnikala".
- In Swedish, tuna is "tonfisk". While "ton" is "tonnen" (alongside in some other languages).
- Incidentally, in Italian tuna is "tonno".
- The icon of Tonne facing towards the screen appears to have an uncanny resemblance of Dopefish, which has a sprite doing similar 4th-wall breaking stare down.

The Town Sword is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is one of the two optional starting weapons of  Siugnas. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its Evolution is the  Lordstar, which requires the Swallow Slice tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Once triggered, Town Sword creates a small circle-shaped damaging area ahead of the character in the faced direction, constantly damaging enemies it touches for about 1 second. It ignores Speed and Duration. Amount affects number of hits.
It can glimmer the "Swallow Slice" tech★, firing a piercing damaging wave forward. This glimmer triggers every 3rd activation.

Tri-Bracelet is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Bi-Bracelet (which is obtained by evolving  Bracelet). This evolution does not require any passive items. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Lapiste Tepisto [DLC], which also requires  Kaiser Knuckle [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Tri-Bracelet shoots out a group of cloudy sparkles with limited  Duration at a random enemy. It inherits the stats of the max level Bi-Bracelet and can benefit from  Heart of Fire (XIX).
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Projectiles explode when they expire. Explosion damage is affected by  Curse.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Projectiles have a chance to freeze enemies, chance is affected by  Luck, freezing duration is equal to Bracelet's  Duration.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Projectiles explode upon hitting an enemy, dealing half of its base damage in an area.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) - Has a chance to fire more than twice every activation.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at nearest enemy, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.
## Levels
Tri-Bracelet has 6 levels. At max level, Tri-Bracelet gets +20 Base Damage, +20% Area, +3 Amount, +0.4 seconds to Duration, and -0.4 seconds of Cooldown.

| Level 4 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Damage up by 20.
| Level 5 | Effect lasts 0.2 seconds longer. Cooldown reduced by 0.2 seconds.
| Level 6 | Fires 1 more projectile. Base Area up by 10%.

Trident is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Isaac [DLC] and  Slogra [DLC]. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 40,000 damage with it.
Its evolution is  Gungnir-Souris [DLC], which requires  Duplicator at max level.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Trident sends out a trident ahead or slightly above and below in a V-shaped pattern, cycling between them in the faced direction. It only attacks to the left or the right of the character, never up, down, or diagonally.

## Tips
- Because of how Trident attacks, it is challenging to play with in maps that require a lot of movement up and down, like Gallo Tower and Astral Stair. Its evolution,  Gungnir-Souris [DLC], suffers from the same problem.
## Demonstrations
 - 
 [A slowed-down animation depicting the Trident's attack pattern of 3 tines firing in a specific direction.]
 A slowed-down animation depicting the Trident's attack pattern of 3 tines firing in a specific direction.
## Trivia
- The codename TP_CHAUVE1 comes from the Chauve-souris, a weapon used by Isaac in Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, which requires a Trident to be created.
- The weapon's icon is similar to the one from Dawn of Sorrow.
- As there are many weapons added in the Ode to Castlevania DLC, almost all passive items are used twice to evolve them, including two ( Parm Aegis and  Karoma's Mana) that had not been officially introduced in the base game at the time, distinguished by one needing the passive item to be maxed and the other does not. However, Trident and  Fulgur [DLC] are the only exception as both require maxed  Duplicator. Given that all the spell books use maxed passive item to evolve; while  Alchemy Whip [DLC] and  Wine Glass [DLC] using  Tirajisú (which also only has two levels) to evolve still separate their evolution method by required and maxed, Trident's method is likely the erroneous one.
- On 15 November 2024, Trident was buffed. In total, max level Trident got 25 more Base Damage, 20% more  Area, and -2 seconds to  Cooldown.
- On 28 October 2025, Trident was buffed again, buffing the starting stats but lowering the effect of the upgrades. In total, max level Trident got 20% more Area, -0.4 seconds to Cooldown, -0.08 seconds to Interval, and +4 knockback.

Trinum Custodem is a weapon union from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Centralis Custos,  Dextro Custos and  Sinestro Custos. It is the starting weapon of  Blue Crescent Moon Cornell.
 Centralis Custos,  Dextro Custos and  Sinestro Custos must be level 6 before Trinum Custodem becomes available.
Carrie Fernandez can be unlocked by uniting  Dextro Custos,  Sinestro Custos, and  Centralis Custos into  Trinum Custodem.
## Effects
Summons all three of Cerberus' heads in a row, attacking horizontally with bites. After that, summons all three of Cerberus' heads at the same time, continuously firing a large spreading burst of fireballs (each of the heads fires two spreading bursts) at a random direction, heavily damaging enemies in a large area. Both bites and fireballs burst are affected by all stat bonuses except Speed and Duration.
This weapon provides a flat +10 Armor, +2.0 Recovery, and -10% Cooldown along with also providing +10 Armor, +2.0 Recovery, and -10% Cooldown boost when the character is taking damage. This weapon can provide a total of +20 Armor, +4.0 Recovery, and -20% Cooldown while the player's character is getting hit.
Obtaining Trinum Custodem also changes Cornell's appearance, which turns him into a werewolf.
## Arcanas
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

| Level 1 | Union of Dextro Custos, Sinistro Custos, and Centralis Custos.

Troll Bomb is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It can be purchased and unlocked from the  Master Librarian [DLC] for 2,800.  Cave Troll [DLC] starts with this weapon.
Its union is  Carnage Heart [DLC], which also requires  NO FUTURE.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
Troll Bomb triggers a massive explosion, dealing massive damage to all enemies on screen, similar to  Neutron Bomb, with an extremely long 2-minute  Cooldown.  Amount affects how many times that explosion occurs when the weapon activates.

## Tips
- Troll Bomb pairs well with  Babi-Onna and  Jonathan Morris due to their passives.
- Babi-Onna's ability to ignore regular  Cooldown in exchange for firing weapons at fixed intervals while moving means Troll Bomb can be set off as frequently as possible.
- Jonathan's charge skill, affected by  Speed, means he can also ignore the Cooldown of Troll Bomb.
-  Royal Flush [DLC], and to an extent  Fibonacci Spritz [DLC], can trigger Troll Bomb independent of its cooldown.
## Trivia
- Troll Bomb is likely a reference to the pickup of the same name from The Binding of Isaac. While most bombs in The Binding of Isaac can be picked up, Troll Bombs cannot. They are depicted with the Trollface character from rage comics.

The Twin Dragon is a weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Diva No. 5 "Virginia" skin and  Kugutsu "Musashi" skin. It is unlocked by leveling it up to level 6.
Its Evolution is the  Gekkabijin, which requires the  Karoma's Mana and Gravedigger tech.
As an Emerald Diorama weapon, it can be selected from  Intuition.
## Effects
Twin Dragon slashes in the faced direction. The slashing projectiles firing in sequence, allowing the direction to be changed mid-attack.
It ignores  Speed and  Duration.
Can glimmer the "Gravedigger" tech, creating a powerful earthquake blast that also fires piercing projectiles upward, which triggers every 3 activations.

Tyrfing is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC for Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by inflicting a total of 20,000 damage with the Tyrfing. It is the starting weapon of  Reinhardt Schneider.
It can be evolved into  Rune Sword with  Spinach. Evolving it also unlocks  Henry as playable character.
As a magic weapon, it can be picked from  Spectral Sword.
## Effects
Tyrfing fires red swords at faced direction, which will return to the character shortly. It can deal critical damage with 3x critical multiplier.

Umbra (meaning "shadow" in Latin) is a weaponfrom the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Shaft. It is unlocked by defeating 4,000 enemies with Shaft.
It can be evolved into  Vol Umbra with Max level  Attractorb. Evolving it unlocks  Elizabeth Bartley as playable character.
It can be selected when using the  Ebony Diabologue.
## Effects
Umbra summons a pair of purple dark ball projectiles that spin upward around the character (clockwise when the character facing left, counter-clockwise when facing right) and damage enemies they contact.

Unearthly Bolt is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  Big Troubler. It is unlocked by defeating one  Bat Dragon.
Its evolution is  Spirit Disturbance, which requires  Tirajisú at max level.
## Effects
Unearthly Bolt spawns green lightning bolts and attacks the closest enemies. When it deals critical hits, it does not inherently provide a damage multiplier, instead creating an additional green explosion with fire particles floating up to damage enemies around the initial target. Consecutive critical hits increase the damage of the weapon, granting an extra +1x per critical hit to the critical multiplier up to a certain cap.  Revival increases the cap of this extra damage. Once the number of consecutive critical hits exceeds the higher value between 1 and 100 times the player's current Revivals, this bonus will reset.
Furthermore, each Revival gives Unearthly Bolt +1  Amount each.
Unearthly Bolt has a 0.12 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.12 seconds by the same explosion. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Unearthly Bolt's critical hit multiplier is doubled from 1x to 2x.
## Levels
Unearthly Bolt has 8 levels. At max level, Unearthly Bolt has +10 Base Damage, +20% Area, +5 Amount, -0.2 seconds of Cooldown, and -0.05 seconds of Interval.

Unholy Vespers are an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  King Bible, and requires  Spellbinder. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Ninth Circle [DLC], which also requires  Icebrand [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Unholy Vespers spawn a ring of red symbols around the player that occasionally has purple pages fall out of it. The symbols revolve clockwise around the player and deal damage to any enemy they touch. It has a small increase in  Area, a massive increase in knockback, and a decrease of  Speed and  Duration. Additional symbols from  Amount are added to the circle and spaced evenly.
Projectile Speed affects how fast the symbols rotate, Duration affects how long they rotate before cooling down, and Area affects how far away from the player they spin which has a cap in size and increases the size of the symbols.
The  Cooldown of Unholy Vespers no longer depends on its Duration, which allows more than one circle of symbols active without any bonuses. By default, its Cooldown is exactly the same as its Duration, creating the illusion that it never ends as its description claimed.
Unholy Vespers has a 1.7 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 1.7 seconds by the same symbol. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows the Unholy Vespers's projectiles to explode when they expire. Damage is based on  Curse.

## Tips
- Bigger Area for Unholy Vespers may be detrimental because they are further apart. If the enemies pushed through the "barrier", even with the much high knockback, can hardly leave again when there is a swamp of enemies constantly pushing more enemies in.
- Combined with the knockback resistance reduction of  Garlic or  Soul Eater, Unholy Vespers can completely prevent enemies from reaching the player, all the way until the end of the game, if paired with other similar large scale area denial weapons.
- Since Unholy Vespers rotates clockwise, when circling enemies, it will hit more and do more damage if you move in counterclockwise circles.
- Speed allows Unholy Vespers to hit more consistently and is very beneficial early on, but due to the weapon's high Hitbox Delay it starts to have less benefit after its symbols can complete a full revolution before it refreshes.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the Bible sub-weapon from the Castlevania series. Both cycle the player and pages of the bible falls out of it.
- The name of the weapon is referencing the track "Unholy Vespers" from Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia.

Unjust Ejection is an evolved weapon from the Emergency Meeting DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Just Vent, requiring  Mini Shapeshifter at max level. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 50,000 as reward.
## Effects
Unjust Ejection periodically summons a massive metal hatch at the left or right side of the screen to the back of the character. As it opens, it pulls in all enemies. Most enemies who are pulled into the hatch's opening before it closes are killed instantly, as it finishes it shows the message "X enemies are ejected." Especially strong enemies and bosses take high damage over time instead. Once Cooldown is low enough, it gains an additional effect where it creates a wall of force and particles to push enemies to the hatch once if the player switches where they face right before the next one starts.
Unjust Ejection Base Damage has been cut in half but it can deal damage at a rapid rate, instead just once to a strong enemy. Cooldown has been drastically increased, while Amount and Area lowered. Interval is lowered by a lot and regains the standard amount of Knockback.

## Tips
- To get the most enemy kills out of Unjust Ejection's effect, it is best to move in the direction away from the side it appears on.
- Unjust Ejection is capable of keeping The Reaper at bay, as its suction effect prevents it from reaching the player.
- Since enemies are pulled in the direction of the player, this weapon poses a high risk if gotten early. Weapons that attack in front of the player, such as Thousand Edge, Emergency Meeting, or Nitesco are good options for keeping the enemies at bay while Unjust Ejection sucks in and kills the rest.
## Trivia
- Unjust Ejection is based on the mechanic of ejection in Among Us, wherein the player with the majority vote is ejected because they are the most suspect as an impostor. However, with Among Us being a social deduction game, impostors have access to more tools for subterfuges and misdirections, sometimes an innocent crewmate gets ejected instead. Thus, the unjust ejection as every enemy is being ejected indiscriminately.

Unsurpassed is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.15. It is the starting weapon of  Para Kooleo. It is unlocked as a starting option for  Penshin Fatcha by evolving  Tonne.
Its evolution is  Penshin Fatcha, which does not require any passive item. It cannot evolve when Para Kooleo starts with Unsurpassed.
As a tuna form, it can be picked from  Penshin Fatcha.
## Effects
Unsurpassed summons tuna from the side behind the character, as they flop and dash through the screen horizontally, they have a limited  Duration.
Unsurpassed has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same tuna. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
## Arcanas
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) adds a chance for this weapon to freeze enemies.
-  Sapphire Mist (I) gives a chance for this weapon to fire twice. The chance is increased by  Luck.
## Levels
Unsurpassed has 6 levels. At max level, Unsurpassed has +40 Base Damage, +10% Speed, and -0.2 seconds of Cooldown.

Valkyrie Turner is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Shadow Pinion, requiring  Wings. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
Its union is  Darkness Illusion [DLC], which also requires  Svarog Statue [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
While moving, Valkyrie Tuner spawns projectiles in the form of flames behind the player, which slowly accelerate backwards and deal damage to enemies walking over them. When the player stops moving, all of the flames turn into burning lasers that move in the direction the player is facing. It has higher  Area,  Duration,  Speed, and Base Damage. However, its  Amount is reduced by 1.
 Move Speed increases its overall spawn rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.  Area also increases how far the flames travel when they are fired.  Speed increases the acceleration.
The flames do more damage when fired based on the following formula: BaseDamage*(n+1), where n is equal to the number of seconds since the flame spawned. This only affects the damage when they are fired.
Valkyrie Turner has a 2 seconds Hitbox Delay when staying on the ground, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 2 seconds by the same flame. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
While playing with a keyboard, the flames are only able to be shot out in eight directions: the cardinal and ordinal directions. When playing with a mouse or gamepad, the flames are able to be fired in any direction.
## Arcanas
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Allows the Valkyrie Tuner's projectiles to explode upon contact with an enemy, dealing half its base damage in an area instead of a Base Damage of 10.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - Defeated enemies drop  Scorched Souls, giving bonus  Max Health and  Might.

## Tips
- By tapping rapidly in one direction, Valkyrie Turner can quickly shoot out flames in that direction. This can be useful if moving forward into a dense group of enemies is necessary. It also retains the lower  Cooldown moving the character.
- Because of the unique movement patterns involved with effectively using this weapon and its base weapon, it has negative synergy with the  Vento Sacro and  Fuwalafuwaloo, which require continuous uninterrupted movement to reach maximum effectiveness.
## Trivia
- The description "Bigger, longer, faster, stronger" is a reference to the song "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" by Daft Punk. It is also accurate to the changes made when it evolved.

The Vampire Killer is an evolved weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of the  Alchemy Whip, which requires the  Tirajisú.
## Effects
Supplementing the Alchemy Whip's basic attack, the Vampire Killer also fires fireball projectiles along with each whip attack at fixed directions, which can pierce through several enemies. Hitting a boss with these fireballs will summon sunlight to constantly incinerate them.
As with its base form, each Boss killed grants the Vampire Killer a flat +2 increase to Base Damage.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Fireball projectiles explode once upon intial contact with an enemy. Damage is based on Curse.
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows the Vampire Killer to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck.
-  Heir of Fate (XIX) - The  Fire damage from this weapon would make the enemies it kills drop  Scorched Souls, a pickup that increases  Max Health and  Might.

Vandalier is a weapon union from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.2.9. It is the union of  Peachone and  Ebony Wings. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Smith IV.
## Effects
Vandalier is a vibrant, multicolored bird that flies around the player and bombards two circling zones with projectiles. Two zones revolve around the player, one moves clockwise, and the other counterclockwise. The bird moves behind the player at a slower speed, but the bombarding circle will always stay in a position relative to the player. Its Base Damage and combined  Amount of projectiles are slightly less, and it reverts the  Cooldown bonus that Peachone and Ebony Wings got, but it increases  Speed and Pool Limit.
By default, Vandalier fires 4 sets of 20 projectiles. Each set fires all of its projectiles at about the same spot, set by the position of the visible zone at the instant that set starts, alternating between each zone. A set firing is on a different timer to the zone being active, so the first set can start firing up to a second after the zone lights up. This means that the number of sets per activation can vary by 1.
 Duration increases the time bombards are active, with 1 second roughly equal to 1 set by default.  Area increases the Area-of-Effect of the projectiles, but not the size of the bombarding circle itself.  Speed increases how fast the circle moves.  Amount increases how many projectiles are fired per set.  Cooldown bonuses reduce the time between each activation, the time between each set of projectiles, and the time between each projectile within a set.  Move Speed improves Vandalier's movement but has virtually no effect on its capability.
## Arcanas
-  Gemini (I) - Creates counterparts  Cygnus and  Zhar Ptytsia. They level up as their base counterparts do and benefit from Limit Breaking. Their bombardment area is slightly further than their counterparts.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Bombarding zone now locks on nearest enemy. Gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.
-  Jail of Crystal (XIV) - Paired With Gemini (I), projectiles shot by  Cygnus will freeze enemies.
-  Out of Bounds (XII) - Paired With Gemini (I) and Jail of Crystal (XIV), enemies frozen by  Cygnus will explode.
-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Paired With Gemini (I), projectiles shot by  Zhar Ptytsia will explode on impact.
## Levels
Vandalier has 8 levels. At max level, Vandalier has +80% Area and -0.75 seconds to Cooldown.

## Tips
- Vandalier benefits the most from  Cooldown and  Duration bonuses, increasing the active duration and attacking more often when so.
- The projectiles originate from the bird itself. The bird will move behind the player, but will be slower than the player. While the bombarding circle will always stay in a position relative to the player, the bird can be left all the way offscreen if you keep moving.
- Once it reaches level 5, Vandalier's Cooldown will be lower than maxed Peachone or Ebony Wings, making it virtually have no downsides compared to its two base weapons combined.
- Once Vandalier is acquired, the character opens up an additional "base weapon" slot in their inventory (as Ebony Wings and Peachone are combined into one item), allowing more room in the build in the late game.
- Vandalier has an interesting interaction with  Chaos in the Dark Night (V), where every 10 seconds the circular zone slows down, stops, changes direction, then accelerates rapidly, and every 10 seconds starting :05 its speed doubles and halves alternately, in total causing its speed to increase every 20 seconds.
## Trivia
-  Move Speed used to increase the bombarding circles' speed, like  Speed. However, this was not intended and was fixed eventually.
- This weapon is inspired by the hidden Vandalier class of the PSX-era Konami TRPG Vandal Hearts, and the sub-weapon version of Suzaku from the Castlevania series. The bird's color is similar to the class' color palette, while the attack pattern is similar to the Vandalier class' strongest attack, Plasma Wave.

The Vanitas Whip is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Julius Belmont. It is unlocked by surviving 20 minutes as Julius.
Its Evolution is the  Aurablaster Tip, which requires the  Hollow Heart.
As a magic whip, it can be picked from  Morning Star.
## Effects
The Vanitas Whip is a whip that lingers on the ground for a few moments before attacking with a mighty slash, forming pillars of fire (affected by Area) that spread out perpendicular to the direction the whip slashed in. Damage of the fires the whip creates is affected by Max Health. The damage increase caps at +120 base damage when at 1700.

-  Heart of Fire (XIX) - Zone damage deals an extra +50% explosive damage.

Vento Sacro is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.7.2. It is the starting weapon of  Zi'Assunta Belpaese. It is unlocked by surviving 15 minutes as Zi'Assunta Belpaese.
Its union is  Fuwalafuwaloo, which also requires  Bloody Tear.
## Effects
Vento Sacro creates multiple slashes horizontally in front of the character, damaging all enemies in the area.
 Move Speed increases its overall fire rate when moving; when the character stops, it initiates the default  Cooldown.  Speed makes the slashes go further out horizontally.  Duration increases how long the hitbox lingers.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have a 5% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
Vento Sacro gains bonus damage from walking nonstop. It caps at 5 flat damage multiplied by level, up to 40 flat damage at Level 8. The actual bonus comes from distance walked divided by 200,000 up to the cap. This bonus will reset once the character stops moving. The unit for distance walked is slightly arbitrary and is not as big as it seems in the game. Limit Break levels do not further increase the cap. The weapon also creates a trail of light blue particle effects that arcs upward. The longer they last indicates the bonus being higher.
| Level | Max bonus damage | Unit walked

| 4 | 20 | 4,000,000
| 5 | 25 | 5,000,000
| 6 | 30 | 6,000,000
| 7 | 35 | 7,000,000
| 8 | 40 | 8,000,000
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Ventro Sacro's critical hit damage multiplier is doubled from 2x to 4x.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows Ventro Sacro's slashes to deal extra flat damage based on  Armor.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Aims at the nearest enemy horizontally, and gains  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Vento Sacro has 8 levels. At max level, Vento Sacro has +4 Base Damage, +60% Area, and +3 Amount.

## Tips
- With enough  Amount,  Cooldown, and  Move Speed, Vento Sacro can be a very deadly weapon to where you are facing horizontally.
- Vento Sacro can deal critical damage by default. The more  Luck you have, the more likely you are to deal critical hits. Luck can be increased with  Clover,  Little Clovers, or the Luck PowerUp. Luck can also be scaled throughout the game with  Wicked Season (XIII) at a rate of 1% per 2 levels.
- Vento Sacro has a normal amount of knockback, but it has an Area-of-Effect that can be controlled unlike most weapons, so it can be useful when trying to escape enemies closing in on you.
- Moving vertically while facing only one direction with a wall behind you can be very effective.
- Because of the uninterrupted movement needed to effectively use this weapon and its evolution, it has negative synergy with Shadow Pinion and Valkyrie Turner, which require stopping to be more effective.
## Trivia
- This is the first weapon that requires an evolved weapon to be united.
- The bonuses for continuously walking give up to 10  Amount to the weapon is changed in patch 0.8.0. In total, the player has to walk 1,000,000 units, divided by the base Amount of the weapon which is increased when leveling up. It takes 250,000, 200,000, 166,667, and 142,858 units walked at Level 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, and 7-8, respectively.
- This weapon is inspired by the Crissaegrim/Valmanway weapon from the Castlevania series; ironically, it is an evolution of the sword instead of a whip. The icon is similar to whip from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin.
- "Vento Sacro" in Italian literally translates as "Sacred Wind".

Venus Crescent is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Summon Spirit Tornado [DLC] at max level and  Gorgeous Moon.
## Effects
Similar to Gorgeous Moon, when Venus Crescent triggers it goes through distinct phases:
- Folded Wings: The character is slowly enveloped by a semi-transparent angel with folded wings, and all enemies on screen, except those immune to  Rosaries, are turned into Experience Gems.
- Generation: Slowly, but gradually getting faster, on-screen enemies are erased and yellow and purple Experience Gems are spawned, which vacuum to the player.
- Exaltation: The angel unfolds its wings, destroys all on-screen enemies and vacuums all experience gems to the player. Souls similar to those from  Soul Steal are also generated, healing the player based on their  Recovery.
- Crystallization: The angel explodes into shards, and a massive experience gem floats around the player and then lands on them, finally giving all of the gained experience throughout the process while a second vacuum occurs.
All experience created during this attack, both from Venus Crescent itself and from any other kills, is not immediately granted. Instead, it is stored in the large experience gem and is doubled before being granted to the player.
Unlike  Pentagram and  Gorgeous Moon,  Amount has an effect on Venus Crescent outside of Limit Break, increasing how many enemies are targeted with each attack during the "Folded Wings" and "Generation" stages of Venus Crescent's attack, instead of the value of Experience Gems created by this weapon.
Much like Gorgeous Moon, Venus Crescent will always have a minimum cooldown of 15 seconds. Venus Crescent also cannot be triggered again while it is already active, notably from Limit Break or  Royal Flush [DLC].
Compared to  Summon Spirit Tornado, Venus Crescent has a much longer  Cooldown and lower  Amount.

Vicious Hunger is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Gatti Amari, and requires  Stone Mask. Evolving it for the first time will unlock 500 as reward.
It is the starting weapon of  Sammy.
Its union is  Power of Lire [DLC], which also requires  Soul Steal [DLC] at max level.
## Effects
Vicious Hunger summons giant yellow cat eyeballs with a hexagram on the edge of the screen. The eyeballs mostly travel in a straight line and may change direction after a while, dealing damage when in contact with enemies. Compared to Gatti Amari, the Base Damage is increased to 30 and will be overridden by Gatti Amari's Base Damage if it is already higher from all the  Floor Chicken consumed. However, it has a slight decrease in  Duration, and a big increase in  Cooldown and  Amount is also lowered by 1.
Vicious Hunger has a 1 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second by the same eyeball. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
Vicious Hunger has a chance to transmute enemies killed by it into  Gold Coins, which can extend the duration of  Gold Fever by 0.05 seconds. The chance of transmuting enemy kills into gold is calculated with the formula:
spawnChance=goldChance*totalLuck
In more detail, the random number generation for transmuting enemy into gold when they are killed are handled via the following procedure:
- First, an array is created, starting from 0, it increments by 0.001 each time up to 0.999. It is then shuffled.
- Then, when the random function is called. A value x in the array is picked using an index starting from 0, it will increase by 1 each time the function is called. As the array only has that 1,000 values, the function takes the index modulo 1,000 (the remainder after a value is divided by it) then used it for the array to prevent exceptions from occurring.
- Next, a set value called goldChance which starts off having a value of 0.005. Based on the Base Damage of Gatti Amari, an additional 0.005 * (baseDamage / 62 OR 1, whichever is lower) is added to goldChance. It is then multiplied by the character's Luck to get a result.
- Gatti Amari has an initial Base Damage of 10, meaning it will add at least 0.000806 and at most another 0.005 to goldChance, ranging from 0.005806 to 0.01.
- Lastly, the result is compared with x, and spawn a Gold Coin if x < result.
They also have a chance to transmute pickups on the screen that are considered edible. The chance of transmuting Pickups into gold is the same as above. However, if it does not happen, there is still a flat 75% chance of them simply consuming the Pickup if it has a value of less than or equal to 2 without any additional effects. Using an identical random number generation method as above, it checks for x >= 0.25 and the value of the item, if both are true, the Pickup will be consumed.
## Interactions
All the interactions Gatti Amari had no longer apply to Vicious Hunger, as it has its own set of interactions:
-  Gold Coins,  Coin Bags, and  Rich Coin Bags are collected and fly towards the character.
-  Floor Chickens,  Little Clovers,  Orologions,  Rosaries,  Nduja Fritta Tantos,  Vacuums, and  Experience Gems are all considered edible. They have a slight chance to transmute into Gold Coins. Otherwise, they have a 75% chance to be simply consumed if they have a value of less than or equal to 2 and have no additional effects.
- This prevents Vicious Hunger from consuming coalesced  red Experience Gems and makes the player lose out on a huge amount of experience. However, this also ironically prevents it from consuming any more Floor Chicken as they always have a value of 30.
- Ignores  Gilded Clovers.
## Arcanas
Selecting Gemini (I) Arcana creates a counterpart - Flock Destroyer - that is functionally the same as the Gatti Amari at max level and keeps the Gatti Amari also at max level, spawning all six types of cats and both benefit from Limit Breaking.

## Tips
- As Vicious Hunger can transmute enemies into Gold Coins, the player should not evolve Gatti Amari until they are satisfied with the power of their current build or if they are trying to reach a certain level for an achievement or unlock (since enemies can drop Experience Gems, but evolving Gatti Amari will result in a lower rate of getting Experience Gems from enemies).
- Pickups no longer have any effect on Vicious Hunger. Unless the player wants to bet on the slim chance of transmuting them into Gold Coins, use them before they are wasted.
- The transmuted Gold Coins can trigger the duration extension for Gold Fever and the healing effect of  Disco of Gold (XV).
- The cats from Gatti Amari need to consume at least 23 Floor Chicken prior to the evolution to be able to override Vicious Hunger's Base Damage.
- They need to consume at least 90 Floor Chickens prior to the evolution to get to 62 Base Damage for the maximum bonus goldChance to transmute more enemies and Pickups into Gold Coins.
- Vicious Hunger lacks Gatti Amari's ability to start fights, which usually makes its overall combat performance inferior to that of its unevolved counterpart. If the player is using Gatti Amari for its damage and area control potential and have no need for further gold, do not evolve the weapon.
## Trivia
- Vicious Hunger references how much  Floor Chicken the cats from Gatti Amari could have consumed, theoretically an infinite amount, and its ability to consume most Pickups without any effect, completely devouring them.
- The ability to transmute everything it touches into gold may be a reference to Midas's Curse.

Victory Sword is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 0.11.0. It is unlocked by defeating 100,000 enemies in a single run while playing as  Queen Sigma.
Its gift is  Sole Solution, which requires  Torrona's Box at max level; Victory Sword will not be replaced by Sole Solution after obtaining it.
It is the starting weapon of  Queen Sigma.
## Effects
Victory Sword creates a series of blue slashes at the closest enemies. When retaliating, it slashes six times around the character and can retaliate every 0.6 seconds.
At level 8, it becomes capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by Luck. Upon reaching level 8, its finisher is also activated, causing every five slashes to become a finisher that slashes vertically, covering a large area.
Victory Sword can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible Stalkers and Drowners in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower and The Bone Zone, causing them to drop chests.
## Arcana
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Victory Sword to critical hit before Level 8. It doubles the damage of Victory Sword's critical hits, causing them to deal 4x damage.
-  Divine Bloodline (IX) - Allows the Victory Sword's slashes to deal extra flat damage based on Armor and increases Max Health by 0.5 when enemies are killed with retaliatory damage.
## Levels
Victory Sword has 12 levels. At max level, Victory Sword has +35 base damage, +60% Area, +3 Amount, and -0.75 seconds of Cooldown. It can critical hit and has a finisher to the attack.

Vjaya Sisters is a weapon union introduced in the 2025 update of the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the union of  Sword Brothers [DLC] at max level and  Thunder Loop.
## Effects
Similar to Thunder Loop, Vjaya Sisters summons lightning bolts that strike random enemies. When each lightning bolt strikes, it spawns a sword in the ground that, after a brief delay of 70 milliseconds, grants 0.3 seconds of invulnerability to the player (affected by  Parm Aegis). Then, after 1.31 seconds, it explodes, dealing 30% of the weapon's damage and granting another 0.3 seconds of invulnerability (affected by  Parm Aegis).
Compared to  Sword Brothers, Vjaya Sisters has increased Base Damage and a faster  Cooldown.
## Arcanas
-  Twilight Requiem (II) - Allows Vjaya Sisters' swords to explode when they expire. Damage is affected by  Curse.
-  Tragic Princess (III) - Reduces Vjaya Sisters'  Cooldown when the character is moving. This reduction is affected by  Move Speed.
-  Pale Diamond Incursion (V) - Vjaya Sisters now aims at the nearest enemy, and gains a  Cooldown bonus based on  Speed.

Losing health generates exploding projectiles. Explosion damage is increased by total recovered health and Magnet bonus. Explosion Area is increased by Magnet.
Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) is one of the Darkanas in Vampire Survivors. It is unlocked by reaching 665  Max Health while playing as  Bat Robbert after obtaining the  Darkasso.
## Overview
While Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) is active, it generates circular, crimson projectiles that revolve around the player and deal damage based on total recovered Health and  Magnet. The projectiles prior to exploding start with 10 Base Damage. These projectiles deal minor contact damage, but will explode after a time.
Projectiles are spawned when losing health and when healing for at least 3.3 Health. The number of projectiles is increased by  Amount, and they orbit faster with  Speed. The area of each projectile's explosion is equal to Magnet.
The contact damage of the projectiles during their orbit is 0.5*Power*Magnet.
The damage of the explosion is increased by multiple factors, and follows the formula:
Power*Magnet+AccumulatedDamage+AccumulatedRecovery+BloodlineDamage.
- The base Power of this weapon is always 1, which is the source of the 10 Base Damage.
- AccumulatedDamage is increased whenever the player receives damage. If AccumulatedDamage is under 5, then it will be increased by the damage the player received multiplied by 0.01. When over 5, the damage the player receives is instead multiplied by 0.001.
- AccumulatedRecovery is increased whenever the player heals or overheals. If AccumulatedRecovery is under 5, then it will be increased by the amount healed multiplied by 0.005. When over 5, the healing received is instead multiplied by 0.001.
- BloodlineDamage is the flat damage bonus provided by  Divine Bloodline (IX).
The value calculated by either formula is ultimately multiplied by 10 for final damage. For the AccumulatedDamage and AccumulatedRecovery values, after the threshold is reached, both values effectively become +1 damage per 100 damage or healing received, respectively.
## Tips
- One of the easiest ways to unlock Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) is to select  Divine Bloodline (IX), and use retaliatory-damage-builds (such as the  Victory Sword) and allow Max Health to reach 665.
- Perhaps a safer unlocking method is to use  Crystal Cries (XII) with freeze builds.
- Another method is pairing  Hidden Anathema (III) with any method of generating pickups, such as  Hail from the Future (X) or  Greatest Jubilee.
- To pair with these methods, you can use the Milk Elemental Enemah, as it gives 400 Max Heath by itself. Combined with Hollow Heart, you don't need much more to get to unlock requirement.
- This Darkana pairs extremely well with any weapon that utilizes Health Drain, such as the  Muramasa [DLC], which rapidly damages the user, resulting in projectiles being fired even if enemies cannot reach the character. At the same time, the Muramasa also heals the user, which steadily increases the damage of Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) throughout the run.
-  Dominus Anger [DLC],  Dominus Hatred [DLC],  Dominus Agony [DLC], and the  Power of Sire [DLC] are also great sources of self-damage.
- Consequently, this makes characters with Health Drain immunity receive less of a benefit from Wandering the Jet Black (XXI), and they will have to rely more on damage from enemies for it to activate. This might require increasing  Curse or  Charm to increase enemy spawn rates through obtaining the  Skull O'Maniac or  Karoma's Mana.
- This Darkana also pairs well with  Cosmo Pavone due to the character's high  Recovery potentially allowing a very high damage output.
## Trivia
- The name of this Darkana is a reference to the song "Wandering the Crystal Blue", which is the theme song for Somnus Reef in Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia.
- Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) can be unlocked in the  Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane by casting the spell "odnomli", the reverse of "ilmondo" or "the world" in Italian.
- This makes Wandering the Jet Black (XXI) a representation of The World Major Arcana card in reverse position, symbolizing a lack of closure, a feeling of incompleteness, emptiness, and a desire for fulfillment.
- This may be reflected in its ability that it activates upon the player receiving damage, or the "emptying" of the player's health bar.

# Weapons
Attack cards
Whip is the first weapon the player gets when they enter the Mad Forest as Antonio.
Weapons are used by the character to fend off enemies, each having its own unique way of doing so. Most weapons deal damage to enemies, while some apply debuffs to enemies or buffs to the player.
The player can select up to six different weapons from level-ups, but it is possible to carry more by picking up weapons that generate with the stage. Most weapons must be unlocked before they can be offered to the player.
Most weapons are unique, which means a character can only gain a weapon once per run, and there is no way to get the same weapon multiple times (even if it is consumed). Exceptions include single-use weapons like  Candybox or  Arma Dio.
## Obtaining
Normally, each character has access to one of the base weapons as their starting weapon and is able to obtain additional base weapons as they level up. Rarity determines the weight of how often that weapon shows up in the pool of possible weapons and passive items during the level-up screen and when opening  Treasure Chests.
## Upgrading
There is a certain chance for weapons that the player has already owned to be offered to them upon level-up. If an already owned weapon is selected, it will be upgraded to a higher level, and it will gain certain stat bonuses unique to the weapon. When a weapon is fully leveled, it cannot appear in the level-up options anymore. Upgrading a weapon will also reset its  Cooldown and activate it instantly, which is useful for powerful weapons with long Cooldown.
## Evolution
Main article: Evolution
When a base weapon is fully leveled and its corresponding passive item is obtained, it can be transformed into an evolved weapon by collecting a  Treasure Chest. Some weapons only need to be fully leveled for them to evolve. Not all weapons have an evolution.
Evolution actually works by removing the base weapon and acquiring the evolved one (with a few exceptions), which means whenever a weapon is evolved, all the effects of the original weapon will be lost, and the evolved weapon's Cooldown starts from zero (which is noticeable for weapons with long Cooldown, like Santa Water). Evolved weapons also remove the base weapon regardless of whether obtained by normal evolution rules or not (for example, obtaining an evolution by  Super Candybox II Turbo will also remove its base weapon).
Certain characters ( Mortaccio,  Yatta Cavallo,  Bianca Ramba, and  O'Sole Meeo) automatically evolve their starting weapon when they morph into a new form, provided that the player has obtained the required relic and met the necessary condition.
## Stats
Weapons have different stats, which define their functions.
See Overview Stats for a list of base stats of the weapons.
| Weapon Stats
| Max Level | The highest level the weapon can be upgraded to. | Rarity | The weight of the weapon in the pool of weapons and passive items.
| Base Damage | The damage dealt by a single projectile per hit. Modified by Might stat. | Area | The base area of the weapon. Modified by Area stat.
| Speed | The base projectile speed of the weapon. Modified by Speed stat. | Amount | The amount of projectiles fired per use. Modified by Amount stat.
| Duration | The duration of the weapon's effect. Modified by Duration stat. | Pierce | The number of enemies a single projectile can hit before being used up.
| Cooldown | The time required for the weapon to be used again. There is a trigger for the cooldown to start after a weapon's duration ends. Modified by Cooldown stat. | Projectile Interval | The time required for an additional projectile to be fired between each Cooldown. Can overlap with another set of shots even before it finishes shooting.
| Hitbox Delay | The time before the same enemy can be hit by the same projectile again. All delays refresh simultaneously as soon as one fully counts down. | Knockback | The knockback dealt multiplier of the weapon. Determines the strength of the knockback effect along with the enemy's knockback taken multiplier and movement speed.
| Pool Limit | The maximum amount of projectiles that can be on screen. | Chance | The chance of a special effect happening. Modified by Luck stat. Technically, Crit Chance is a separate stat but both have not been used at the same time yet.
| Crit Multi | Damage multiplier applied to critical hits. | Block by Walls | Can the projectile be blocked by obstacles.
- ↑ The damage displayed with the "Damage Numbers" option ticked shows a randomized value within ±5 of the scaled base damage, but this is only a visual feature and the damage dealt by a weapon is always the same.
## Types
There are base, evolutions or unions, and special weapons.
See Combos for a list of which passive items and their corresponding player stats affect which weapon.
Certain weapons are counted as specific weapon type, which will interact with certain effects. This include:
-  Fire damage weapons, which have synergy with  Heir of Fate (XIX),  Dario Bossi [DLC], Whiteout and The Coop.
-  Hell damage weapons, which have synergy with  Baal'Thasar [DLC].
-  Blood damage weapons, which have synergy with  Megalo Syuuto Moonspell [DLC] and  Baal'Thasar [DLC].
Despite not listed as a weapon type, certain weapons have Freeze effect and synergies with various Arcanas such as  Crystal Cries (XII).
## Base Weapons
Base weapons can be chosen by leveling up. Most of them are locked behind achievements at first.

## Evolutions
Traditionally, evolved weapons cannot be upgraded, only have one level, and have a rarity of 1. However, newer expansion content such as the Emerald Diorama breaks many of the older conventions for weapon evolutions. Notable exceptions of older weapons that broke these conventions are the Bi-Bracelet, Tri-Bracelet, Alucard Swords, Vol Confodere, Melio Confodere, Vol Luminatio, and Vol Umbra. Many newer weapons also have additional secondary evolutions.

Whip is a weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Antonio Belpaese. It is unlocked by default.
Its evolution is  Bloody Tear, which requires  Hollow Heart.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms [DLC].
## Effects
Whip creates a slash horizontally that frontally originates from the character's torso, damaging all enemies in the area.
Consecutive slashes from increased  Amount alternate between firing towards and away from the direction the character is facing, getting progressively higher.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Allows Whip to critical hit. Its critical hits deal 4x damage and have a 20% chance to occur. This chance is affected by  Luck.
## Levels
Whip has 8 levels. At max level, Whip has +30 Base Damage, +20%  Area, and +1  Amount.

## Tips
- With enough  Amount, Whip can be a very deadly weapon when you are positioned south of enemies.
- Whip can deal critical damage after  Slash (XVI) is picked up. The more  Luck you have, the more likely you are to deal critical hits. Luck can be increased with  Clover,  Little Clovers, or the Luck PowerUp.
- Whip has a normal amount of knockback, but it has an AOE that can be controlled unlike most weapons, so it can be useful when trying to escape enemies closing in on you.
- Quickly switching between facing left and right will allow multiple slashes in the same direction rather than alternating.
## Trivia
- This weapon is inspired by the iconic whip weapon from the Castlevania series. The icon is similar to whips from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin.
