Wicked Ruler is an evolved weapon from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.14. It is the evolution of  Chaos Rune, and requires  Spellbinder at max level.
## Effects
Instead of firing from the bottom of the screen, Wicked Ruler fires runes from a runic circle orbiting the player and the player themselves, firing chaotic projectiles towards them and the closest enemy respectively. This rune circle can deal contact damage. It has a slightly decreased Base Damage.
 Amount affects how many runes are summoned with each activation, while  Speed and  Duration affect how many times each rune can deal damage.
Every 20 seconds, the red ring of runes around the player will begin to contract and the rune circle will gravitate towards the player. Once both reach the player, the weapon will flash, summoning a horizontal line of bright red runes across the screen. After a short delay, Wicked Ruler will fire another burst of red runes in the last direction the player moved, which will continue to bounce around the screen, dealing increased damage. The cooldown of this ability is affected by  Cooldown.
Wicked Ruler has a 0.03 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.03 seconds by the same rune. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.

## Trivia
- Wicked Ruler initially had multiple glitches. When it started to attack, it froze the game, which made the character and enemies unable to move, and made experience gems unable to spawn. Additionally, it was displayed as a 1.0 item and placed after counterparts in the Collection.
- Since this weapon is a reward from completing the Gallo Tower ARG, it caused confusion whether the glitches were part of the ARG or genuine mistakes.
- Its secondary attack is similar to the Singularity attack of  SpellStrom [DLC], with a long Cooldown that deal screen-covering damage.

Wind Whip is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Simon Belmont. It is unlocked by surviving 12 minutes with Simon Belmont.
Its evolution is  Spirit Tornado Tip, which requires  Crown.
As a magic whip, it can be picked from  Morning Star.
## Effects
Wind Whip creates a slash in front of the character and covers below the character, the height of where it comes out is randomized. Its damage is multiplied by  Growth times 2.
Consecutive slashes from increased  Amount alternate between firing towards and away from the direction the character is facing, with the even ones covering above the character. It does not get progressively higher like  Whip.

Wine Glass is a weapon from the Ode to Castlevania DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the starting weapon of  Vlad Tepes Dracula [DLC].
Its evolution is  Meal Ticket [DLC], which requires  Tirajisú at max level.
As a vampire-killing tool, it can be picked from  Coat of Arms.
## Effects
Wine Glass throws a wine glass at the nearest enemies which creates a small explosion on contact. At Level 1 to 3, it plays a light glass breaking sound effect; Level 4 to 6 is medium; and Level 7 and 8 is heavy.
Wine Glass' base  Amount is multiplied by 4, so each wine glass seems to create multiple explosions. At max level, each wine glass stacks 16 projectiles together. This can result in them piercing enemies despite only having one Pierce.  Beginning (X) directly increases base Amount of weapon and greatly benefits this weapon.
## Levels
Wine Glass has 8 levels. At max level, Wine Glass has +4 Base Damage, +40% Area, +60% Speed, +3 Amount, and -0.3 seconds of Interval.

Yatta Daikarin is a morph from the base game version of Vampire Survivors that was introduced in Patch 1.5.0. It is the evolution of  Cherry Bomb, and requires  Chaos Rosalia relic and reaching level 80 while playing as  Yatta Cavallo.
Alternatively, it can be obtained via Cosmic Finger rewards from  Gold Fingers, or the Edition of  Yatta Cavallo's  Survarot.
## Effect
Yatta Daikarin throws a spinning bomb at the nearest enemy. The bomb travels in a straight line, bouncing off enemies, walls, and edges of the screen. They will decelerate and eventually stop; when they explode, they create star particles. It also draws a constellation on the screen, the line drawn can deal damage and stop when a star is made. Once the seventh star is created, all the star explodes into lines of star particles. Yatta Daikarin guarantees the chance to explode, gains  Duration and extra Pool Limit.
 Might and  Area affect both the bouncing Cherry Bombs and their explosions.
Only the constellation is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal extra damage based on  Luck bonus as a multiplier and have 5% chance to occur. The chance is also affected by Luck. The damage is further multiplied by  Amount.
It causes Yatta Cavallo to visually transform into a floating celestial beast made of stars and constellations. If a character other than Cavallo gets the weapon, a translucent, transformed Yatta Cavallo appears behind the character.
## Arcanas
-  Slash (XVI) - Doubles the damage of Yatta Daikarin's critical hits, causing them to deal double the Luck bonus as a multiplier amount of damage.

## Tips
-  Luck increases the critical hit frequency and damage bonuses, greatly increasing the damage output of the weapon. However, Luck is obsolete for the chance to explode as it is guaranteed.
- Yatta Daikarin can create a relatively safe space within all the explosions with increased  Amount and  Cooldown reduction.
- As the bombs are not limited by bounces, more  Duration and  Speed allow the bombs to hit more enemies over their lifetime.
## Trivia
- The design of the bombs might have been inspired by the Cherry Bomb from Ōkami, the explosions also have similar flower petal effects.
- The constellation is a reference to Amaterasu having to dot missing stars in a constellation to restore the power of Celestial Brush gods, allowing them to grant their power to her.
- Yatta Daikarin's name is likely derived from the special attack Happo Daikarin from the manga and anime Ranma ½, which took the form of similarly-shaped bombs thrown at the enemy.
- Morphing Cavallo set it to 1 specifically, making it no longer dependent on  Luck to explode as a bonus for them, while getting Yatta Daikarin through another method would make the intended chance remain at 60%, the same value as a maxed Cherry Bomb. However, there used to be an oversight of the explosion chance being set to 60 instead of 0.6, as most stats translate decimals into percentages, making the chance to explode 6000% would be redundant beyond 100%, and lowering it by 60 times with another method that still gets it to 100% when it is more closely related to the weapon itself is illogical.
- In an unknown patch, the chance value has been set to 1, making Cavallo's bonus redundant.

The Zweihander is an evolved weapon from the Emerald Diorama DLC of Vampire Survivors. It is the evolution of  Flamberge.
Its Evolution is the  Galatyn, which requires the Absetzen tech.
## Effects
Can glimmer the "Absetzen" tech.
